While the fleet is becalmed near Sark, Black Simon and Aylward slip ashore at night so Simon can collect a grim 'forfeit' from La Muette, the brutal pirate king who once tortured him as a prisoner, killing him in payment of an old boast.

characters: Raoul de la Roche Pierre de Bras
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Marching through devastated Brittany, Nigel runs down and captures the young French squire Raoul after rescuing him from ambushing bandits, the two become fast friends and rivals in honor, and then discover that Aylward has been taken prisoner by the savage robber-baron of La Brohiniere.

characters: Oliver de St. Yvon (the Butcher of La Brohiniere)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: The English besiege the castle of the sadistic 'Butcher' to free his archer prisoners; a burning-gate assault fails with heavy losses, and Raoul is mortally wounded, dying in Nigel's arms after the failed attack.

After his earlier failure, Nigel joins Black Simon and a blind guide to dig into an underground passage beneath La Brohiniere castle, rescues the tortured archers including Aylward, kills the Butcher, and helps Knolles finally take the castle.

On reaching Ploermel the English learn a year's truce has begun; the Breton commander Beaumanoir proposes settling honor through a formal combat of thirty champions a side, and personally challenges Nigel to be his opponent.

themes: the historic Combat of the Thirty
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: The famous Battle of the Thirty is fought at the midway oak; Nigel is struck down early and Bambro is killed, and the English lose the day when Montaubon rides his warhorse through their exhausted ranks.

Recovering for months from his wounds, Nigel is at last summoned by Chandos to rejoin the army in Gascony, reunites joyfully with Aylward on the road, and arrives at the English camp as the Black Prince prepares to face King John's massive French army.

King John holds a stormy council deciding to attack the entrenched English on foot; a treacherous spy falsely reports that the English are fleeing, spurring the eager French nobles to advance as the Battle of Poitiers begins.

At Poitiers the French cavalry charge and infantry assault are shattered by English archers and knights; in the final melee Nigel fights beside the Prince and it emerges that King John himself surrendered to him, at last earning Nigel his knighthood.

Nigel returns to Cosford as a celebrated knight and is joyfully reunited with Lady Mary, who accepts his betrothal that same night; the tale closes with a reflection on their long, happy marriage and the passing of that heroic age.

characters: Marie Madeleine d'Aubray, Marquise de Brinvilliers (in vision)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/tales_of_terr.plot: A collector's ancient leather wine-funnel, slept beside as a sleep-experiment, gives the narrator a horrifying vivid dream of a 17th-century woman undergoing water torture, which Dacre then proves depicts the real historical poisoner the Marquise de Brinvilliers.

Rival archaeologist Kennedy pressures the poorer Burger into revealing his secret newly discovered catacomb by threatening to expose an old love affair; Burger, whose fiancée Kennedy had seduced and abandoned, leads him deep into the labyrinth and abandons him there to die.

The brilliant but reckless surgeon Douglas Stone is lured by a disguised Lord Sannox into cutting away the lip of a veiled 'patient' to save her from poison, only to discover, too late, that she is his own mistress Lady Sannox, mutilated as the husband's calculated revenge.

A special train carrying a mysterious financier and his bodyguard vanishes completely between two stations in broad daylight; years later a condemned criminal's death-row confession reveals the train was secretly diverted onto a disused mine line and destroyed in a pit to silence a political scandal.

A young doctor answers a bizarre advertisement requiring beetle-collecting skill and physical courage, and finds himself secretly guarding Lord Linchmere's brother-in-law Sir Thomas Rossiter, a periodically homicidal maniac, until a night attack proves the danger real and Rossiter is committed.

A young man is found shot dead alone in a locked first-class compartment carrying six watches and no ticket, baffling police for years, until a confessional letter reveals he was a card-sharper's protege shot by his own mentor after his brother tried to pull him from a life of crime.

themes: a phonograph as a relic of love
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/tales_of_terr.plot: A tutor at a great English house grows suspicious of his reclusive employer's secret nightly visits with a mysterious female voice, and eventually discovers the reformed rake is playing a phonograph recording of his dying wife's voice, which alone keeps him from relapsing into drink.

A respected village doctor is apparently murdered and his fiancée's brother is tried for the killing, but at the sensational trial it emerges the corpse was actually the doctor's disreputable twin brother, who died of a weak heart, and the doctor had staged his own death to escape old scandal.

themes: an ancient Jewish relic (urim and thummim)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/tales_of_terr.plot: The new curator of a museum finds a priceless ancient jeweled breastplate mysteriously tampered with each night, and discovers his predecessor's future son-in-law had stolen the gems and substituted fakes, while the old professor has been secretly breaking in nightly to restore the true stones and avoid a scandal.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_adventure.plot: In occupied Venice, Gerard is lured by a forged letter into the hands of a secret Venetian tribunal that tortures French officers, discovers his lover Lucia is condemned to the same fate, and swaps places to take her mutilation punishment himself until French soldiers arrive to save them both.

Newly arrived and mocked by his fellow officers, Gerard volunteers to sneak disguised as a friar into besieged Saragossa, finds the French agent tortured to death, and single-handedly ignites the enemy's powder magazine so the city can be stormed, winning his comrades' respect at last.

Sent by Massena to scout the English lines at Torres Vedras, Gerard's horse is shot under him; he steals an English general's hunter, gets swept accidentally into a full fox hunt behind enemy lines, kills the fox himself with his sabre, and gallops back to French lines amid the astonished applause of both armies.

Gerard is sent alone to light a signal beacon warning a cut-off French army corps to retreat; captured by the brutal guerrilla chief 'The Smiler' and sentenced to death, he is secretly freed by a guerrilla lieutenant who substitutes a dead comrade's body on the pyre, and lives to see the answering signal fire lit.

As a paroled French prisoner enjoying English sporting hospitality, Gerard falls for his host's sister Lady Jane, only to learn she is secretly married; when her estranged husband tries to force her back, Gerard fights a duel with him but deliberately shoots wide, reconciling the couple.

During the terrible retreat from Moscow, Gerard leads a detachment to seize grain at Minsk but is ambushed after a Russian woman he has fallen for deliberately mistranslates a captured message; captured himself, he escapes with her secret help after killing his brutal captor Major Sergine.

Carrying Napoleon's orders to Marshal Grouchy, Gerard accidentally rides into the advancing Prussian army, is trapped disguised in a forest inn, overhears a Prussian plot to capture or kill Napoleon, and races back through the collapsing French lines to warn the Emperor as Waterloo is lost.

Years after Waterloo, Gerard is recruited into a secret naval plot to smuggle Napoleon off St. Helena, but on finally reaching Longwood in the night he finds the Emperor has just died, and the tale becomes his own farewell to his old comrades.

Holmes is hired by the King of Bohemia to recover a compromising photograph held by Irene Adler; a staged fire-alarm trick reveals its hiding place, but Adler secretly marries and flees the country first, outwitting Holmes and earning his lasting respect as simply 'the woman.'

Holmes investigates a bizarre 'Red-Headed League' scheme that paid a red-haired pawnbroker to leave his shop empty every morning, deduces it is a ruse by his assistant John Clay to tunnel into a neighboring bank vault, and captures the gang red-handed as they break through into 30,000 napoleons of French gold.

themes: the value of trifles in deduction
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_adventure.plot: Mary Sutherland asks Holmes to find her fiancé Hosmer Angel, who vanished on their wedding day; Holmes deduces that Angel was in fact her controlling stepfather James Windibank in disguise, scheming to keep her tied to him and out of a real marriage so he could keep control of her income.

James McCarthy is accused of murdering his father near Boscombe Pool, but Holmes reads the ground and the dying man's garbled last word ('Ballarat') to identify the true killer as neighbour John Turner, whom the victim had blackmailed for decades over a shared criminal past in Australia.

themes: the Ku Klux Klan and hidden crime
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_adventure.plot: John Openshaw seeks Holmes's help after his uncle and father both die mysteriously following anonymous letters containing orange pips from the Ku Klux Klan demanding return of stolen papers; despite Holmes's efforts Openshaw is murdered before he can be saved, and Holmes can only send the pips onward to the killers, who are lost at sea before facing justice.

themes: opium dens and the London underworld
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_adventure.plot: Investigating the apparent murder of businessman Neville St Clair, whose bloodstained clothes are found in an opium den, Holmes discovers that St Clair is not dead but has been secretly living a double life as the disfigured beggar Hugh Boone, earning far more by begging than by his respectable profession.

A stolen jewel, the Countess of Morcar's blue carbuncle, turns up inside a Christmas goose; tracing the goose's owners back through a chain of sellers, Holmes identifies the thief as hotel attendant James Ryder and lets him go free out of compassion rather than send him to prison.

themes: justice turned back on the villain
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_adventure.plot: Helen Stoner fears for her life after her twin sister died mysteriously before her own wedding, both under the roof of their violent stepfather Dr Roylott; Holmes discovers Roylott has been using a trained venomous swamp adder sent through a fake ventilator to murder his stepdaughters and preserve their inheritance, and the snake ultimately kills Roylott himself.

Hydraulic engineer Victor Hatherley is hired for a mysterious night job by the sinister 'Colonel Lysander Stark,' discovers the machine is used by a coining gang rather than for fuller's-earth, is nearly crushed in the press and loses his thumb escaping, and though Holmes traces the gang's hideout, the criminals burn the house and escape.

Lord St Simon's American bride Hatty Doran vanishes from her own wedding breakfast; Holmes deduces she fled not from foul play but to rejoin Frank Moulton, her first husband whom she had believed killed by Apaches and who reappeared at the church during the ceremony.

Banker Alexander Holder wrongly accuses his son Arthur of stealing gems from a valuable coronet left as security, but Holmes proves that Holder's niece Mary secretly stole the gems for her lover Sir George Burnwell, and that Arthur was innocently trying to recover them when caught.

Governess Violet Hunter is hired under bizarre conditions (cutting her hair, wearing a specific dress) by Jephro Rucastle; Holmes deduces she has been made to impersonate Rucastle's imprisoned daughter Alice to drive off her suitor, and helps rescue Alice, who escapes and marries her fiancé while Rucastle is mauled by his own guard dog.

themes: table of contents for Volume I
outbreak and causes of the war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: This is the table of contents for Volume I, listing its chapters from the diplomatic breaking of the peace and the opening of the war through the Battles of Mons, Le Cateau, the Marne, and the Aisne, the La Bassée-Armentières operations, the two chapters of the First Battle of Ypres, a retrospect, and the winter lull of 1914.

themes: table of contents for Volume II
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: This is the table of contents for Volume II, listing its chapters on the opening months of 1915, Neuve Chapelle and Hill 60, the two stages of the Second Battle of Ypres (the gas attack and the Bellewaarde Lines), the Battle of Richebourg-Festubert, the trenches of Hooge, and the three chapters covering the Battle of Loos.

themes: table of contents for Volume III
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: This is the table of contents for Volume III, listing its chapters on the build-up from January to July 1916 and the successive phases of the Battle of the Somme, from the July 1 attacks on Gommecourt, Serre, and Beaumont Hamel through Gough's northern-flank operations, the Thiepval Ridge, and the Battle of the Ancre in November 1916.

themes: table of contents for Volume IV
German withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: This is the table of contents for Volume IV, listing its chapters on the German retreat to the Arras-Soissons front, the Battle of Arras, the Battle of Messines, the four chapters covering the Third Battle of Ypres (Passchendaele), and the two phases of the Battle of Cambrai.

themes: table of contents for Volume V
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: This is the table of contents for Volume V, listing its chapters on events up to March 21, 1918, the several corps-by-corps attacks of the Second Battle of the Somme (the German Spring Offensive), the Somme front from April onward, the two-part Battle of the Lys, and the Battles of the Chemin des Dames and of the Ardres.

themes: table of contents for Volume VI
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: This is the table of contents for Volume VI, dedicated to General Sir William Robertson, listing its chapters on the opening operations of July-August 1918, the Battle of Amiens, the sustained advances of Rawlinson's Fourth Army, Byng's Third Army, and Horne's First Army through the Hindenburg Line and the Battle of the Selle, down to the war's end in November 1918.

themes: retreat from Mons to the Marne
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: Volume I's full text opens with Conan Doyle's political analysis of Anglo-German rivalry and the diplomatic collapse of July-August 1914, Britain's entry into war over the invasion of Belgium, and Kitchener's mobilization of the New Armies, before narrating the BEF's opening 1914 campaign under Sir John French, from the retreat from Mons and Le Cateau through the Marne, the Aisne, and the First Battle of Ypres to the onset of trench deadlock.

Volume II's full text covers the British campaign through 1915, including the attack at Neuve Chapelle and Hill 60, the German chlorine gas attack that opened the Second Battle of Ypres and the subsequent Bellewaarde fighting, the Battle of Richebourg-Festubert, the mine warfare at Hooge, and the costly Battle of Loos in the autumn.

Volume III's full text (covering 1916) narrates the Battle of the Somme in detail, from the catastrophic first-day assaults on Gommecourt, Serre, and Beaumont Hamel through the slow attritional fighting of July and August, the breaking of the German second and third lines, the gaining of the Thiepval Ridge, and the final Battle of the Ancre in November 1916.

themes: German retirement to the Hindenburg Line
first massed tank attack at Cambrai
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: Volume IV's full text covers 1917: the German withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line, Allenby's Battle of Arras, Plumer's mine assault at Messines, the grinding months-long Third Battle of Ypres culminating in the mud of Passchendaele, and the Battle of Cambrai, notable for the first large-scale use of tanks.

themes: collapse and fighting retreat of the Fifth Army
crisis of unified Allied command under Foch
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: Volume V's full text covers the crisis of March-June 1918, as Ludendorff's Spring Offensive smashes into Gough's Fifth Army and Byng's Third Army on the Somme, forcing a desperate fighting retreat, followed by the German attack on the Lys and further blows at the Chemin des Dames and Ardres, amid the establishment of Foch as Allied generalissimo.

themes: Battle of Amiens as turning point
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_british_c.plot: Volume VI's full text narrates the final Allied victory campaign of 1918, opening with Rawlinson's Fourth Army's decisive Battle of Amiens on August 8, then following Byng's Third Army and Horne's First Army as they smash through the Hindenburg Line and press the German retreat through the Battle of the Selle to the general Allied advance that ends with the Armistice on November 11, 1918.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_captain_o.plot: Aboard a whaler trapped in Arctic ice, the ship's doctor records the escalating madness of Captain Craigie, who is haunted by visions of a spectral woman while the superstitious crew report their own ghostly sightings; the captain finally runs out onto the ice after the apparition and is later found dead, smiling, his arms still outstretched.

themes: mutiny and mass murder at sea
the mystery of the Marie Celeste
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_captain_o.plot: Dr. Jephson recounts his voyage on the Marie Celeste with the sinister quadroon Goring, who secretly orchestrates the murder of the captain, his family, and the crew with the help of African conspirators, sparing Jephson alone because of a sacred stone relic, then reveals himself as a lifelong avenger of his enslaved mother before setting him free to tell the tale.

themes: the soul separated from the body
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_captain_o.plot: A mesmeric experiment meant to let a professor and his student commune spirit-to-spirit instead swaps their souls into each other's bodies, producing a string of chaotic, comic misadventures until the two repeat the experiment to switch back, after which Fritz is finally allowed to marry the professor's daughter Elise.

A reclusive Highland hermit rescues a young Russian woman from a shipwreck and refuses to surrender her to Ourganeff, the sailor who had earlier abducted her as his forced bride, but Ourganeff seizes her again during a storm and both are washed ashore dead the next morning, his body still shielding hers from the sea.

A nervous transatlantic passenger overhears two fellow travellers discussing a mysterious ticking box and becomes convinced they are Fenian bombers plotting to destroy the ship, working himself into a frenzy of dread until the box, sprung at the appointed hour, turns out to release two carrier pigeons for a private betting race.

A young corkcutter emigrating to Canada is robbed and beaten into a near-fatal head injury that erases his memory, and he spends fifty years rebuilding a successful life under a new name until the sound of west-country sailors' voices restores his past, prompting him to return home and find his faithful sweetheart Mary still waiting, whom he finally marries in old age.

A frustrated amateur author falls asleep and dreams that history's great English novelists gather around his table to jointly narrate a composite adventure story, each contributing a chapter written in an exaggerated parody of his own distinctive style, before the dream dissolves and he wakes to his wife's scolding.

Narrator Armitage recounts how his friend Cowles becomes fatally infatuated with the hypnotically powerful Kate Northcott, whose two previous suitors died mysteriously after breaking off their engagements to her, and after Cowles too flees in horror from some terrible revelation, he is lured over a sea-cliff to his death by her spectral apparition.

A mysterious itinerant preacher reforms the rough mining camp of Jackman's Gulch through relentless scripture-reading, then reveals himself to be the notorious bushranger Conky Jim, holding the congregation at gunpoint during a staged church service while his accomplices murder the gold-keeper and steal the camp's stored gold.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_case_book.plot: Holmes uses a wax dummy of himself and eavesdropping from a hidden door to trick Count Sylvius and his accomplice Sam Merton into revealing the hiding place of the stolen Mazarin diamond, then plants the recovered stone in the pocket of the skeptical Lord Cantlemere as a practical joke.

Holmes investigates the death of the wife of ruthless millionaire Neil Gibson, whose governess Grace Dunbar stands accused of murder; by reconstructing the crime with a weighted revolver on a string, Holmes proves Mrs Gibson staged her own suicide to frame her rival for her husband's affections.

themes: love and obsession in old age
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_case_book.plot: Holmes investigates why elderly Professor Presbury's wolfhound keeps attacking him and why the professor is seen crawling at night, discovering that Presbury has been injecting a monkey-derived serum obtained from a Prague scientist in a desperate bid to seem youthful enough to win his young fiancée.

Called to investigate a mother apparently drinking her baby's blood, Holmes deduces she was actually sucking poison from an arrow wound inflicted on the infant by her jealous stepson, who resented his half-brother.

An American conman posing as 'John Garrideb' invents a fake inheritance scheme to lure a harmless collector out of his rooms so he can search for a hidden counterfeiting press left by a man he had killed years before; Holmes exposes him as the wanted criminal 'Killer' Evans.

Holmes tries to stop a beautiful, infatuated young woman from marrying the murderous Baron Gruner, and after being beaten by the Baron's thugs, steals Gruner's diary of conquests to expose him—only for a jilted former victim to disfigure the Baron with vitriol, finally breaking the engagement.

Narrated by Holmes himself, he helps a former soldier uncover why his war comrade has been hidden away by his father, revealing the young man believes he contracted leprosy in South Africa and is living in secret isolation—though a specialist ultimately diagnoses a harmless skin condition.

An elderly, miserly retired paint merchant claims his young wife eloped with a doctor and stole his savings, but Holmes deduces that he murdered both his wife and her supposed lover, gassing them in his sealed strong-room, and exposes him by luring him away with a fake telegram to search the house.

Holmes protects an elderly widow from a scheme by a wealthy beauty to buy and destroy her late son's unpublished manuscript, which exposed how she had cruelly discarded him as a lover, and negotiates the return of stolen money for the widow's world travels.

In his Sussex retirement, Holmes investigates the agonizing death of a science teacher on a seaside beach, suspecting murder by a rival for the same woman's affections, before discovering the true culprit is a lion's-mane jellyfish in the bathing pool.

A veiled, disfigured former circus performer confesses to Holmes that she and her lover conspired to murder her brutal husband and stage it as a lion attack, but the lion turned on her too, and Holmes persuades her not to take her own life despite her ruined face and lifelong seclusion.

Holmes investigates strange goings-on at a racing estate—a hidden coffin, burned bones, an impersonated invalid—and discovers that debt-ridden Sir Robert Norberton concealed his sister's natural death and had an actor impersonate her so he could keep racing his Derby horse until his gamble paid off.

themes: racial prejudice in the justice system
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_case_of_m.plot: Conan Doyle lays out his investigation into the wrongful conviction of George Edalji, a half-Parsee solicitor framed for cattle-maiming, detailing years of anonymous hoax letters against his family, flawed forensic evidence, and the near-blind Edalji's physical inability to have committed the crimes.

Conan Doyle publishes facsimile handwriting comparisons to demolish the police theory that George Edalji wrote the anonymous 'Greatorex' letters that incriminated him, arguing the Home Office's refusal of compensation rests on the discredited testimony of expert Thomas Gurrin.

Conan Doyle builds a profile of the true anonymous letter-writers as brothers connected to Walsall Grammar School, tracing recurring handwriting quirks and grudges across the 1892-95 and 1907 letter campaigns to show they, not Edalji, were responsible.

themes: continuity of a persecutor's identity across decades
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_case_of_m.plot: Conan Doyle compares handwriting samples spanning 1893 to 1907 to prove the same 'bad boy' persecutor—writing as 'Martin Molton'—authored all the anonymous letters, definitively clearing George Edalji of authorship.

Conan Doyle formally lays out his case that Royden Sharp, a former ship's apprentice with a large horse-lancet and a record of violence, committed the Wyrley cattle-maiming outrages for which George Edalji was wrongly convicted.

Conan Doyle details Royden Sharp's school record of forgery, arson, cruelty, and expulsion from Walsall Grammar School as early evidence of the destructive character later responsible for the Wyrley outrages.

A schoolfellow, Wynne, gives a first-hand account of young Royden Sharp's destructive pranks, lies, and vandalism at Walsall Grammar School, corroborating Conan Doyle's case that Sharp was the true author of the persecuting letters.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_coming_of.plot: Conan Doyle recounts how he first heard of and pursued the 'Cottingley fairy' photographs taken by two young girls, tracing the chain of correspondents and assembling early evidence for their authenticity.

themes: belief in fairies as a new frontier of knowledge
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_coming_of.plot: Conan Doyle publishes the first full account of the Cottingley fairy photographs in the Strand Magazine, presenting Gardner's investigation into the girls' family and photographic experts' opinions that the negatives showed no signs of fakery.

Conan Doyle surveys the press reception of the fairy photographs, including a skeptical Westminster Gazette investigation and heated exchanges with critics like Major Hall-Edwards and Maurice Hewlett who argued the images were faked.

A second series of fairy photographs is taken and authenticated, and a clairvoyant companion accompanies the girls to independently corroborate their visions of fairies in the glen, even as fresh photographic attempts later fail.

A detailed, diary-style record of a clairvoyant observer's sightings alongside the two girls in the Cottingley glen, describing gnomes, water nymphs, wood elves, and dancing fairy bands seen over several days.

themes: independent historical and contemporary testimony of fairy sightings
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_coming_of.plot: Conan Doyle compiles independent accounts of fairy sightings from various witnesses across decades—children, clergymen, and psychics—arguing that consistent details across unconnected testimonies support the reality of such beings.

Conan Doyle presents further letters and testimonies received after publication of the fairy photographs, from witnesses in the Isle of Man, New Zealand, Canada, and elsewhere describing their own encounters with fairies.

Conan Doyle presents the Theosophical explanation of fairies as nature spirits tied to plant growth and elemental evolution, drawing on Edward Gardner's and Bishop Leadbeater's occult classifications of fairy types worldwide.

A brief front-matter chapter heading introducing the start of Conan Doyle's History of Spiritualism, covering the mystical visions of Swedenborg and the prophetic movement of Edward Irving and the Shakers; no narrative content beyond the chapter listing.
A brief front-matter chapter heading, titled 'The Prophet of the New Revelation,' from the opening of Conan Doyle's History of Spiritualism; no narrative content beyond the chapter title.
Recounts the 1848 Hydesville rapping phenomena that are held to mark the origin of Spiritualism, and traces the early public career of the Fox Sisters as the first celebrated mediums.
Describes the rapid early spread of Spiritualist phenomena and mediums across America in the years following the Hydesville episode.
Traces the arrival of Spiritualism in England and its continued, gradually strengthening progress among English believers and investigators.
Covers the celebrated career of the medium D. D. Home and the cabinet séance demonstrations of the Davenport Brothers, both central figures in the history of physical mediumship.
Describes the scientific experiments and investigations into physical mediumship conducted by the chemist and physicist Sir William Crookes in the early 1870s.
Recounts the materialization séances conducted by the Eddy Brothers and by the medium couple the Holmeses.
Covers the mediumship and subsequent legal troubles of the slate-writing medium Henry Slade and of Dr. Monck.
Discusses collective, organized investigations of Spiritualist phenomena undertaken by scientific bodies, with an appendix closing the historical survey.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: Describes how King Leopold used Stanley's expeditions and hundreds of dubious native treaties to found the Congo Free State under the Berlin Conference, promising free trade and native welfare that were never honoured.

themes: state monopoly on land and produce
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: Traces the Congo State's development from philanthropic pretence to a system of forced labour and land monopoly, culminating in the illegal executions of the British trader Stokes and the Austrian trader Rabinck.

themes: chain of command and moral guilt
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: Explains the mechanics of the rubber-collection system, in which armed capitas terrorize villages to meet quotas, and argues that ultimate responsibility for the resulting atrocities rests with King Leopold himself.

Presents independent eyewitness testimony from the English traveller Glave, the American missionary Murphy, and the Swedish missionary Sjoblom documenting massacres, hand-severing, and the state's complicity in the violence.
Covers the Mongalla massacres carried out under Captain Lothaire, the confessions of agents Lacroix and Moray published in the Belgian press, and the show trials that punished only subordinates.

themes: rubber terror in the Crown Domain
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: American missionary Joseph Clark's letters spanning 1893 to 1900 document the catastrophic depopulation of the Lake Mantumba region and a native uprising against the rubber agents.
Consul Roger Casement's landmark 1904 official report details mutilations, illegal fines, and direct testimony from natives describing Belgian-ordered killings and hand-taking.
King Leopold's own Commission of Inquiry takes harrowing testimony, including Chief Lontulu's account of massacre and forced cannibalism, exposing the systemic complicity of Belgian officials.

After the Commission's report, abuses continue unabated; missionary Stannard is prosecuted for repeating native testimony, and traveller Murdoch documents ongoing forced labour and depopulation in the Crown Domain.

themes: Catholic testimony against the Congo State
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: The Jesuit Father Vermeersch's writings corroborate the Protestant missionaries' accusations, criticizing the State's seizure of native land and the secretive finances of the Crown Domain.
Recent British consular reports document ongoing forced rubber collection, extreme poverty, and abuse of natives in the A.B.I.R. and Kasai concession territories despite claimed reforms.

Traces the political history of British protests, Belgian parliamentary debates led by reformers Vandervelde and Lorand, and the 1908 annexation of the Congo by Belgium that changed nothing in practice.
Conan Doyle systematically rebuts common Congolese-apologist arguments point by point, comparing Congo impunity unfavourably to British and German colonial accountability.

themes: compensation and punishment of the guilty
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: Proposes solutions to end the Congo atrocities, including international partition of the territory or unilateral British intervention, and calls for compensation for victims; an appendix separately covers the unrelated Edalji miscarriage-of-justice case.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_dealings_.plot: Believed hanged, Sharkey escapes execution and impersonates the Governor of St Kitt's aboard Captain Scarrow's ship, murders the mate, and flees after terrorizing the crew mid-voyage.

The reformed pirate Stephen Craddock disguises a ship to lure and trap Sharkey, but is himself captured; Sharkey turns the ruse against a welcoming party at Jamaica until Craddock swims to warn them, dying in the attempt.

After massacring the passengers of a captured ship, Sharkey discovers the surviving Spanish woman he has abused is a leper who has infected him; his mutinous crew, fearing contagion, maroons captain and woman together.
Merchant Copley Banks, whose wife and sons Sharkey murdered years before, turns pirate himself to win Sharkey's trust, then traps him bound over a powder-primed cannon and blows him up in revenge.
The British frigate Leda, lured into a trap by a French frigate, is saved when the pirate brig Slapping Sal draws the Frenchman's fire and is destroyed, redeeming the memory of its criminal captain.
A respectable county magistrate secretly turns masked highway robber for one night to rob the fraudulent banker who ruined him, is unmasked by a friend, and justifies the act as private justice.

Sailors salvaging a derelict brig find a locked antique treasure chest that has already killed two men who tried to force it open, and discover it conceals a spring-loaded spike trap guarding a worthless candlestick.

Trapped in Arctic ice aboard a whaler, the ship's doctor keeps a journal recording the increasingly deranged behaviour of Captain Craigie, who is haunted by visions of a lost sweetheart while the crew report ghostly cries on the ice. The captain finally leaps overboard to follow the apparition and is found dead and smiling, and the portrait of the woman he loved is later found cut from its frame in his cabin.

themes: isolation on a remote trading post
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_dealings_.plot: A yachtsman visiting a lonely West African trading station learns that native watchmen keep vanishing from the cooperage every third night; he joins the resident doctor for an overnight vigil, during which the fevered station agent Walker is found crushed to death in his sleep, and the true culprit is revealed to be a giant python swept downriver in a flood.

Two Yokohama clerks embezzle their employer's money to cover gambling debts and flee by yawl; overtaken by a pursuing police boat, Jelland shoots his weaker partner rather than see him captured and is himself mortally wounded, and a sudden squall carries the boat, its stolen gold, and the dying men out to sea, never to be found again.

A doctor sailing aboard the real-life mystery ship Marie Celeste recounts how his fellow passenger Goring, a vengeful mixed-race man avenging his mother's death at white hands, secretly sabotages the voyage and orchestrates the murder of the captain's family and crew by an African war party, sparing only Jephson because the natives revere a sacred meteorite stone he carries, before setting him free to tell the tale.

A nervous transatlantic passenger overhears two men discussing a mysterious ticking box and becomes convinced they are dynamiters planning to destroy the ship; after a night of mounting terror he confronts them at the critical moment, only to discover the 'infernal machine' is a trap releasing carrier pigeons for a private betting race.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_doings_of.plot: The impoverished McIntyre siblings bid farewell to Laura's fiancé, the sailor Hector Spurling, before he redeploys; both Laura and Hector separately describe strange encounters with an eccentric stranger, who gave Hector an unexplained fifty-pound note, introducing the mystery of the new owner of the great house being built nearby.

Robert learns the vicar has been handed a huge cheque by the new, mysterious owner of the great house; wandering in thought he strikes up conversation with a smoke-grimed 'workman' about the estate and its riches, only to discover the workman is Raffles Haw himself, who invites him inside.

Raffles Haw reveals his true identity to Robert and tours him through his fantastical mansion's marble courts, mechanical lifts, and a vast gem collection worth millions, explaining his belief that great wealth carries a duty to keep it circulating usefully rather than hoarded.

In his smoking room Haw dazzles Robert with rare tobaccos, a wine-dispensing device, and a mechanical crystal chamber that transports smokers into simulated Amazon and Egyptian scenes, then confides his loneliness and asks Robert to be his trusted go-between with the world, learning along the way that Robert's sister Laura is the woman he has been asking about.

Robert's account of Haw's wealth inflames his father's greed and his sister's ambition; Haw visits Elmdene, generously buys Robert's paintings, charms Laura by offering to send her a tiger, and that night Laura secretly asks Robert to hide her existing engagement to Hector from their new benefactor.

themes: warning of danger in courting a rich man
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_doings_of.plot: Raffles Haw sends Laura a live tiger in a cage as a token of admiration, causing a village sensation; Robert warns his sister that she seems to be encouraging Haw's romantic interest, which she does not deny.

Haw's fame for secret charity spreads as he single-handedly saves the Garraweg brothers' bank from collapse, but he firmly refuses beggars and the grasping old McIntyre, and shows Laura and Robert a burglar-trap that has caught two intruders in his mansion.

As Haw's courtship of Laura intensifies, he confides to Robert that he is in fact a 'billionaire' burdened by the responsibility of his fortune, outlining fantastical world-improving schemes—a shaft to the Antipodes, global canals, paying off the National Debt—that leave Robert uncertain whether Haw is a genius or a madman.

Old McIntyre spies on the weekly waggon delivering mysterious 'gold' to Haw's laboratory and grows obsessed with its source; meanwhile Haw proposes marriage to Laura, who accepts despite her existing engagement to Hector Spurling and writes him a letter breaking it off.

Haw takes Robert into his confidence and reveals the secret of his fortune: an electrical process he discovered by accident that transmutes base metals progressively—lead into mercury, platinum, and finally gold—which he has used to amass immense wealth while wrestling with the responsibility the discovery has placed on him.

Haw shows Robert his hidden laboratory and a treasure-room stacked with gold ingots, then demonstrates the transmutation process converting lead into gold before his eyes, binding him to secrecy and revealing that a sealed document will pass on the 'greater secret' only after his own death.

Robert loses interest in his painting now that he shares Haw's secret, while Laura prepares for a hastily arranged wedding to conceal her broken engagement; old McIntyre, embittered after Haw refuses him a loan, accuses Haw of being loved only for his money, unaware that Haw himself overhears the insult and coldly rebukes him.

Driven mad by greed, old McIntyre sneaks into Haw's laboratory at night to embrace and steal gold ingots, then attacks Haw with a razor when discovered; Robert arrives just in time to help subdue his clearly insane father, and the two men quietly confine him rather than expose the scandal.

Haw is devastated to learn from the vicar that his wealth has demoralised the whole community and unmanned Robert; while comforting Laura, Hector Spurling suddenly returns from sea unannounced, revealing to the stunned Haw that Laura was already engaged, and the shattered engagement leaves him reeling.

Summoned to the Hall, Robert finds Haw has spent his final hours smashing all his machinery and destroying his gold and gems before dying quietly of a broken heart, leaving a letter renouncing his alchemical secret forever as having brought only corruption and misery to everyone it touched; the McIntyre family is left scattered and ruined by its contact with his fortune.

themes: evidence for spiritualism and survival after death
psychic obsession as a cause of illness
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_edge_of_t.plot: In this nonfiction chapter of his spiritualist survey, Doyle marshals case after case as evidence of psychic phenomena: Houdini's inexplicable escapes, Dr Wickland's trance-mediumship treatment of patients supposedly 'obsessed' by earthbound spirits, purported posthumous messages from Oscar Wilde received through automatic writing, a haunted-house investigation with Mr Podmore, and eyewitness accounts of fairy sightings, all presented to rebut sceptics like Dr Haldane.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_exploits_.plot: Young Hussar Gerard accompanies Sub-Lieutenant Duroc to confront Baron Straubenthal, revealed as the Jacobin who had Duroc's father murdered during the Revolution; after Duroc strikes him, the Baron traps them in a storeroom, but the pair blast their way out with an improvised petard, kill the Baron and his dogs, rescue his abused stepdaughter, and flee the castle moments before its powder magazine explodes.

themes: secrecy and duty to the Emperor
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_exploits_.plot: Napoleon secretly recruits Gerard to escort a decoy (De Goudin) to a night meeting with two assassins from the Corsican 'Brothers of Ajaccio'; after the decoy is stabbed, Gerard kills both attackers, only to discover the real Napoleon had secretly followed and watched everything, rewarding him with a promotion and sworn silence.

Wounded and stranded in Spain, Gerard is ambushed by guerrillas led by the poetry-writing brigand El Cuchillo, is rescued by a young English dragoon officer, then gambles his freedom on a game of écarté with his rescuer before Lord Wellington himself intervenes and takes him prisoner with a pun on the word 'king.'

Imprisoned at Dartmoor, Gerard engineers an elaborate escape nearly foiled by his cowardly cellmate's betrayal; after a night spent running in circles, stealing a coat, and being knocked out by a champion boxer in training, he is recaptured, only to learn the letter he carried all along announced his own prisoner exchange.

characters: the Countess of La Ronda (Mrs Morgan)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_exploits_.plot: Sent with fifty hussars to hang the renegade brigand 'Marshal Millefleurs' and free a hostage countess, Gerard joins forces with his old English friend the Bart, is captured through a disguised abbot's trickery, but turns the tables by capturing the villain himself and negotiating a prisoner exchange—only to be outwitted again when the 'Countess' proves to be the brigand's own devoted wife.

characters: the false 'Countess Palotta' / Princess of Saxe-Felstein
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_exploits_.plot: Carrying secret papers meant to keep the Prince of Saxe-Felstein loyal to Napoleon, Gerard is seduced and robbed of them by a supposed damsel in distress who turns out to be the Prince's own patriotic wife; he still bluffs his way before the Prince's council, but a fiery nationalist song sways the Prince to join the German uprising, and Gerard barely escapes hanging by her night-riders.

Sent by Napoleon with a despatch deliberately meant to fall into enemy hands, Gerard instead fights his way alone through occupied towns, escapes capture by disguising himself as a captured Cossack officer, and delivers the letter as ordered—only to be furiously scolded by Napoleon for succeeding at a mission designed to fail, before being awarded the medal of honour anyway.

As Napoleon's empire collapses in 1814, Gerard and two comrades are secretly tested with a false offer to betray the Emperor, then trusted with retrieving vital papers from the Countess Walewska's carriage; after a deadly chase in which two comrades are killed by an unknown traitor's agents, Gerard alone recovers the papers and helps Napoleon bury them secretly in the forest, obediently forgetting their location.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_firm_of_g.plot: This file contains only the book's front matter — a dedication to Professor William K. Burton and a preface thanking Mr P. G. Houlgrave for research on the African chapters — with no narrative content.

John Girdlestone visits his dying friend John Harston, who bequeaths most of his fortune to his daughter Kate and extracts a solemn oath from Girdlestone to guard and treat her as his own child; Girdlestone privately calculates the inheritance while his son Ezra coldly speculates about it.

The philanthropist Jefferson Edwards visits Girdlestone's office seeking donations for a dubious 'Aboriginal Evolution Society'; Girdlestone makes a showy donation, privately regarding it as a shrewd investment in his public reputation.

The widow of a sailor who died in the firm's service comes begging for her husband's back pay; Girdlestone coldly denies her any help despite pious platitudes, while the humble clerk Gilray secretly gives her money from his own pocket.

The drunken Captain Miggs reports the Black Eagle's dangerous voyage and threatens to expose Girdlestone's practice of overloading past the Plimsoll line; Girdlestone silences him by restoring his pay, revealing the firm deliberately runs unsafe, over-insured ships.

Student Tom Dimsdale and his friend Jack Garraway practice boxing in Edinburgh lodgings; Tom's father Dr. Dimsdale arrives unannounced, mistakes their sparring for a violent assault, and tackles Garraway before the confusion is cleared up.
Dr. Dimsdale is taken by his son and Garraway to watch the raucous rectorial election riot at Edinburgh University, where a 'Liberal' victory placard sparks a wild scramble around a statue.

The Dimsdale party watches the England-Scotland rugby international in Edinburgh; Tom scores the decisive try and breaks his collarbone, and in the aftermath realizes he has fallen in love with his cousin Kate.
Distracted by his love for Kate, Tom struggles to prepare for his first professional medical exam; he scrapes through the zoology and botany vivas thanks to lucky guesses and a sympathetic examiner.
Tom disastrously fails his chemistry viva after fixating on the word 'cacodyl,' walks out in humiliation, and writes to his father asking to abandon medicine for a career in commerce.

The impecunious, aristocratic Major Clutterbuck and his German companion Von Baumser are introduced in their shabby lodgings; after Ezra Girdlestone refuses him a loan, Von Baumser reveals he has secret information that the Girdlestone firm is financially rotten.

John Girdlestone confesses to his son that he has secretly speculated away the firm's capital and that they face ruin; the two agree that Ezra should marry the wealthy ward Kate Harston, and Girdlestone proposes a scheme to 'corner' the diamond market.

Girdlestone explains his plan to fake a diamond discovery abroad to crash prices and buy in cheap, with Ezra to travel to the diamond fields and Major Clutterbuck proposed as an agent; Girdlestone also swindles his devoted clerk Gilray out of his inheritance under the guise of a favorable loan.
Kate, kept isolated by Girdlestone, chances upon Tom in the street; they walk together, she recounts Ezra's cruelty to a cat, and Tom declares his love, leading to a secret engagement.

Ezra tries to recruit Major Clutterbuck as an agent in the fraudulent diamond scheme; the major, offended despite his own dubious morals, refuses, and when Ezra attacks him he draws a pistol and forces him out at gunpoint, later revealing it was unloaded.

Girdlestone persuades Dr. Dimsdale to buy Tom a partnership in the firm for seven thousand pounds, using the money to shore up the firm's finances while Tom believes he has joined a thriving business.

Tom proves himself a capable and fair-minded partner in the firm and continues secretly meeting Kate; Ezra departs for Africa to execute the diamond scheme, and Girdlestone shows unexpected emotion at his son's departure while eyeing Kate with strange dread.

Ezra's letters from Kimberley describe his shrewd diamond dealings and racist treatment of Black workers; back in London, Girdlestone reviews his secret private ledger revealing the firm's true dire financial state as Major Clutterbuck arrives.

Major Clutterbuck reveals he knows of the Girdlestones' fraudulent diamond scheme and blackmails John Girdlestone into paying him a thousand pounds for silence, which he then spends extravagantly with Von Baumser.

Fabricated news of a huge diamond discovery in the Ural Mountains spreads through the London press and Stock Exchange, causing panic among diamond dealers, while Girdlestone feigns concern for his son's investments.

News of the fake Russian diamond discovery reaches Kimberley via a sensational newspaper editor; Ezra rides to spread the alarming news among miners, and the next morning a ruined digger, 'Unlucky Jim,' is found to have shot himself.

Ezra secretly buys up diamonds cheaply during the panic through his agent Farintosh, but Farintosh and his accomplices Burt and Williams conspire against him, and Burt knocks Ezra senseless while the trio flee with his diamonds and money.

Ezra recovers and leads a mounted police pursuit of the thieves across the veldt; in a gunfight Farintosh is mortally wounded and, before dying, reveals that a genuine new diamond field has been discovered at Jagersfontein, dooming the Girdlestones' scheme regardless.
Ezra returns to London having lost most of the diamond profits; facing utter ruin, he and his father decide the only way to save the firm is for Ezra to marry Kate Harston and seize her inheritance.
Girdlestone discovers Tom and Kate's secret engagement and forces Tom to promise to avoid all contact with Kate for an indefinite trial period, then secretly destroys Tom's explanatory letter to her.

With Tom kept away, Ezra courts Kate with false gifts and manufactured jealousy, including a staged sighting at the opera and a forged love letter, deliberately breaking her heart to make her more receptive to his advances.
John Girdlestone pressures Kate directly to accept Ezra's proposal by appealing to guilt and false paternal concern, while privately he and Ezra continue scheming to secure her fortune by any means.

The now-prosperous Major Clutterbuck becomes infatuated with his neighbor, the widow Mrs. Scully, and wins an introduction to her by inventing an elaborate fictional connection to a 'Major-General Scully.'
The major and Von Baumser reminisce over the trophies and tales of the major's military past in their lodgings, and receive an invitation to a dance at Mrs. Scully's boarding house.

At a lively boarding-house dance, Major Clutterbuck proposes marriage to Mrs. Scully; after each confesses uncertainty about the other's finances, they agree to marry for love, and she asks him to give up gambling.

While overseeing cargo unloading, Tom learns from Captain Miggs and the mate McPherson the full extent of Girdlestone's insurance fraud with unsafe ships; then Von Baumser lets slip that Ezra is rumored to be marrying Kate, and a horrified Tom rushes off to confront the truth at Eccleston Square.

Ezra proposes to Kate in the breakfast room and is refused; enraged, he kicks her dog and storms out, and John Girdlestone then confronts Kate before announcing she must leave for Hampshire that same afternoon. Tom Dimsdale arrives at Eccleston Square that evening only to learn the household has left with no address.

Ezra returns home and manipulates the jealous maid Rebecca into agreeing to go down to Hampshire as Kate's companion (really a spy). Meanwhile Tom confides in his parents about Kate's disappearance, and Dr. Dimsdale resolves to help find her while distrusting the Girdlestones.

Girdlestone takes Kate by train to a remote Hampshire station and then by wagonette to the crumbling, isolated Hampton Priory, where the sinister old caretaker Mrs. Jorrocks receives them for the night.

Girdlestone reveals Kate is to be kept prisoner at the Priory and denies her writing materials. She attempts to slip away through the grounds but is stopped by the paid gatekeeper Bill Stevens, and finds the walled grounds completely inescapable.

Rebecca joins Kate at the Priory amid a ghost story of a monk murdered by rats in the cellars. That night Ezra arrives, and he and his father openly discuss their ruinous finances and plot to murder Kate for her inheritance, weighing whether to bring in the violent Burt.

Kate fails again to escape, pelted by village boys while perched on a shed roof, and is later handed a 'poison' bottle by Girdlestone in a veiled suicide temptation, which she smashes. That night, sneaking out at 2am, she is confronted in the corridor by an apparition of a Dominican friar and faints from terror.

Tom follows Ezra by cab to a pub where Ezra meets the thuggish Burt, then chases them to Waterloo Station where a brawl breaks out before police pull the men apart and Ezra and Burt escape. Afterward Major Clutterbuck rushes up to Tom bearing an urgent letter.

Kate recovers from her fainting fit and rebuffs her guardian's veiled suicide temptation; Girdlestone telegraphs London for a 'doctor' (really Burt) and tells Stevens that Kate is dying and delirious. Kate bribes Stevens with her watch to post a plea for help, but he tears it up the moment she is out of sight.

Kate climbs onto the shed roof again and this time succeeds in hailing a passing stranger, Mrs. Scully, in her pony-carriage, telling her the full story of her imprisonment and fear of murder; Mrs. Scully promises to alert Major Clutterbuck in London.

Girdlestone telegraphs Ezra that the 'case is hopeless,' sealing the murder plan, while Mrs. Scully writes to Major Clutterbuck describing Kate's plight. Clutterbuck and Von Baumser resolve to gather armed allies and rush to Hampshire, meeting Tom Dimsdale en route with the urgent letter.

Kate feels hopeful after secretly arranging help through Mrs. Scully, but the jealous maid Rebecca accuses her of expecting Ezra; at breakfast Girdlestone unsettles her with a chilling anecdote and a memento-mori text, and the errand boy John confirms that Mrs. Scully has written to the major.

Ezra brings the hired thug Burt to the Priory, and Girdlestone lays out the plan to fake Kate's death on the railway line for five hundred pounds; the three men then spy on Kate through the window as she works in the garden.
Rebecca jealously accuses Ezra of loving Kate; Kate then receives a forged note purportedly from Ezra offering to help her escape that night at the withered oak, and decides to accept the invitation.

Ezra and Girdlestone set their ambush at the withered oak, but Rebecca has intercepted the note and gone out disguised in Kate's cloak and bonnet; Burt clubs her down in the darkness, believing he has killed Kate.

Tom, the major, Von Baumser and two Nihilist allies travel to the Priory and climb the wall, where they witness the murderers carrying a body to the railway; moments later Kate herself appears alive and unharmed, exposing that the killers struck the wrong woman.

The fleeing Girdlestones realize in horror that they have murdered Rebecca instead of Kate, and bribe the fisherman Sampson to sail them by night to the Downs so they can catch their ship the Black Eagle and escape to Spain.

Police capture Burt at the murder scene while the Girdlestones escape; Tom carries the exhausted Kate back to the Priory, and the inspector searches the house, uncovering Girdlestone's monk disguise and hypocritical diary.

The Girdlestones sail through the night and the following day along the coast, finally overtaking and boarding their own ship the Black Eagle, whose drunken captain Miggs at first believes he is hallucinating when he sees them.

The rotten, leaking Black Eagle is caught in a violent storm and wrecked on the Spanish coast; clinging together to a narrow rock ledge, Ezra kicks his father's hands loose, sending him to his death, while he himself is hauled to safety.

Burt is convicted and executed for Rebecca's murder; Tom marries Kate and the major marries Mrs. Scully in a joint wedding, the Girdlestone firm survives under new partners, and Ezra's fate ends obscurely years later in America.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Conan Doyle's preface to the final edition explains his revision process across sixteen editions and acknowledges the war correspondents whose reports supplied his material.

Traces Boer origins from Dutch and Huguenot settlers at the Cape through the Great Trek, the founding of the Transvaal and Orange Free State, the first Boer War, and the annexation disputes leading up to Majuba Hill.

Explains the discovery of Rand gold, the resulting Uitlander grievances over taxation, franchise, and corrupt Boer administration, and narrates the failed Uitlander reform agitation culminating in the Jameson Raid and its trials.

Covers the Bloemfontein Conference between Milner and Kruger, the failed franchise negotiations and British dispatches through 1899, and ends with the Transvaal's rejection of terms and its own ultimatum to Britain.

Describes Britain's inadequate garrison in South Africa versus Boer strength, the reinforcement of Natal, colonial offers of troops, and the final ultimatum exchange that brings war on October 11, 1899.

Describes the Boer invasion of Natal and the Battle of Talana Hill, where British infantry storm the hill at heavy cost (Symons mortally wounded) while a cavalry detachment is surrounded and forced to surrender, followed by Yule's difficult retreat to Ladysmith.

Recounts the British victory at Elandslaagte, where French and Hamilton's force storms a strong Boer position and captures guns and prisoners, followed by the smaller action at Rietfontein fought to protect the retreating Dundee column.

Describes White's failed general engagement around Ladysmith, where the main force is driven back but saved by naval quick-firers, while the isolated Nicholson's Nek column under Carleton loses its ammunition mules and is forced to surrender to Boer forces led by de Wet.

Covers the siege of Kimberley and Methuen's costly advance through the battles of Belmont and Enslin, culminating in the hard-fought crossing of the Modder River against Cronje's concealed trench line.

Narrates the disastrous night approach of the Highland Brigade into Cronje's concealed trenches at Magersfontein, Wauchope's death and heavy Highland losses, and Methuen's decision to withdraw after a costly, unsuccessful day of fighting.

Gatacre's night march toward the Boer position at Stormberg goes astray, and at dawn his exhausted column is ambushed on broken ground; the attack fails and roughly 600 men are left behind as prisoners in a humiliating retreat to Molteno.

themes: frontal assault on entrenched river position
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Buller's first attempt to relieve Ladysmith by storming the Tugela at Colenso collapses when Hart's Irish Brigade cannot find the ford and Colonel Long's guns are shot to pieces and abandoned; a shaken Buller afterward heliographs White suggesting surrender of Ladysmith, but White firmly refuses.

In the wake of the week of British defeats at Stormberg, Magersfontein and Colenso, London places Lord Roberts and Kitchener in supreme command and calls up massive reinforcements, while the stalled British armies wait and Colonel Pilcher's small colonial raiding column scores a rare bright success at Sunnyside.

themes: daring night raids on enemy guns
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Ladysmith endures months of bombardment, hunger and enteric fever under Joubert's investment, punctuated by gallant British sorties that spike Boer guns, until the massed Boer assault on Caesar's Camp and Wagon Hill on January 6th is repulsed after a desperate day-long fight.

General French uses a small, highly mobile mounted force to screen and herd the Boer invaders into Colesberg over many weeks of skirmishing, suffering a costly failed night attack by the Suffolks, until reinforced Boers under Schoeman and later De la Rey force a British withdrawal to Arundel.

Buller's second relief attempt crosses the Tugela and storms Spion Kop by night, but the exposed summit is scourged all day by Boer artillery; after Woodgate falls, Thorneycroft orders a night withdrawal just as Botha's discouraged Boers were themselves on the point of retreating, so the hard-won hill is lost.

Buller stages a feigned attack on Brakfontein while his real force storms and takes the hill of Vaalkranz across the Tugela, but his customary slowness in following up lets the Boers reinforce, and after two exposed days he again abandons the position and withdraws.

themes: cumulative cost of the Tugela campaign
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: In his fourth attempt Buller turns the Boer left via Monte Christo and Cingolo, then fights his way through the Pieters Hills despite Hart's brigade being badly mauled, finally breaking Botha's line so that Dundonald's cavalry rides into Ladysmith and ends the 118-day siege on March 3rd.

Kimberley endures a long siege complicated by friction between the military governor Kekewich and the domineering Cecil Rhodes, and by a huge Boer gun bombarding the town, until General French's cavalry, sent by Lord Roberts, makes a dramatic hundred-mile ride to relieve the city on February 15th.

themes: costly frontal assault versus starvation siege
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: After French's cavalry relieves Kimberley, Roberts's infantry traps Cronje's retreating Transvaal army by the Modder River; a bloody frontal assault ordered by Kitchener fails, but Roberts then patiently bombards and starves the laager until Cronje surrenders unconditionally on Majuba Day.

themes: missed chance to seize enemy leaders
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Roberts resumes his advance from Paardeberg, outflanking Boer positions at Poplars Grove (where Kruger and Steyn narrowly escape) and storming through at Driefontein, before marching his exhausted army into Bloemfontein on March 13th.

themes: ripple effects of a central victory
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Roberts's capture of Bloemfontein relieves pressure on the outlying British forces under Clements, Gatacre, Brabant and Buller, who advance in turn across the southern Free State and Natal, while a Boer peace overture to Lord Salisbury is answered with an uncompromising refusal to recognise Republican independence.

themes: British reverses during an operational pause
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: During Roberts's six-week halt at Bloemfontein a severe enteric fever epidemic devastates the army, while De Wet exploits the lull to ambush Broadwood's column at Sanna's Post, capturing guns and wagons, and to force the surrender of a detachment at Reddersberg.

themes: failed siege of a colonial garrison
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: A large Boer force besieges Colonel Dalgety's colonial garrison at Wepener for seventeen days without success, while British columns under Rundle, French and Ian Hamilton try to trap De Wet's retreating army in the south-east, but he slips clean through their converging cordons near Thabanchu.

Baden-Powell's small, resourceful garrison holds Mafeking through seven months of bombardment and assault, repelling Eloff's final desperate storm of the town in May, until the combined relief columns of Mahon and Plumer arrive on May 17th to end the 217-day siege.

Roberts's army sweeps rapidly north through the Free State and into the Transvaal, taking Johannesburg and then entering Pretoria on June 5th after a short action on the southern forts, freeing thousands of British prisoners held at Waterval.

themes: continued resistance after the capital's fall
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Buller forces Laing's Nek and enters the Transvaal from Natal while Roberts fights Botha's rallied army at Diamond Hill near Pretoria, dispersing but failing to destroy it, even as De Wet begins his disruptive raids on the British railway line to the south.

themes: mass surrender of a Boer army
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: De Wet's raiders destroy convoys and capture garrisons at Lindley and Roodeval along Roberts's vital railway, provoking a major British pursuit that eventually traps the main body of Free State fighters in the Brandwater Basin, forcing General Prinsloo's mass surrender at Fouriesburg.

Boer attacks flare up around Pretoria and in the west while Lord Kitchener and Lord Methuen conduct a long, muddy chase of De Wet's commando across the Vaal and the Magaliesberg, who repeatedly slips the net, even as an early Kitchener-Botha peace parley comes to nothing.

Combined British columns under Buller, French and Hamilton drive Botha's weakening army from its last strong position at Bergendal and pursue it to the Portuguese frontier, capturing the remaining Boer guns as Kruger flees into exile and Pole-Carew occupies Komatipoort.

De Wet raids into the Transvaal but is repulsed at Frederickstad and loses his guns in the surprise action at Bothaville where Le Gallais is killed; after seizing Dewetsdorp he is chased in a long, muddy pursuit by Charles Knox's columns back and forth across the Caledon River.

themes: heavy British losses on a mountain
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Scattered guerrilla fighting spreads across the Transvaal and culminates in the disaster at Nooitgedacht, where De la Rey and Beyers combine to surprise and rout much of Clements's column on the Magaliesberg; soon after, Lord Roberts departs for England and hands command to Lord Kitchener.

Boer commandos under Hertzog and Kritzinger cross into Cape Colony hoping to spark a Dutch rebellion, ranging deep toward the coast, while De Wet's own attempt to invade the Colony is hunted for weeks by Plumer and other columns and driven back across the Orange River with heavy losses.

Scattered Boer attacks on posts such as Belfast and Lichtenburg are repelled, Kitchener's peace talks with Botha at Middelburg break down over the demand for independence, and French leads a huge seven-column drive across the eastern Transvaal that strips the Boers of their last guns in that region.

themes: dash to capture the last Boer capital
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Plumer's mobile column dashes north to seize Pietersburg while other British forces sweep the Roos-Senekal district; the winter months bring the blockhouse system to maturity alongside sharp actions at Vlakfontein and the surprise night rout of Australians at Wilmansrust.

For months small guerrilla bands under Kritzinger, Scheepers and Lotter roam Cape Colony evading pursuit, until General French's coordinated drives finally destroy Lotter's commando and corner others, after which the young Scheepers is tried and executed while Kritzinger is acquitted.

A renewed wave of Boer offensives from September to December 1901 brings Gough's disaster at Blood River Poort, the gallant repulse of attacks on Forts Itala and Prospect, Colonel Benson's death in the fierce action at Brakenlaagte, and De Wet's devastating Christmas Eve surprise of the Yeomanry camp at Tweefontein.

themes: De Wet's narrow escape from encirclement
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: Through early 1902 relentless British drives and an ever-denser blockhouse network steadily shrink Boer numbers across the Transvaal and Orange River Colony, with De Wet barely slipping through one carefully laid trap, while the Bushveld Carbineers officers are tried and executed for the murder of Boer prisoners.

themes: capture and chivalrous treatment of a British general
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_boe.plot: De la Rey wins the war's last Boer victories, ambushing a convoy and then defeating and severely wounding Lord Methuen at Tweebosch, before Kitchener's elaborate long-distance night-drive operations finally crush his commando's offensive power at Rooiwal.

After months of negotiation, sixty-four Boer delegates meet at Vereeniging and vote to accept the British peace terms, and on May 31st, 1902 the Treaty of Vereeniging is signed, ending the war and annexing the former republics to the British Empire.

themes: restitution and compromise with a ghost
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_kei.plot: Dr Hardacre visits his rich uncle Sir Dominick Holden, an old Anglo-Indian surgeon haunted nightly by the ghost of a one-handed Indian patient whose amputated hand, promised to him after death, was lost in a fire. Hardacre obtains a substitute hand from a London hospital, and after a first failure realizes it must be a left hand, ending the haunting for good.

New schoolmaster Harold Weld discovers that his brutal, bullying colleague Theophilus St. James seems to dominate the gentle headmaster Dr McCarthy; after Weld is dismissed for prying too closely and later intervenes in a violent late-night struggle, it is revealed St. James is McCarthy's own son, an escaped convict the headmaster has sheltered for years.

An imprisoned burglar petitions for a review of his case, recounting how a scheming Lady Mannering lured him into robbing her husband's gold medal collection, then murdered her husband herself with his knife and framed the burglar for the killing.

Professor von Baumgarten and his student Fritz undertake a mesmeric experiment meant to prove the soul can leave the body; their souls accidentally swap bodies, producing comic chaos as each behaves according to the other's body and habits, until they repeat the experiment to restore themselves.

A frustrated, unpublished writer dreams that the great masters of English fiction gather at his table and collaboratively improvise a swashbuckling adventure about one Cyprian Overbeck Wells, each contributing in his own unmistakable style and needling one another, until the dream dissolves with his wife waking him.

A London séance circle, joined by a French occultist, attempts to materialize a thought-form after Deacon has spent the day painting a unicorn; the experiment unwittingly conjures a real, violent unicorn into the darkened studio, terrorizing the sitters before it vanishes.

Egyptologist Vansittart Smith, dozing overnight in the Louvre, witnesses a strange museum attendant unwrap and mourn a mummy; the attendant reveals himself as an ancient Egyptian who gained forbidden immortality and has searched four thousand years for a ring holding the antidote that will finally let him die and rejoin his beloved.

A Western town's electrical committee tries to execute a desperado with a massive overdose of electricity, but instead of killing him it renders him virtually immortal, impervious to hanging and gunfire alike, leaving the authorities baffled about what to do with him.

themes: the thin veil between life and death
the terror of the new motor age
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_kei.plot: A man recounts the exhilarating, terrifying maiden drive of his new motorcar down a steep hill with failing brakes, ending in a fatal crash; dazed among the wreckage he meets his old friend Stanley, long dead of enteric fever, and realizes with a shock that he too has just died.

Medical student Abercrombie Smith comes to suspect that his sinister neighbour Bellingham has learned to reanimate his mummy, Lot 249, and is using the creature to attack his enemies; after an attempt on his own life, Smith confronts Bellingham at gunpoint and forces him to hack up and burn the mummy and his occult papers.

themes: the empire's toll on its people
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_kei.plot: A Ceylon coffee merchant sails for home with his new bride while his friend Atkinson escorts her separately after he falls mysteriously ill; Vansittart dies of smallpox at sea, and his becalmed widow later sees what seems to be his corpse leap from the ocean, a moment the narrator later rationalizes as a decomposing body released from its burial weights.

A mixed group of holidaymakers trapped in a stalled observation-tower lift are terrorized by a religious-fanatic maintenance worker who deliberately weakens the cable, intending their deaths as a divine 'sign'; the officer Stangate leads them to break out onto the girders just as the madman leaps across and falls to his death.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_sha.plot: Narrator Jock Calder recalls the night of a false French-invasion beacon alarm on the Scottish border in his childhood, and how years later at boarding school he foiled a burglary by accident, winning the lasting friendship of the school's champion, Jim Horscroft.

Jock recalls his cousin Edie's childhood visits and fanciful storytelling, then describes how, at eighteen, he meets her again as a striking young woman come to live at West Inch after her father's sudden death.

themes: Napoleonic war as backdrop to private drama
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_sha.plot: Jock and Edie watch a naval skirmish between a British merchantman and French privateers from the shore; when Edie admires the enemy captain's daring and disparages country men as unworthy, a stung Jock threatens to enlist as a soldier, and the two share their first kiss.

Jim Horscroft returns from Edinburgh and quickly falls for Edie; Jock catches the two secretly courting on the hillside, confronts Jim, and Edie cruelly and openly chooses Jim over Jock, shattering their friendship and Jock's hopes.

With news that Napoleon has abdicated and peace declared, Jock and Jim find a mysterious, gravely wounded shipwrecked Frenchman on the beach who gives his name as Bonaventure de Lapp; despite Jim's suspicion, Jock brings the stranger home to West Inch.

themes: a mysterious past revealed in fragments
hints of a grand hidden identity
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_sha.plot: De Lapp settles into West Inch, winning over the family with harrowing war stories and lavish gifts, while Jock secretly notices that one of de Lapp's letters is addressed to 'the King of Sweden,' deepening the mystery of who he really is.

Over the following months de Lapp reveals startling military expertise, is treated with sudden deference by Major Elliott who recognizes him from the Peninsular War, and is caught by Jock secretly signalling someone from the ruined Peel tower, deepening suspicion about his true purpose.
A mysterious yacht anchors offshore, and Jock intercepts a secret letter left for Edie in the garden; confronting her, he is stunned to learn she has already secretly married de Lapp.

Jock learns the details of Edie's secret Catholic marriage to de Lapp and confronts him directly; de Lapp gives lavish farewell gifts to Jock's parents while Jock dreads how the betrayed Jim Horscroft will react when he learns the news.

Edie and de Lapp elope by yacht, leaving a letter revealing he is really Colonel de Lissac, aide-de-camp to Napoleon; Jim's devastation turns to grim resolve when news arrives that Napoleon has escaped Elba, and Jock, Jim, and Major Elliott all enlist to fight in the renewed war.

Jock and Jim join the 71st Highland Light Infantry and march with Wellington's army through Belgium as Napoleon crosses the frontier and pushes back the Prussians, the brigade finally taking its position on the ridge above the coming battlefield.

themes: the horror and chaos of Waterloo
courage under artillery and cavalry assault
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_sha.plot: On the morning of Waterloo, Jim and Jock glimpse Napoleon and, to Jim's fury, de Lissac riding at his side; the 71st endures relentless cannonade and cuirassier and lancer charges in square while the farm of Hougoumont burns and is fiercely defended all day.

As Napoleon's Imperial Guard makes its final advance, Jim recognizes de Lissac among the French officers and charges recklessly at him, triggering the brigade's decisive countercharge that breaks the Guard's column and turns the battle.

The morning after Waterloo, Jock and Major Elliott find Jim Horscroft dead from bayonet wounds and, nearby, the mortally wounded de Lissac, who confesses his past crimes, including the execution of the Duc d'Enghien, and dies asking Jock to carry his last words and possessions to Edie.

themes: disillusionment with vanity and social climbing
closure and return to peaceful rural life
the fading of the great shadow of war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_great_sha.plot: Jock visits Edie in Paris and finds her already remarried into high society, indifferent to Jim's death and eager to hide her humble origins from her new friends; Jock then returns home to marry, farm, and raise a family in the peace that follows, closing his memoir of the era.

themes: divided loyalty between Ireland and the British Army
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_green_fla.plot: An embittered Irish soldier in a British square fighting Sudanese dervishes nearly leads his mutinous, disaffected company to break and flee, but at the critical moment rallies them around a small green Irish flag, and they fight and die defending it, saving the square from disaster.

Merchant captain Scarrow takes aboard a passenger claiming to be the ailing Governor of St Kitt's returning to England, only to discover near voyage's end that 'the Governor' is actually the notorious pirate Sharkey in disguise, who has murdered the real governor, and who now robs and humiliates the crew before escaping.

themes: a trap mirrored back on its maker
defiance in the face of certain death
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_green_fla.plot: Reformed pirate Stephen Craddock disguises his ship as Sharkey's own vessel to lure and capture him, but Sharkey outwits him by seizing his real ship first and impersonating Craddock's triumphant homecoming to Jamaica; breaking free at the last moment, Craddock swims toward the welcoming official party to warn them, dying of gunshot wounds as he does so.

Copley Banks, whose wife and sons were murdered by the pirate Sharkey, spends two years disguising himself as a fellow pirate captain to win Sharkey's trust, then lures him aboard drunk, binds him over a loaded cannon, and blows up his ship in revenge.

A poor medical assistant, desperate for money to finish his degree, is secretly recruited to box the feared prizefighter the Master of Croxley in place of an injured local champion, training against his employer's wishes before the decisive match.
