During the Franco-Prussian War a Prussian officer sent to arrest a French count for guerrilla killings is instead captured, and the grieving count forces him to relive, blow by blow, the cruelties once inflicted on his own dead son by a captor before finally releasing him unharmed.

Sailors salvage an abandoned Brazilian brig along with a sealed antique treasure chest bearing a warning not to open it; when the greedy first mate forces the lock, a hidden spring-loaded blade kills him, and the captain has the chest thrown overboard.

A ruined London stockbroker recuperating at an Irish horse fair observes two mysterious foreign buyers bidding extravagantly against each other for horses and deduces that war is imminent, wiring his partner to sell securities just hours before France declares war on Germany.

A hard-drinking young farmer, warned by his doctor that he might suffer alcoholic hallucinations of monstrous animals, joins a record-breaking fox hunt and believes he has witnessed a giant demon fox slaughter the hounds, only to learn afterward it was an escaped Siberian wolf.

Three newspaper war correspondents camped by the Nile during the Sudan campaign are attacked by a small dervish raiding party; the young novice among them, wounded in the skirmish, makes a desperate night ride on a captured racing camel to be first to telegraph the story home.

A green British officer commanding a remote desert outpost fails to interrogate a mysterious captured Arab traveller, who escapes overnight, and is later mortified to learn the 'prisoner' was his own commanding general testing him in disguise.

A French embassy aide, learning that Egypt has fallen to the British just before a peace treaty is to be signed, kidnaps and delays a Foreign Office courier overnight by reciting the Koran to him, ensuring the treaty is signed before London learns the news.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_gully_of_.plot: Two young miners are murdered by a bushranger gang hiding in a mountain gully; a search party of miners and troopers tracks the killers, and young trooper Braxton, secretly backed by the miner Chicago Bill, single-handedly captures the whole gang at their mountain camp.

themes: reformation of a lawless mining camp
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_gully_of_.plot: A seemingly pious itinerant preacher reforms the morals of a wild Australian gold-mining camp over several months, then reveals himself as the bushranger Conky Jim, holding the assembled congregation at gunpoint in their own makeshift church while his confederates murder the gold-keeper and steal the camp's treasure.

A prison doctor draws out the life story of Maloney, the captured Bluemansdyke bushranger who saved his own neck by turning Queen's evidence, hearing of his fugitive years hunted across the world before he is finally killed years later in a shoot-out with an old enemy.

In Buda-Pesth a series of otherwise inexplicable murders among close friends are traced to an antique silver hatchet bearing a centuries-old curse compelling whoever grasps it to attack the person they love best.

A reclusive philosopher living alone on the remote Scottish coast rescues a young Russian woman from a shipwreck and is then stalked by the sailor who loves her and had originally abducted her; the two Russians ultimately drown together in a storm, the man's body still shielding hers.

A nervous passenger on a transatlantic steamer overhears two men discussing a mysterious ticking device and becomes convinced they are anarchist bombers planning to destroy the ship at ten o'clock, only to discover at the tense climax that the box contains a pair of racing pigeons for a private wager.

A young English corn-merchant's clerk sent on a secret business errand into rural Russia is mistaken for a fellow conspirator by a Nihilist secret society, nearly condemned to death alongside them when the real agent arrives, and is saved only by a police raid on the meeting.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_history_o.plot: An account of the Swedish scientist and seer Emanuel Swedenborg's visionary experiences and detailed descriptions of the spirit world, arguing that despite his obscure theology he was in effect the first great modern medium and pioneer of Spiritualism.

themes: religious ecstasy and speaking in tongues
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_history_o.plot: Chronicles Scottish preacher Edward Irving's London congregation erupting into 'gift of tongues' phenomena in the early 1830s, leading to his censure and early death, alongside the parallel spirit visitations experienced for years by American Shaker communities.

Traces the life of the barely educated young clairvoyant Andrew Jackson Davis, who while mesmerized dictated a vast philosophical work full of accurate technological prophecies, becoming, in Conan Doyle's account, the intellectual herald of the coming Spiritualist movement.

Recounts the famous 1848 Hydesville 'rappings' in which the young Fox sisters made contact with a spirit claiming to be a murdered peddler buried in the cellar, an event that launched the modern Spiritualist movement and was seemingly confirmed decades later by the discovery of a skeleton in the house walls.

Follows the later careers of the Fox sisters as celebrated mediums who married into respectability but were worn down by promiscuous public sittings and alcohol, culminating in Margaret's sensational 1888 public 'confession' of fraud and her subsequent tearful retraction.

Surveys the rapid spread of mediumship across America in the 1850s, including the dramatic conversions of sceptical Judge Edmonds and Professor Hare, the eccentric colony of self-proclaimed prophet Thomas Lake Harris, and the claim that a trance medium's message influenced Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation.

Describes American medium Mrs Hayden's pioneering 1852 visit to London, the vicious ridicule she endured from the British press, and the prominent scientists and free-thinkers, including Professor De Morgan and Robert Owen, who were convinced of her genuine powers.

Traces Spiritualism's steady growth in Britain through the 1860s-80s, the founding of societies and journals, and the heated scientific debate ignited when Professor Barrett presented psychic research to the British Association for the Advancement of Science.

Chronicles the career of D. D. Home, the celebrated medium whose repeated levitations and physical phenomena were witnessed by scientists, aristocrats, and European royalty, and who, unlike most mediums, never accepted payment for his gift.

Recounts the Davenport brothers' famous cabinet seances performed before huge public audiences across America and Europe under rigorous roped and sealed tests, and the riots, mob violence, and conjuring rivalries that dogged their controversial career.

Details eminent chemist William Crookes's rigorous four-year scientific investigation of teenage medium Florence Cook, including forty-four photographs of the materialised spirit form 'Katie King,' and his public declaration of belief that damaged his standing among sceptical scientific colleagues.

themes: the Katie King scandal and vindication
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_history_o.plot: Describes Colonel Olcott's ten-week investigation of the Eddy brothers' extraordinary materialisation phenomena at a remote Vermont farmhouse, and the subsequent Philadelphia scandal surrounding the rival Holmes mediums' own 'Katie King,' which Olcott's careful inquiry largely vindicated despite an alleged confession.

themes: mixed record of genuine power and fraud
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_history_o.plot: Follows slate-writing medium Henry Slade's sensational London prosecution and conviction (later overturned on a technicality), his subsequent vindication through rigorous experiments with German physicist Zollner, and the more troubled, occasionally fraudulent career of fellow materialisation medium Dr Monck.

themes: history of Spiritualism as a religious movement
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_history_o.plot: In this preface Conan Doyle explains why he undertook to write a history of Spiritualism, criticizes earlier partial or hostile accounts of the movement, and thanks his research assistant W. Leslie Curnow for his invaluable help compiling the material.

Chapter XIV surveys formal collective investigations into Spiritualism (the Dialectical Society 1869-71, the Seybert Commission 1884-87, the Institut General Psychologique sittings with Eusapia Palladino, and the Scientific American/Harvard inquiry into Mrs. Crandon, "Margery"), weighing sympathetic committee findings against hostile or inconclusive ones. An appendix adds early Hydesville-house haunting testimony, Horace Greeley's and the De Morgans' accounts, and a Davenport Brothers letter, closing Volume I.

This file contains only the chapter heading ("The Career of Eusapia Palladino"), no body text; per the title the chapter is devoted to the Italian physical medium's biography and the investigations of her powers.

This file contains only the chapter heading, no body text; per the title the chapter surveys great mediums of 1870-1900, namely Charles H. Foster, Madame d'Esperance, William Eglinton, and Stainton Moses.

This file contains only the chapter heading ("The Society for Psychical Research"), no body text; per the title the chapter covers the founding and work of the SPR, associated with figures such as Sidgwick, Myers, Gurney, and Barrett.

This file contains only the chapter headings ("Ectoplasm" and "Spirit Photography"), no body text; per the titles the chapters cover ectoplasmic materialization research and the history of spirit photography.
This file contains only the chapter heading ("Voice Mediumship and Moulds"), no body text; per the title the chapter covers direct-voice mediums and mediums producing paraffin-wax mould casts.

This file contains only the chapter heading ("French, German, and Italian Spiritualism"), no body text; per the title the chapter surveys Spiritualist movements and investigators in France, Germany, and Italy.
This file contains only the chapter heading ("Some Great Modern Mediums"), no body text; per the title the chapter profiles leading contemporary mediums of the author's own time.

This file contains only the chapter headings ("Spiritualism and the War" and "The Religious Aspect of Spiritualism"), no body text; per the titles the chapters cover the surge of Spiritualist belief during WWI bereavement (as with Oliver Lodge's son Raymond) and Spiritualism's religious implications.

This file contains only the chapter heading ("The After-Life as Seen by Spiritualists") plus an appendix marker, no body text; per the title the chapter presents the Spiritualist conception of the afterlife.

A biographical account of the Neapolitan medium Eusapia Palladino, tracing her career from obscure origins through decades of scientific investigation across Europe, culminating in the 1908 SPR inquiry by three skeptics who became convinced of her genuine powers despite her occasional trickery.

Profiles four notable mediums of 1870-1900: Charles Foster's clairvoyant skin-writing, Madame d'Esperance's materialisations of the spirit Yolande, William Eglinton's physical phenomena and slate-writing, and Stainton Moses's physical mediumship and inspired religious writings.

Reviews the founding and mixed record of the Society for Psychical Research, criticizing its hostility toward physical mediums while praising its lengthy investigation of Mrs. Piper and the elaborate 'cross correspondence' scripts including the Ear of Dionysius case.

Traces the history and scientific documentation of ectoplasm from early Spiritualist descriptions through Richet's coining of the term with medium Eva C., to Schrenck Notzing's and Geley's laboratory investigations and Crawford's theory of 'psychic rods.'

Surveys the history of spirit photography from Mumler's first 1861 result through numerous mediums (Hudson, Buguet, Boursnell, Wyllie, Hope, Deane), examining evidential 'extras,' controlled tests, and fraud accusations including Buguet's forced confession.

Examines voice mediumship from Jonathan Koons and Mary Marshall through Elizabeth Blake and Etta Wriedt, then details the physical evidence of ectoplasmic moulds and paraffin gloves obtained from mediums including Kluski, verified by Geley's controlled wax-immersion experiments.

Surveys French Spiritism founded by Allan Kardec with its reincarnation doctrine, then German Spiritualism through du Prel, von Hartmann and Driesch, and finally Italian Spiritualism's rich tradition of investigators (Lombroso, Morselli, Bozzano, Chiaia) converted through Eusapia Palladino.

Conan Doyle recounts his personal sittings with numerous contemporary mediums he judged genuine, including trance medium Mrs. Osborne Leonard, voice mediums Valiantine and Wriedt, materialisation medium Jonson, apport medium Bailey, and the automatic writer Vale Owen.

Describes how the First World War intensified public interest in Spiritualism, presenting prophecies of the war, apparitions and telepathic experiences of soldiers, spirit photographs of the fallen, and the legend of the Angels of Mons.

Argues that Spiritualism is compatible with and indeed restores primitive Christianity, citing early Church Fathers' psychic practices, sympathetic clergy testimonies, and new inspired scripts (the Cummins/Cleophas and Philip scripts) as evidence of continuity with apostolic gifts.

themes: appendix testimonies on early Fox and Davenport phenomena
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_history_o.plot: Describes Spiritualist teachings on the afterlife, ranging from earth-bound spirits through punitive and happy spheres, illustrated by scripts such as Lester Coltman's, followed by an appendix of corroborating historical testimonies including the pre-Fox Hydesville hauntings and the De Morgans' experiences.

themes: friendship and rivalry between Holmes and Watson
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Holmes and Watson deduce the character of an unseen visitor from the walking stick he left behind; the visitor, Dr James Mortimer, then arrives and hints at a serious problem on which he wants Holmes's professional advice.

Mortimer reads an old family manuscript telling the legend of the diabolical hound that pursued and killed the wicked Hugo Baskerville, then reports the recent mysterious death of Sir Charles Baskerville near the moor gate, revealing he found the footprints of a gigantic hound near the body.

Holmes questions Mortimer closely about the Yew Alley, the hound's footprints, and other moor sightings, then learns that Sir Henry Baskerville, the last heir, is arriving in London; Holmes studies a map of the moor and begins reconstructing the theory that Sir Charles was running in fear from something across the moor.

Sir Henry Baskerville shows Holmes a warning letter made of pasted newspaper words telling him to keep away from the moor, and reports a missing new boot; after the meeting Holmes and Watson trail Mortimer and Baskerville and spot a bearded man secretly following them in a cab, but lose him.

themes: the mystery of the missing boots
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: At the hotel Sir Henry discovers a second boot has vanished and the first mysteriously reappears; Holmes learns of the huge Baskerville inheritance, persuades Watson to accompany Sir Henry to Devonshire, and questions the cabman who reveals his mysterious fare cheekily claimed to be Sherlock Holmes himself.

themes: arrival at an ancestral house of gloom
the escaped convict on the moor
an unexplained woman's sobbing at night
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Holmes sees Watson and Sir Henry off to Devonshire with instructions to report facts; they reach gloomy Baskerville Hall, meet the butler Barrymore and his wife, and learn a dangerous escaped convict, Selden, is loose on the moor; that night Watson hears a woman sobbing somewhere in the house.

themes: a cryptic warning from a woman
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Watson discovers Barrymore lied about his wife's crying, meets the naturalist Stapleton who discusses the hound legend and the deadly mire, hears an eerie howl on the moor, and is urgently warned by Miss Stapleton to go back to London before she retracts the warning under her brother's watch.

themes: surveillance and suspicion of the household
growing romance between Sir Henry and Miss Stapleton
cataloguing the neighbours of the moor
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: In his first letter-report to Holmes, Watson describes the escaped convict, the budding attraction between Sir Henry and Miss Stapleton, eccentric neighbour Frankland, and his own night-time discovery of Barrymore stealthily holding a candle to a window as if signalling someone on the moor.

themes: the cry of the hound heard on the moor
the mysterious figure on the tor
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Watson and Sir Henry catch Barrymore signalling to Mrs Barrymore's fugitive brother Selden hiding on the moor, then chase the convict at night and hear the terrifying howl of a hound; fleeing home, Watson glimpses an unknown tall man silhouetted on a tor, while separately Stapleton furiously interrupts Sir Henry's proposal to his sister before later apologizing.

Watson's diary records the household's fear of the phantom hound and his confrontation with Barrymore, who confesses that Sir Charles died after a secret appointment with a woman signing herself 'L.L.'; Dr Mortimer identifies her as Laura Lyons of Coombe Tracey, and Watson also learns of a second stranger hiding on the moor.

Watson presses Laura Lyons in Coombe Tracey until she admits writing to Sir Charles but denies keeping the appointment, then uses gossipy neighbour Frankland's telescope sighting of a mysterious boy to track the hidden stranger on the moor to a stone hut, where he discovers the stranger is Sherlock Holmes himself.

Holmes reveals to Watson that he has secretly been on the moor and that Stapleton's 'sister' is really his wife; hearing the hound's cry, they rush out and find a body they at first take for Sir Henry but which proves to be the escaped convict Selden, killed while wearing Sir Henry's cast-off clothes, and Holmes conceals his suspicions from the arriving Stapleton.

themes: tightening the net around a villain
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Holmes explains why they still lack evidence to arrest Stapleton, spots his resemblance to a wicked ancestor in a family portrait proving him a Baskerville, extracts a full confession from Laura Lyons, and sets a trap using Sir Henry as bait for a dinner at Merripit House while Inspector Lestrade arrives from London to help.

themes: exposure of a faked supernatural hoax
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Holmes, Watson and Lestrade lie in wait as Stapleton's phosphorus-painted hound attacks Sir Henry on the fog-bound moor; they shoot the beast dead and save Sir Henry, then find Mrs Stapleton bound and beaten inside Merripit House, and she directs them toward the Grimpen Mire where her husband has fled.

themes: mechanics of a staged supernatural crime
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_hound_of_.plot: Back at Baker Street months later, Holmes recounts the whole solved case to Watson in detail—Stapleton's hidden Baskerville ancestry, his murder plot against Sir Charles and Sir Henry for the inheritance, and how every clue fitted together—while Stapleton himself is presumed to have drowned in the Grimpen Mire.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_land_of_m.plot: Journalists Malone and Enid Challenger prepare to investigate London's Spiritualist churches for a newspaper series; Challenger scoffs loudly at Spiritualism but is drawn into confessing an eerie unexplained incident of ghostly knocking he experienced the night after his wife's cremation.

Malone and Enid attend a crowded Spiritualist church service where medium Mrs Debbs delivers startling clairvoyant readings, one of which shocks Malone by naming his late colleague Professor Summerlee, and a mysterious visiting prophet, Miromar, delivers an ominous warning of coming judgement upon a materialistic mankind.

Surgeon Dr Atkinson, revealed as a cautious student of psychic matters, joins Malone and Enid after the seance; the three then visit Professor Challenger, who furiously mocks the medium's message about 'Summerlee' as absurd trickery and lectures Atkinson for taking it seriously.

Grocer Bolsover invites Malone and Enid to his home circle; editor Mervin warns Malone that mishandled psychic forces can be dangerous, and at the Bolsover seance the pair witness a child-spirit control called 'Wee One,' a levitating trumpet, and the 'rescue' of a confused earthbound spirit, deepening Malone's fascination despite Challenger's mockery.

After Malone publicly defends Spiritualists against a scoffing novelist at his club, he and Enid attend a materialization seance at the Psychic College with medium Linden, where several 'spirit' figures appear from the cabinet, including one Malone believes may be his own dead mother.

themes: persecution of genuine mediums by unjust law
apocalyptic prophecy of a coming new world
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_land_of_m.plot: Over the novel's remaining chapters, medium Tom Linden is entrapped and imprisoned under the Vagrancy Act while his brutal fraudulent brother Silas is exposed and dies in a supernatural accident; Roxton and Mason exorcise a haunted house, Malone and Mailey witness seance experiments in Paris, and finally Professor Challenger, after publicly humiliating himself debating Spiritualism, is converted when his own daughter Enid proves to be a medium and delivers him private proof from beyond the grave, clearing the way for Malone and Enid's marriage amid Miromar's warnings of a coming spiritual reckoning for the world.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: In 146 BC the last surviving Carthaginian war galley, commanded by Black Magro with the statesman Gisco aboard, limps home after Carthage's catastrophic naval defeat, only to be run down and dragged to destruction by pursuing Roman galleys within sight of the city, foreshadowing Carthage's total annihilation and even Rome's own eventual fall.

themes: manipulation of public taste by a claque
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: A rustic Greek shepherd-poet, Policles, stumbles into Emperor Nero's rigged singing contest at Olympia, publicly denounces Nero's dreadful performance and sings his own superior improvised ode, then flees for his life on learning that the ridiculous 'fop' he insulted was the Emperor himself.

themes: the thinness of the veil between past and present
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: A modern Scottish couple visiting the Roman excavations at Newstead are overwhelmed by vivid shared 'memories' of an ancient massacre, culminating in a dream in which the husband relives storming the fort and abducting his wife in a former Roman-era life, ending in a violent confrontation with her lover Marcus.

themes: futility of gentle coercion against faith
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: In Domitian's Rome a Christian slave, Datus, smashes his master's prized statue of Venus as blasphemous; despite the patrician Flaccus's attempt to win him over with kindness, Datus destroys the statue again rather than recant, and the Emperor condemns him to face wild beasts in the arena.

An enormous Thracian peasant, Theckla, joins the Roman army as 'Maximin,' rises through brute strength and ruthlessness to be proclaimed Emperor by mutinous soldiers after the murder of young Severus Alexander, rules through fear and plunder, and is finally murdered by his own troops outside besieged Aquileia.

A Christian hermit on the empire's eastern edge witnesses the vast Hunnic horde sweeping in from the steppe, kills the barbarian scout who has just murdered his rival Arian hermit-neighbor, and rides through the night to warn the Roman frontier fort of Tyras that the invasion has begun.

The Roman governor of Britain announces to his officers and a delegation of British nationalist leaders that all legions are being withdrawn to defend Rome itself; the Britons, who had long demanded self-governance, panic at the news and beg the Romans to stay, but the withdrawal proceeds and Britain descends into slaughter and conquest by invaders.

themes: seeds of conquest disguised as alliance
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: A Romano-British trader who speaks Saxon reports, in a letter to a friend, on the arrival of the first shiploads of Saxon mercenary-settlers invited by King Vortigern, observing their customs, religion and chieftains' debates, and concludes uneasily that these 'temporary' guests intend eventually to claim the island for themselves.

An abbot brings the illegitimate son of the now-Empress Theodora to Constantinople hoping for her mercy; nearly persuaded by the sinister eunuch Basil to have the boy and abbot secretly murdered to protect her secret, Theodora relents at the last moment and instead has the blackmailing eunuch himself thrown down the palace well to his death.

themes: merchants' tales within a frame narrative
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: A Constantinople merchant recounts to friends how, years earlier in the Arabian desert, his caravan was saved from robbers by a rival Arab caravan led by a charismatic visionary named Mahomet, who spoke prophetically of spreading his new faith by the sword across the world, one day even against Constantinople itself.

themes: psychic residue in a haunted object
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: An overworked accountant, driven to nervous exhaustion by a forensic fraud audit, begins seeing increasingly vivid visions in an antique silver mirror of a terrified woman and courtiers, which his doctor eventually identifies as the historical murder of Rizzio before Mary, Queen of Scots, at Holyrood Palace.

The infamous pirate Sharkey and his crew slaughter the passengers of a captured ship but keep and abuse a young Spanish noblewoman, only to discover she is a leper who has contaminated Sharkey himself; his mutinous crew then maroons the pair together on a remote island, from which Sharkey never returns.

The boastful Hussar Etienne Gerard recalls how, fleeing in terror from a charging bull while courting Marie Ravon in Normandy, he was tossed clean through her bedroom window, and used the mishap to spontaneously propose marriage on the spot, winning both his bride and, in the retelling, his cherished reputation for fearlessness.

Champion boxer Tom Spring is secretly hired and trained by a mysterious veiled noblewoman to fight her own husband, Lord Falconbridge, in revenge for his infidelity and cruelty; Spring wins the bout fairly, refuses to finish off the beaten lord at his employer's furious urging, and only afterward learns the scandalous truth behind the fight.

Farm girl Dolly Foster tries to choose between two suitors by discovering which one secretly leaves a flower on her windowsill each morning, but on the morning after a fatal haymaking accident she learns it was actually the nameless, unregarded farmhand Bill who had loved her silently and crawled to leave the flower with his dying strength.

themes: empire's human cost in young lives
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: A coffee-planter falls fatally ill with smallpox at sea soon after his wedding; his widow and a friend, waiting at Madeira, witness what seems to be his ghostly apparition leaping from the ocean at the very hour of his shipboard burial, an event the narrator gives both a telepathic and a coldly physical explanation.

themes: invention as both triumph and horror
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: Two inventing partners secretly test their revolutionary flying-machine motor; when Brown reveals he has patented it under his own name alone, a struggle in the darkened barn ends with Brown accidentally killing himself on his own knife, and the horrified Pericord straps the corpse into the machine and sends it flying out to sea, his sanity destroyed by the experience.

themes: a subterranean monster from a lost world
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_gall.plot: A consumptive doctor recuperating in Derbyshire investigates local rumors of a monster in the ancient Blue John cave-mine, eventually tracking and shooting a huge blind cave-bear-like creature that has been killing sheep and a local man, surviving grievously injured while the terrified villagers permanently seal the cave.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_last_of_t.plot: The Roman viceroy Pontus receives orders to withdraw all legions from Britain to defend the crumbling Empire, and when a British deputation belatedly begs to keep the legions, Rome refuses, leaving Britain to fall into slaughter and ruin.

A shattered Carthaginian galley commanded by Magro, carrying the statesman Gisco, limps toward Carthage after a naval defeat and is deliberately sunk in a death-grapple with two pursuing Roman ships within sight of the city, foreshadowing Carthage's destruction and Rome's future fall to a fog-bound island in the north.

A modern Scottish couple visiting the excavated Roman fort at Newstead are overtaken by a shared vision of a violent Roman-era night attack, in which the husband relives abducting the wife (in a former life) from a burning settlement before a Roman soldier named Marcus attacks them.

The Christian hermit Simon Melas, living in isolation beyond the Dniester, witnesses the vast horde of the Huns sweeping westward, kills a Hun scout who has murdered his Arian rival hermit, and rides through the night to warn the Roman garrison at Tyras of the coming invasion.

The Greek shepherd-poet Policles stumbles into a rigged singing contest staged for the Emperor Nero at Olympia, publicly denounces Nero's dreadful performance, and narrowly escapes execution while the court flatters Nero into believing his critic was the god Pan.

A Romano-British trader writes to his friend Crassus describing the arrival of the first Saxon ships invited by King Vortigern to help defend Britain, detailing the customs and rivalries of chiefs Kenna, Lanc, and Hasta, and closing with the ominous suggestion that the Saxons will end up owning the island.

The Christian slave Datus defaces his master's prized Greek statue of Venus as an act of religious duty; when the senator Emilius Flaccus tries clemency instead of the Emperor Domitian's cruelty, Datus destroys the statue further and is condemned to face a leopard in the arena.

A giant Thracian peasant named Theckla joins the Roman army, rises through the ranks under Severus and his successors, is proclaimed Emperor Maximinus by his mutinous legions after murdering Severus Alexander's regime, rules through brute terror, and is finally cut down by his own soldiers during the failed siege of Aquileia.

The Byzantine merchant Manuel Ducas recalls meeting a charismatic caravan leader named Mahomet in the Arabian desert, who spoke of his new faith and prophesied the eventual conquest of idolaters, Jews, and Christians alike, foreshadowing the rise of Islam and its future threat to Constantinople.

An overworked accountant, driven to nervous exhaustion by a fraud investigation, begins seeing visions in an antique silver mirror that gradually reveal themselves to be the historical murder of David Rizzio before Mary Queen of Scots at Holyrood, culminating in his collapse after witnessing the killing in full.

An old abbot secretly brings Theodora's hidden illegitimate son Leon to Constantinople to reunite him with his mother, now Empress; the scheming eunuch Basil nearly has both killed to protect her secret, but Theodora relents, spares her son and the abbot, and instead has Basil thrown to his death in the palace well.

In ancient Tyre, the Greek chief Odysseus, en route to the Trojan War, and the future Israelite king David, building Jerusalem, unknowingly cross paths at a temple, where the prophetess Alaga foretells that both men's fame will endure for three thousand years.

A Roman legate at the siege of Jerusalem writes home describing the fall of the temple, and recounts a night conversation with the centurion Longinus, who reveals he was present at the crucifixion decades before and has never forgotten Christ's eyes, hinting at his own quiet conversion to Christianity.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_lost_worl.plot: Journalist Edward Malone proposes marriage to Gladys, who refuses him but declares she could only love a man of heroic deeds and dangerous adventure, spurring Malone to resolve to find a quest worthy of her.

News editor McArdle assigns Malone to interview the notoriously violent Professor Challenger, a zoologist ridiculed for unproven South American discoveries; Malone researches Challenger with Tarp Henry's help and drafts a flattering letter to secure an interview.

Malone visits Challenger under a false pretext, is exposed as a journalist and violently thrown out after a brawl in the street, but his honest answer to an intervening policeman prompts Challenger to invite him back inside.

Challenger shows Malone a dead explorer's sketchbook, damaged photographs, and a strange bone as evidence of a South American plateau where prehistoric creatures survive, and invites him to attend a public lecture that evening.

At a chaotic public lecture Challenger disrupts Waldron's talk and challenges the audience to send representatives to verify his claims; skeptical Professor Summerlee agrees to go, and Malone and Lord John Roxton volunteer to accompany him to South America.

Malone visits Lord John Roxton's rooms, where Roxton recounts his past war against South American slave-traders, equips Malone with a rifle, and the pair prepare with Professor Summerlee to sail for the Amazon under Challenger's sealed instructions.

The expedition travels up the Amazon to Manaos, assembles its native and half-breed crew, and opens Challenger's sealed instructions to find a blank page, only for Challenger himself to arrive and take command as they prepare to vanish into unexplored territory.

The party canoes up a tributary of the Amazon toward the plateau, surviving a knife-fight between Gomez and Zambo and days of menacing war-drums from unseen Indians. Following Challenger's landmarks through a hidden green tunnel and bamboo brake, they finally sight the red cliffs of the plateau and glimpse what may be a pterodactyl.

The party finds Maple White's skeleton and chalk trail-marks, scales an isolated pinnacle, and fells a tree to bridge the chasm onto the plateau. Once across, the half-breed Gomez topples the bridge in revenge for his brother's death and is shot by Lord John, leaving the four men marooned on the plateau.

The marooned party builds a thorn-hedge stronghold called Fort Challenger, tracks and observes live iguanodons grazing, and is savagely attacked by a colony of pterodactyls at a swamp rookery. On returning to camp they find their stores ransacked by an unseen powerful creature.

Malone climbs the giant gingko tree to chart the plateau from above and comes face to face with a hidden ape-man among the branches. He completes the first map of the land and, at his companions' urging, names the central lake 'Lake Gladys' after the woman he loves.

Driven by vanity, Malone sneaks out alone at night to explore the central lake, is chased by a carnivorous dinosaur, and escapes by falling into a native trap-pit. Returning at dawn he finds the camp ransacked and his three companions vanished, with only a pool of blood left behind.

Lord John, having escaped the ape-men, reunites with Malone and recounts how Challenger and Summerlee were captured by ape-men led by a chief eerily resembling Challenger. The two men storm the ape-men's execution ground with rifles, shoot the ape-king, and rescue Summerlee, Challenger, and several Indian prisoners.

After Malone barely survives another ape-man attack, the four men ally with the rescued Accala Indians and their young chief Maretas, joining a full war party that decisively defeats and wipes out the ape-men tribe in a pitched battle at the cliff edge.

Living among the grateful but unhelpful Accala, the party survives an attack by giant toad-like monsters repelled with poisoned arrows, while Challenger constructs a hydrogen balloon from a lizard's stomach. Maretas secretly gives Malone a map to a hidden tunnel, which the four men use to descend from the plateau at last.

The four explorers present their findings to a packed, riotous meeting of the Zoological Institute in London, silencing the skeptical Dr. Illingworth by releasing a live pterodactyl that escapes through a window. Malone returns home triumphant only to find Gladys already married to another man, and the story closes with the friends sharing Lord John's diamonds over supper.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_love_affa.plot: This unit is not narrative prose but the front-matter table of contents for Volume I, listing chapter titles covering the outbreak of WWI and early campaigns (Mons, Le Cateau, the Marne, the Aisne, La Bassée-Armentières, and First Ypres). No characters appear or act in this unit; only the title page names the protagonist George Vincent Parker.

A table-of-contents style chapter listing the major 1915 engagements of the British campaign in France and Flanders, from Neuve Chapelle and Hill 60 through the gas attack at the Second Battle of Ypres to the Battle of Loos.

A table-of-contents style chapter outlining the phases of the 1916 Battle of the Somme, from the opening assaults on Gommecourt and Beaumont Hamel through the breaking of successive German lines to the Battle of the Ancre.

themes: the Battle of Cambrai and early tank warfare
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_love_affa.plot: A table-of-contents style chapter covering 1917 operations, from the German withdrawal on the Arras-Soissons front through Arras, Messines, the prolonged Third Ypres offensive, to the tank assault at Cambrai.

themes: the Second Battle of the Somme
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_love_affa.plot: A table-of-contents style chapter tracing the British retreats of spring 1918 during the German offensive, covering the Second Battle of the Somme, the Battle of the Lys, and fighting along the Chemin des Dames.

themes: advance to victory and the Armistice
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_love_affa.plot: A table-of-contents style chapter listing the closing 1918 offensives of the British armies, from the Battle of Amiens through the breaking of the Hindenburg Line to the final advances ending the war.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_man_from_.plot: Newly posted Bimbashi Hilary Joyce commands a lonely Sudanese frontier post and captures a mysterious silent Arab prisoner who later escapes; the prisoner turns out to be his own General in disguise, teaching the young officer a humbling lesson.

Reclusive scholar James Upperton, preparing to move into an isolated moorland cottage, is intrigued by the sudden, tearful arrival of a beautiful and secretive fellow lodger, Eva Cameron, at his Yorkshire boarding house.

Upperton discovers that Eva Cameron wandered the moors all night; before he departs for his lonely new cottage she extracts from him a strange, urgent promise to bolt his door at night, deepening the mystery around her.

Upperton meets a strange new neighbour calling himself the surgeon of Gaster Fell, then secretly spies on him and is horrified to witness him violently seize and imprison a frail elderly companion in a barred, isolated cottage.

After a night intruder nearly attacks him, Upperton learns via a letter from J. Cameron that the 'surgeon' is in fact a devoted son secretly caring for his insane, escaped father, resolving the story's earlier horrors as tragic family duty.

An unnamed narrator, obsessively imitating the writer George Borrow's style and habits, blunders through a Sussex village picking odd quarrels and reciting poetry to strangers, culminating in being kicked by a carter he had tried to provoke into a boxing match.

Misanthropic hermit John M'Vittie rescues Sophie Ramusine from a shipwreck along with her Russian pursuer Ourganeff; when Ourganeff finally abducts her during a storm, both are later found dead on the shore, his body still shielding hers from the sea.

Inventors Pericord and Brown secretly test a flying machine in a remote barn, but a fight over patent credit ends with Brown accidentally killed; the horrified Pericord straps the corpse to the device and launches it out to sea, and is later found insane in an asylum.

Solicitor Frank Alder helps young Felix Stanniford finally open a room sealed years earlier by his vanished banker father, discovering the father's mummified body: he had secretly killed himself there to spare his wife the shock of his financial ruin.

Emotionless physiologist Professor Ainslie Grey marries a widow, Mrs O'James, only to discover she is the presumed-dead first wife of his own star pupil O'Brien; he nobly steps aside for the reunited couple and soon dies of what is quietly termed a broken heart.

themes: the healing touch and bedside manner
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_man_from_.plot: An old-fashioned but beloved country doctor, James Winter, is contrasted with two modern young physicians in his district; when the narrator falls ill with influenza he instinctively sends for the reassuring old doctor rather than his up-to-date rival.

A squeamish first-year medical student is taken by a senior classmate to witness his first operation and faints from dread partway through the famous surgeon Archer's lecture, only to learn afterward that the operation never actually took place at all.

Young Sir Francis Norton learns from Dr Horace Selby that he has inherited a hereditary venereal taint from his dissolute grandfather and must call off his imminent wedding; unable to face the shame, he is found dead the next day in what is really a disguised suicide.

Commonplace shopkeeper Robert Johnson endures a terrifying night of waiting while his wife Lucy undergoes a dangerous childbirth attended by Doctors Miles and Pritchard, discovering unexpected depths of feeling in himself before mother and newborn son survive.

After a medical association dinner, three doctors trade dramatic and macabre stories from their careers -- madness, deformity, misdiagnosis and self-sacrifice -- while a young layman secretly transcribes their conversation for publication.

themes: irony of doctors stricken by their own specialty
courage in the face of death
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_man_from_.plot: A veteran surgeon recounts to a young listener the tragic death of a brilliant colleague, James Walker, from the very nerve disease he had studied, alongside a chaotic operating-room mishap that cost another surgeon, M'Namara, his ear.

Prejudiced country doctor James Ripley is professionally humiliated and then won over by his brilliant new rival, Dr Verrinder Smith, a woman; when he proposes marriage after she saves his life, she gently refuses, choosing her scientific career instead.

themes: building a medical practice through publicity
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_man_from_.plot: Struggling young doctor Tom Crabbe and his old friend Barton stage a fake near-drowning and dramatic electrical 'resuscitation' to get Crabbe's name into the local papers, and the elaborate hoax succeeds in launching his medical practice.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_maracot_d.plot: Narrated through letters and documents, oceanographer Dr Maracot leads Cyrus Headley and mechanic Bill Scanlan in a steel diving cage to the ocean floor near the Canaries, where a giant crustacean attacks and severs their hawser, sending them plunging toward the abyss.

themes: first contact with a lost civilization
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_maracot_d.plot: As their air runs out at the bottom of the Atlantic, the three explorers discover they have landed atop a buried ancient city; surviving Atlanteans led by Manda rescue them using breathable vitrine suits and bring them into their underwater refuge.

The castaways adjust to life among the Atlanteans, using a thought-projecting screen to explain their arrival and learn the Atlanteans' history, while a near-disastrous intrusion into the temple of Baal reveals the survivors' dark religious past.

On a guided expedition across the ocean floor the men visit a coal mine worked by enslaved fair-haired labourers and explore the ruined Atlantean capital, then witness a vivid recorded history revealing how pride and decadence brought catastrophe upon the ancient civilization.

themes: plans of escape to the surface
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_maracot_d.plot: The party discovers the wreck of their own ship the Stratford nearby with the drowned Captain Howie still at his post; after further deep-sea dangers Headley falls in love with Mona while Scanlan rigs a radio and the group plots a daring ascent using buoyant gas globes.

Amid further undersea terrors, Headley learns through an Atlantean vision that he and Mona were lovers in a past life who were killed by her father; the community's peace is then threatened when Temple priests try to sacrifice the mixed-race baby of Scanlan's friend Berbrix.

themes: triumph of good over ancient darkness
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_maracot_d.plot: Exploring a forbidden black temple, the men summon the immortal demon-sorcerer Baal-seepa, who threatens to destroy the Atlantean colony; Dr Maracot, empowered by a benevolent spirit, spiritually confronts and banishes the demon, saving the community before the castaways later ascend to the surface world.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_memoirs_o.plot: Grant Munro consults Holmes about his wife's secretive nocturnal visits to a mysterious cottage; Holmes and Watson accompany him to confront the tenant, revealing that Effie's first husband was a Black American whose daughter Lucy she had hidden from Munro out of fear of his prejudice.

Hall Pycroft is lured from a new job at Mawson's by two brothers who invent a bogus company to keep him occupied in Birmingham while an impostor takes his place at the firm to rob it; Holmes deduces the scheme from a stuffed tooth, and they find the impostor's brother has attempted suicide after the real robbery and murder at Mawson's is exposed.

Holmes recounts his first case, from his college days, in which a blackmailing former shipmate named Hudson exposes his friend's father as a former convict who had survived a mutiny aboard the convict ship Gloria Scott; a coded warning letter drives the old man to a fatal stroke.

Holmes solves the disappearance of a butler and a housemaid at Hurlstone by decoding an old family catechism, tracing the steps to a hidden cellar where he finds the ancient crown of the Stuarts and the butler's body, deducing that the jilted housemaid caused his death and hid the evidence.

While recuperating in Surrey, Holmes investigates the murder of a coachman found with a torn note in his hand, deduces from the handwriting that father and son Cunningham are responsible for a blackmail-driven murder, and stages a fake collapse to retrieve the missing scrap of evidence from their house.

Holmes investigates the mysterious death of Colonel Barclay, found locked in a room after a quarrel with his wife, and traces it to a crippled old soldier, Henry Wood, betrayed by Barclay decades earlier in India, whose sudden reappearance so shocked Barclay that he collapsed dead from apoplexy.

themes: fear of past crimes catching up
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_memoirs_o.plot: A young doctor's mysteriously wealthy benefactor Blessington is terrorized by strange 'Russian' patients and found hanged; Holmes deduces murder and reveals Blessington was really the informer Sutton from the old Worthingdon bank gang, killed in revenge by his former accomplices.

Holmes's brother Mycroft introduces the case of interpreter Melas, kidnapped twice to translate threats against a starved Greek prisoner whose sister's fortune two Englishmen are trying to seize; Holmes and Mycroft trace them to a house where the prisoner is found dead and Melas near death from charcoal fumes.

Foreign Office clerk Percy Phelps seeks Holmes's help after a secret naval treaty vanishes from his desk while he fetches coffee; Holmes deduces that Phelps's future brother-in-law Joseph Harrison stole it and, after failed attempts to retrieve it from the house, tricks Harrison into recovering it himself, restoring it to Phelps at breakfast.

Holmes reveals to Watson the existence of criminal mastermind Professor Moriarty and, after surviving several attempts on his life, flees with Watson across Europe pursued by Moriarty, culminating in their apparent mutual deaths as they grapple at the Reichenbach Falls.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_mystery_o.plot: John Fothergill West introduces himself as narrator and compiler and explains how his impoverished Sanskrit-scholar father and his sister Esther came to Wigtownshire to manage the estate of Branksome for their ailing kinsman William Farintosh.

John and Esther see lights in the long-empty Cloomber Hall and discover that General Heatherstone has leased it; the reclusive, jumpy general questions West about strangers and vagrants, and after the family's arrival a placard rejecting all visitors offends the Wests when they call to welcome them.

Gabriel Heatherstone apologizes to West for her father's rude placard, and her brother Mordaunt confides that the family lives under a constant, real but inexplicable danger tied to their father, alarming West with his own prematurely grey hair.

Esther is frightened by Cloomber Hall lit up every night; the four young people grow close, John and Gabriel become secretly engaged, and Gabriel reveals her father's terror always peaks on October 5th, until General Heatherstone catches the couple together.

General Heatherstone confronts West at gunpoint but calms down on learning of his engagement to Gabriel, obliquely warns of a danger too strange to explain, and enlists West as part of a possible defensive 'garrison' should Cloomber ever be raided.

themes: return of a figure from the past
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_mystery_o.plot: A destitute ex-soldier, Corporal Rufus Smith, invokes the name 'Ghoolab Shah' and the Tarada Pass to the general, provoking terror; Heatherstone takes him in as gardener despite Smith's menacing manner, deepening the mystery of their shared past.

Coachman Israel Stakes recounts in dialect his employment at Cloomber, the general's sleepless nightly pacing, a terrifying unexplained ringing sound he overhears while hiding, and his abrupt dismissal after Corporal Smith's arrival.

themes: Eastern occult knowledge versus Western science
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_mystery_o.plot: Dr Easterling recalls his single visit to treat General Heatherstone's fever, during which the general lectures him on odyllic force and Eastern mysticism, then reacts with horror and hears a strange ringing sound when discussing a mountain pass from his past, after which he refuses all further visits.

A letter from Mordaunt explains that he and Gabriel are voluntarily confined until October 5th, when their father's crisis of fear is expected to resolve, leaving West and his sister anxious and unable to help.

A violent storm wrecks the barque Belinda on the coast; John and local fishermen rescue the crew, but three Buddhist-priest passengers are apparently drowned, and the superstitious mate blames them for causing the storm and for the wreck occurring in the Bay of Kirkmaiden.

The morning after the wreck, West and the sailors are astonished to find Ram Singh alive and unharmed on the shore; he politely declines all offers of food, shelter, and travel, explains his ascetic Buddhist practices, and hints he is far older than he appears.

West learns the Buddhist castaways have stayed nearby and warns the general, who reacts with terrified resignation; Ram Singh then shows West two Yogis in deep trance and speaks of inescapable occult law, deepening West's foreboding before the fateful October 5th.

Mordaunt bursts in at midnight reporting that three Buddhists summoned his father and Corporal Smith away into the darkness; a farewell letter and old journal entries reveal General Heatherstone's guilt in killing the holy man Ghoolab Shah in Afghanistan decades earlier and the astral-bell curse that followed.

Heatherstone's 1841 journal recounts a successful ambush of Afridi tribesmen in the Terada Pass during which he kills the ancient holy man Ghoolab Shah, followed that night by a spectral visitation cursing him and Smith with inescapable retribution and an eerie warning bell that haunts him for forty years.

West and Mordaunt track the general and Smith with a bloodhound across the bleak Bog of Cree to the bottomless Hole of Cree, where footprints show only three of five returned, confirming the men's deaths; the story closes with marriages, family losses, and West's defense of Eastern occult science as true.

themes: prophecy of spiritual religion after war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_new_revel.plot: Conan Doyle dedicates the book to those who braved ridicule to testify to spiritualist truth and opens with a 1899 trance prophecy by medium Mrs Piper foretelling a great war followed by clearer spirit communication.

Conan Doyle narrates his own slow conversion from materialist doctor to believer in spirit communication, describing early skeptical seances, disappointing false messages, and the influence of respected scientists and General Drayson's advice that convinced him to keep investigating.

themes: testing spirit testimony against verifiable facts
reinterpreting Christ's miracles as psychic phenomena
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_new_revel.plot: Doyle argues that spirit messages should be tested against verifiable details before being trusted, and proposes that the 'New Revelation' confirms rather than destroys core Christian teaching, reinterpreting Christ's life and miracles as expressions of mediumship and psychic law.

Doyle synthesizes consistent spirit-world descriptions gathered from many independent sources - painless death, a period of rest, reunion with loved ones, graded spheres of moral progress replacing hell, and a life of interest and occupation - as evidence for a coherent afterlife.

themes: limitations and errors of spirit communication
evidential proof through automatic writing and poltergeist cases
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_new_revel.plot: Doyle examines the flaws in spirit communication - unreliable timing, difficulty transmitting names, occasional lying spirits - recounts his own prophetic dream of 'Piave,' and closes with supplementary evidence including automatic-writing testimony and the Cheriton Dugout poltergeist case.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_poison_be.plot: Malone is sent by his news editor McArdle to interview Challenger about a sensational Times letter on cosmic changes; he, Summerlee and Lord John Roxton, each mysteriously told to bring oxygen, travel down to Rotherfield bickering en route and arrive at Challenger's house.

Challenger reveals that a poisonous belt of ether is sweeping the earth causing worldwide death, recounts his own bizarre symptoms as proof, and as telegrams confirm mass death spreading from the tropics the group readies an airtight, oxygen-stocked room.

themes: debate on the continuity of life
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_poison_be.plot: Sealed in the oxygenated boudoir, the group watches the world outside die around them (the chauffeur Austin, golfers, a train wreck, burning towns) while philosophizing about death, as McArdle is heard dying mid-telephone-call to Malone.

themes: diary-keeping at the end of the world
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_poison_be.plot: Through the night the party takes notes, debates a surviving amoeba and man's place in nature, and as their last oxygen cylinder fails Challenger smashes the window to face the ether directly, only to find the poison belt has already passed.

themes: despair of being the sole survivors
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_poison_be.plot: Believing themselves the last people alive, the group motors from Rotherfield to London through streets littered with corpses, finds one elderly survivor, Mrs Burston, kept alive by her asthma oxygen, rings a church bell hoping for other survivors, and returns home disheartened.

themes: death revealed as mere suspended animation
world resuming as if nothing happened
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_poison_be.plot: The seemingly dead world suddenly wakes from what proves to have been universal catalepsy lasting twenty-eight hours, everyone resumes exactly what they were doing, and Malone realizes his eyewitness account will be the greatest newspaper scoop of all time.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_refugees/.plot: In Paris, guardsman Amory de Catinat visits his cousin Adele Catinat before returning to duty at Versailles, and they learn her merchant father has been ordered to quarter dragoons; the American frontiersman Amos Green then arrives unannounced with a pet bear and a black fox pelt gift for Adele.

The king's elaborate morning levee at Versailles is depicted in detail, culminating in Louis XIV questioning the returned governor Frontenac about the state of Canada and the Huguenot English colonies, while courtiers gossip about the king's cooling affection for Madame de Montespan in favor of Madame de Maintenon.

On guard duty, De Catinat turns away the banished Monsieur de Vivonne and then faces down the furious Madame de Montespan, who tries to force her way in to see the king; Louis eventually grants her a private audience later that afternoon.

After Mass, Louis XIV dismisses the pleas of the wronged Huguenot merchant Catinat and is pressed by his confessor and Bossuet to revoke the Edict of Nantes, while the clergy privately conspire to use Madame de Maintenon's influence toward that end.

Guardsmen abuse the old Huguenot Catinat outside the palace until De Catinat intervenes and has them arrested; Catinat then reveals that Captain Dalbert's dragoons have been terrorizing his household and threatening Adele, prompting De Catinat to rush back to Paris with him.

Amos Green dangles Captain Dalbert from a balcony to make him leave the house, but Dalbert breaks his word and a brawl erupts until the Prince of Conde arrives and orders the dragoons away, after which the household thanks Green for saving Adele and De Catinat.

Riding to Versailles, De Catinat and Amos Green compare France and America and encounter Madame de Montespan, who bitterly warns De Catinat of her continuing influence, before Nanon summons him urgently to Madame de Maintenon.

De Catinat is summoned by Madame de Maintenon, who questions him about the king's promised meeting with Madame de Montespan and, after he reveals the appointed hour, is seen secretly pushing back the clock to delay the rival's audience.

King Louis visits Madame de Maintenon, debating whether to revoke the Edict of Nantes, listens to Corneille read a comedy, then furiously rebukes Louvois for overstepping in a diplomatic matter before Madame de Montespan bursts in, furious.

Madame de Montespan furiously confronts the king over a broken promise and is banished from court, but when Louis goes to deliver the sentence in person she wins him back with tears and passion, and he rescinds the order.

Bossuet and Pere la Chaise persuade Madame de Maintenon to accept a secret marriage to the king in exchange for her support in expelling the Huguenots; that evening a repentant Louis returns and proposes marriage, which she accepts.

The king faces a wave of objections to his planned marriage from his brother, his son, Fenelon, and Louvois; afterward la Chaise and Bossuet, fearing his resolve is weakening, urge Madame de Maintenon to feign resignation from court to force his hand.

When Madame de Maintenon threatens to leave court, the king impulsively decides to marry her that very night in secret, and dispatches De Catinat and his American friend Amos Green to summon the Archbishop of Paris to Versailles by midnight.

Madame de Montespan learns from her brother de Vivonne of the king's secret marriage plan and gives him her jewels and gold to intercept and delay the royal messengers, imprisoning them at her estranged husband's castle; he sends word that the Archbishop will not arrive that night.

Riding to Paris to fetch the Archbishop, De Catinat and Amos Green discover their tack has been sabotaged, quarrel over whether to take a safer route, and are thrown from their horses when they hit a hidden trip-cord strung across the road.

De Vivonne's ruffians capture the injured De Catinat while Amos Green, feigning death, secretly escapes; Amos Green later reappears disguised as the bloodied coachman driving the runaway carriage into the Seine to free De Catinat, and is seized by the pursuers.

De Catinat and Amos Green, having been recaptured and imprisoned in the dungeon of the Castle of Portillac by an unknown lord's men, learn that Amos secretly relayed the king's message to the archbishop, who has already reached Versailles to perform the royal wedding.

Working through the night, Amos Green loosens the bars of their cell window; after a jailer spies them and a castle alarm sounds, the two prisoners watch a scaffold built beneath their window and see Francoise de Montespan led out to be executed.

The king reads a bag of intercepted private letters that expose the true, often mocking opinions of his courtiers and family, then, reassured by Madame de Maintenon's loyal letter, secretly marries her that night before a small group of witnesses.

Louis tells Madame de Montespan she must leave court permanently; enraged and desperate, she nearly stabs her own son until Madame de Maintenon disarms her, and Montespan then learns that her rival has secretly become the king's wife.

Fleeing the palace at night, Montespan is abducted by her estranged and vengeful husband Maurice, who beats her in the carriage and reveals he means to try and execute her at his castle of Portillac under his feudal right of high justice.

De Catinat and Amos Green burst from their dungeon window to halt Montespan's execution, kill the headsman and hold off her husband until Major de Brissac arrives with royal cavalry to rescue the lady and arrest the seigneur.

themes: revocation of the Edict of Nantes
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_refugees/.plot: Pressured by his confessors and wife, Louis signs the revocation of the Edict of Nantes; when De Catinat refuses to abjure his Huguenot faith he is stripped of his commission, and he rushes home to gather his uncle and Adele and flee France aboard Ephraim Savage's ship.

The refugees sail down the Seine aboard Captain Ephraim Savage's brigantine Golden Rod and are chased off Honfleur by a royal guard-boat seeking the fleeing Huguenots, which Savage outwits and beats off before escaping into open sea.

The Golden Rod finds a drifting boat with a dead family and a dying Huguenot pastor from Isigny; before he dies, he marries De Catinat and Adele on deck, while two captured Frenchmen are set free in the recovered boat.
The Golden Rod strikes an iceberg in fog and sinks; Captain Ephraim Savage refuses to abandon ship but survives, and the castaways find him waiting in an ice cave when they row back to the berg.

As the iceberg begins to split apart beneath them, the castaways climb to its summit and spot a French warship, the St. Christophe, below; they are rescued and taken aboard, bound for Canada with the new governor-general.

The ship reaches Quebec; old Catinat, having glimpsed the promised land, dies on deck after a Franciscan friar exposes the family's Huguenot faith, and De Catinat learns he and Adele are to be shipped back to France while the Americans sail home free.

themes: canoe flight up the St. Lawrence
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_refugees/.plot: Amos and Ephraim (disguised as a friar) return by night to smuggle De Catinat and Adele off the prison ship at Quebec, and the party paddles upriver by canoe, encountering Indian warnings of a coming Iroquois war and abandoning a captured hostile friar on an island.

The party paddles up the St. Lawrence toward the Richelieu River seeking safety with De Catinat's friend the seigneur of Sainte Marie, but spotting the vengeful friar pursuing them by canoe, they abandon the river route and strike overland through the forest.

Trekking through the forest toward the Richelieu, the party meets the mutilated Jesuit missionary Father Ignatius Morat, horribly tortured by the Iroquois yet cheerfully returning to his mission, who blesses them before they part.

themes: feudal seigneury in the New World
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_refugees/.plot: The refugees reach the Richelieu and are welcomed at the seigneury of Sainte Marie, meeting the famous frontiersman Du Lhut and the flamboyant old seigneur, who receives feudal tribute from his tenants and hosts the party for the night.

Leaving Adele safe at Sainte Marie under Onega's protection, De Catinat, Amos, Ephraim and Du Lhut set out through the woods toward the Poitou blockhouse, are stalked by two Iroquois scouts, and Du Lhut kills the Mohawk war chief Brown Moose in an ambush.

The four men find the Poitou blockhouse garrison slaughtered and tortured, learn a huge Iroquois war party is closing on Sainte Marie, and race back through the night, setting the dry forest on fire behind enemy warriors before reaching Sainte Marie's lights.

themes: class and courtly manners amid danger
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_refugees/.plot: De Catinat reunites with Adele at the Sainte Marie stockade just as word arrives of an approaching Iroquois war party, and Amos Green sets a hidden powder trap outside the walls as the garrison braces for the first shots of the attack.

The Iroquois launch a massed assault on the stockade, killing Onega's son; Amos Green detonates his hidden powder cache to shatter a lurking war party, but a renewed rush finally breaches the palisade and drives the survivors back into the manor house.

As the house is besieged, the women and children flee by canoe under cover of darkness while a Franciscan friar hunting De Catinat as a heretic arrives and destroys the last boat; Iroquois canoes give chase and one is sunk by cannon fire before warriors storm the house.

The last defenders make a stand on the stone staircase, repelling a rush of Iroquois warriors with concentrated fire, then endure a night of drunken revelry and the torture-death of a captured comrade before spotting an Iroquois canoe at dawn carrying Onega and Adele as prisoners.

De Catinat dives into the river to reach his wife's captor canoe and is himself taken prisoner, but the Iroquois abruptly withdraw as a relief flotilla led by Chambly arrives, and the survivors set off at once in pursuit of the captives.

themes: aftermath and dispersion of the Huguenots
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_refugees/.plot: The Iroquois march their captives to a war camp where Onega and De Catinat are condemned to the stake and Adele to forced marriage, but Ephraim Savage's rescue party storms the camp just in time, killing the Flemish Bastard and freeing the prisoners as the novel closes on the refugees' later peaceful life in America.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: Holmes reveals to Watson that he faked his death at Reichenbach Falls to escape Moriarty's surviving allies, then uses a wax dummy of himself as bait in an empty house to trap Colonel Moran, the gang's chief assassin, who murdered Ronald Adair with an air-gun.

Solicitor John McFarlane is accused of murdering builder Jonas Oldacre, who had suddenly named him heir, but Holmes proves Oldacre faked his own death and hid in his house to frame the young man out of an old grudge against his mother.

themes: American criminal past intruding on English life
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: Holmes decodes a mysterious cipher of stick-figure 'dancing men' used by Elsie Cubitt's former criminal suitor Abe Slaney to threaten her, but arrives in Norfolk too late to prevent a shootout that kills her husband Hilton Cubitt and leaves her gravely wounded.

Holmes investigates a bearded cyclist secretly shadowing music teacher Violet Smith and uncovers a plot by fortune-hunters to force her into marriage for her inherited wealth, arriving just after a defrocked clergyman marries her to the brutal Woodley before Carruthers shoots him to stop the sham union.

themes: deduction from tracks and bicycle tires
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: Holmes and Watson investigate the disappearance of the Duke of Holdernesse's schoolboy son and a missing German master, tracing bicycle tracks across a moor to find the master murdered; Holmes uncovers that the Duke's illegitimate son James Wilder engineered the kidnapping with the innkeeper Reuben Hayes, who committed the murder, and forces the Duke to pay the promised reward and reform his household.

A brutal retired sea captain, Black Peter Carey, is found harpooned to death in his cabin; while Inspector Hopkins arrests a young man, Neligan, connected to stolen securities, Holmes deduces the true killer must be a powerful seaman and traps the real murderer, harpooner Patrick Cairns, who confesses to killing Carey in self-defense over a blackmail dispute tied to an old shipboard murder.

themes: blackmail and moral versus legal justice
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: Holmes tries to negotiate with the notorious blackmailer Milverton to recover compromising letters for a client, then burgles his house at night to destroy his blackmail archive, but witnesses another of Milverton's victims shoot him dead; Holmes and Watson escape and later refuse to help Lestrade investigate the murder.

A series of smashed plaster busts of Napoleon and a related murder puzzle Lestrade, but Holmes deduces that a fugitive Italian sculptor, Beppo, is searching the busts for the stolen Borgia pearl he hid in wet plaster before his arrest, and Holmes captures him and recovers the pearl by breaking the last bust himself.

themes: class loyalty of an old servant
deduction from height and physical clues
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: A university tutor discovers that the proofs of a scholarship examination have been secretly copied, and Holmes deduces from a scratch, pencil shavings, and clay from a jumping-pit that the tall athlete Gilchrist is the culprit, shielded afterward by his family's old servant Bannister, leading Gilchrist to withdraw from the exam in disgrace rather than face scandal.

Holmes investigates the murder of a professor's secretary, deducing from a pair of pince-nez that a short-sighted woman intruder killed him accidentally while searching for documents, and discovers she is the professor's estranged Nihilist wife hidden in his study, seeking papers to free an innocent man from Siberian exile; she dies of poison after handing over the packet.

themes: disappearance on the eve of a sporting match
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: Holmes is asked to find a champion rugby player who vanished before an important match, and after tracking a secretive doctor's carriage with a scent hound, discovers that the missing man had secretly married a dying woman and was at her deathbed, hiding the marriage from his miserly uncle.

themes: deduction from wine glasses and a frayed rope
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: A brutal baronet is found murdered and his wife claims burglars did it, but Holmes deduces from inconsistent wineglass evidence and rope-cutting marks that the story is fabricated, tracking down the wife's sailor lover Jack Crocker, who killed the husband in her defense, and Holmes lets him go free after a mock trial.

themes: international politics and the threat of war
murder by a jealous foreign wife
diplomatic discretion and covering up scandal
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_return_of.plot: A vital secret state letter vanishes from a minister's despatch-box, and Holmes links its disappearance to the murder of spy Eduardo Lucas, ultimately discovering that the minister's wife had stolen the document to buy back an old indiscreet letter from Lucas, whose jealous wife then killed him; Holmes recovers the letter from its hiding place and secretly returns it to avert a European war.

themes: cocaine use and craving for mental stimulation
the science of observation and deduction
demonstration of deductive method on Watson's watch
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_sign_of_t.plot: Holmes injects cocaine out of boredom and lectures Watson on the exact science of deduction, demonstrating his method by reading Watson's late brother's history from his watch, until their idle afternoon is interrupted by the arrival of a new client, Miss Mary Morstan.

Mary Morstan tells Holmes and Watson of her father's unexplained disappearance a decade earlier and the yearly gift of pearls that followed, then shows them a letter summoning her to a secret meeting; Holmes agrees to accompany her that evening.
Holmes deduces a link between Major Sholto's death and the pearl gifts, then he, Watson and Mary ride through fog to the Lyceum Theatre and are driven by a strange coachman to Pondicherry Lodge.

Thaddeus Sholto welcomes the group to his ornate rooms and recounts his father's deathbed confession about the hidden Agra treasure and a menacing bearded intruder, revealing that the treasure has now been found.
The party reaches Pondicherry Lodge to find Bartholomew Sholto murdered in a bolted room with a poisoned thorn wound and the treasure gone, while Watson and Mary comfort each other amid the horror.
Holmes examines tracks and the roof entry to deduce a wooden-legged man and a tiny barefoot accomplice, while the pompous Inspector Athelney Jones arrives and wrongly arrests Thaddeus Sholto.
Watson escorts Mary home and fetches the tracker dog Toby from old Sherman; he and Holmes follow the creosote scent across London only to be led comically to a creosote barrel in a timber-yard.

Holmes and Watson trace the true scent to Mordecai Smith's boatyard, learn the launch Aurora and its owner have vanished, and Holmes sends the Baker Street Irregulars to scour the river while theorizing about a small Andaman Islander accomplice.

Days pass without word of the Aurora; Holmes disguises himself as an old sailor to investigate personally, then startles Watson and the humbled Athelney Jones by revealing his disguise back at Baker Street.

Holmes, Watson and Jones chase the Aurora down the Thames in a police launch, shoot the Andaman Islander Tonga as he readies his blowpipe, and capture Jonathan Small after his escape bogs down in marsh mud.

The captured Small insists he did not kill Bartholomew Sholto; Watson brings the treasure chest to Mary only to find it empty, and, freed from the barrier her wealth would have posed, he declares his love and she accepts him.

Small narrates his full history — his maiming, the Mutiny, the murder of the merchant Achmet, his imprisonment, and Sholto's betrayal of their oath — explaining decades of pursuit for the Agra treasure, while Watson confirms his engagement to Mary.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_tragedy_o.plot: The passengers of the steamer Korosko are introduced as they travel the Nile toward the Egyptian frontier, the chapter closing on an unsettling jackal's cry and Miss Adams's foreboding before their planned desert excursion.

On deck that night Cochrane, Brown and Headingly argue over the burdens and merits of British rule in Egypt and the danger from the Dervishes, before the party retires as the desert lies silent around Wady Haifa.
The party rides donkeys under armed escort to the temple ruins and pulpit rock of Abousir, admiring the desert view until a line of camel-riding raiders is spotted emerging from the hills.

Dervish raiders under Ali Wad Ibrahim overrun the tourist party at Abousir Rock, killing donkey-boys and soldiers, wounding several travelers, and taking the survivors captive after the cowardly dragoman Mansoor betrays the hidden women.
The captives are marched across the desert by camel under brutal conditions; Cecil Brown is fatally knifed resisting a search of his clothes, and the group clings to hope of pursuit as night falls.

The captives learn the Korosko itself was seized and Mrs Belmont is brought among them; the fierce Emir Abderrahman assumes command and, after a punishing night march, gives the prisoners an ultimatum to embrace Islam or be killed.
Marching along an ancient caravan route littered with animal bones, the resigned captives discuss mortality and enlist Fardet to delay the coming religious inquisition while praying for rescue.

A rescue plot by loyal Egyptian soldiers collapses because the women cannot be saved too; Fardet stalls the one-eyed Moolah's conversion test with conjuring tricks, and when it fails the four men draw lots for one spare camel before being sentenced to death.

Stephens confesses his love to Sadie as the men await execution; the women are led away with Cochrane, gunfire signals an ambush of the raiders, and the Egyptian Camel Corps, aided by the reappeared Mr Stuart, destroys the Dervish band.

The rescued group watches the Egyptian Camel Corps annihilate the remaining raiders, is joyously reunited with Belmont, Fardet and Stephens who were saved by loyal soldiers, and later reflects aboard the returning steamer on what their ordeal has taught them.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_valley_of.plot: Holmes and Watson decode a coded warning from Moriarty's informant Porlock about danger threatening a man named Douglas at Birlstone, just as Inspector MacDonald arrives to report that Douglas has already been murdered.

themes: mutual respect between amateur and police
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_valley_of.plot: Holmes lectures MacDonald on Professor Moriarty's concealed wealth and criminal organization as proof he lies behind the Birlstone murder, and the three set off by train for Sussex with only sparse facts about the case.

A background narrative reveals John Douglas shot dead in his study at moated Birlstone Manor, with a bloodstained open window, a mysterious card marked V.V. 341, and his wedding ring missing, baffling the local sergeant and household.

Holmes, Watson, MacDonald and local detective White Mason examine the Birlstone crime scene together, debating whether the killer came from inside or outside the house, and uncover an American-made shotgun, a missing dumb-bell, and an abandoned bicycle.

The detectives interview the butler Ames, housekeeper Mrs Allen, Cecil Barker and the strangely composed Mrs Douglas, and Holmes discovers Barker's bloodstained slippers exactly match the mark left on the windowsill, implying fabricated evidence.

Watson catches Barker and Mrs Douglas laughing together in the garden, deepening suspicion, while Holmes lays out his theory that the couple is lying to shield an outside avenger and plans a solitary night vigil in the study centered on the missing dumb-bell.

Holmes engineers a trap by announcing the moat will be drained, catches Barker retrieving a weighted bundle of clothes and a knife from the water, and reveals that John Douglas is alive in hiding, having swapped identities with the American assassin he killed in self-defense.
