Twenty years earlier, young Irishman Jack McMurdo travels by train into the Vermissa Valley coalfields, reveals himself as a Freeman lodge member and a fugitive from Chicago, and defiantly clashes with two policemen before reaching his lodgings.

McMurdo courts Ettie Shafter despite her father's warning that the Freemen are really the murderous Scowrers, clashes violently with rival suitor Ted Baldwin, and wins over the fearsome Bodymaster Boss McGinty by proving his criminal credentials, joining the Vermissa lodge.

themes: brutal punishment of a critical press
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_valley_of.plot: McMurdo undergoes a brutal branding initiation into the Scowrers' lodge at Vermissa, then joins the gang that night in a savage beating of newspaper editor James Stanger, though he restrains Baldwin from killing the man outright.

Morris secretly confesses his horror and guilt over the Scowrers to McMurdo on Miller Hill; McGinty later grills McMurdo about the meeting, and when police arrest McMurdo for the Stanger assault, McGinty's false alibi gets him acquitted in court.

McMurdo promises Ettie he will leave the lodge within a year as hired gunmen murder mine manager Dunn and engineer Menzies at Crow Hill; McGinty then orders McMurdo to kill foreman Chester Wilcox, whose empty house he dynamites after Wilcox has already fled.

Morris shows McMurdo a letter warning that Pinkerton detective Birdy Edwards is investigating the lodge; McMurdo claims to know the man and persuades the lodge to let him lure Edwards to his house for a killing, while also preparing an escape plan with Ettie.

McMurdo reveals himself as Pinkerton detective Birdy Edwards and armed police storm the ambush, capturing the lodge leaders who are later hanged or imprisoned; an epilogue shows Douglas (Edwards) apparently lost at sea, with Holmes suspecting Moriarty orchestrated the murder.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_vital_mes.plot: Conan Doyle argues WWI was a divine shock meant to force religious renewal, calling for two reforms: discarding the vengeful Old Testament and refocusing Christianity on Christ's life rather than his death, as prelude to a new spiritual revelation.

Conan Doyle traces Spiritualism from the 1848 Hydesville rappings through pioneering mediums like D. D. Home, and scientific endorsements by Crookes, Hare and others, arguing physical and photographic evidence proves genuine spirit communication despite fraud and ridicule.

Conan Doyle lays out the theory of a spiritual duplicate body that separates from the physical at death, citing Crookes' materialisation of Katie King, mediums' test messages, and books like Lodge's Raymond as proof, then describes conditions of the afterlife and the mechanics of mediumship (ectoplasm, direct voice, spirit photography).

themes: moral development and punishment after death
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_vital_mes.plot: Using a verified direct-voice test message received by Ernest Oaten as proof of authenticity, Conan Doyle describes the coming world as a happy, graded continuation of earthly life with restored bodies, arguing sin is punished only by a temporary 'borderland' of development rather than eternal hell.

themes: parallels between early Christianity and modern spiritualism
psychic gifts of Christ and the Apostles
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_vital_mes.plot: Conan Doyle argues Pentecost and Christ's miracles were essentially psychic phenomena analogous to modern mediumship, appends evidential appendices (Geley's ectoplasm experiments, Margaret Cameron's cross-corroborated automatic writing, Crewe spirit photographs), and calls on the churches to embrace this new revelation or continue to decline.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_wandering.plot: Conan Doyle recounts the Merthyr seance that inspired his mission, his British lecture tours, and a London farewell luncheon where most of the 290 guests stood to testify to personal contact with the dead. After a discussion at Exeter on spiritualism's relation to Christianity, he sets sail with his family for Australia aboard the "Naldera" on 13 August 1920.

The ship voyage carries Doyle from Gibraltar through the Mediterranean, Suez Canal, Aden, Bombay and Ceylon to Western Australia, mixing war memories with shipboard lectures on spiritualism, a mango-trick conjuring demonstration in Colombo, and the family's arrival and welcome at Fremantle and Perth.

Doyle arrives in Adelaide, welcomed by Premier Hughes and challenged to public debates, and delivers well-attended lectures including a photograph exhibition marked by an unexplained "spot light" phenomenon. He tours drought-stricken vineyards and the bush, visiting naturalist T. P. Bellchambers, before departing for Melbourne.

In Melbourne Doyle faces a hostile press campaign led by the Argus but draws large lecture audiences; he investigates the controversial apport medium Charles Bailey over two sittings, meets Prime Minister Hughes and the Federal Government, attends Lord Forster's vice-regal arrival, and reflects on Australian drink and horse-racing.

Doyle spends a day in the Dandenong bush with Henry Stead, retells the documented 1883 case of the drowned Browne brothers whose spirits communicated through medium George Spriggs, lectures in Geelong and Bendigo (descending a gold mine), and visits the Wynnes' Nerrin-Nerrin sheep station in western Victoria.

Doyle investigates the clairvoyant healer M. J. Bloomfield's diagnostic powers, attends a Rescue Circle session under Mr. Tozer, sits with American voice-medium Mrs. Susanna Harris who produces evidential spirit voices, enjoys Melbourne's gardens and cricket, and delivers his final large Melbourne lecture defending himself against the Argus's hostility.

Doyle receives an enormous welcome in Sydney, lectures to record crowds, proposes an unaccepted formal test-case challenge to skeptics, surf-bathes at Manly, meets literary and occult figures including poet Leon Gellert, artist Norman Lindsay and Theosophist Bishop Leadbeater, and reflects at length on Madame Blavatsky's Theosophy and the disputed character of medium D. D. Home.

Doyle sails to New Zealand through dangerous fog off Auckland, fends off a photographers' challenge to his psychic photographs, is warmly received in Auckland by clergyman Jasper Calder, discusses Pacific winds and Atlantis with eccentric meteorologist Clement Wragge, then travels to windy Wellington, examines rare books, and recounts an old Maori seance as corroborating spirit communication.

Doyle tours the South Island, engaging in a newspaper controversy with Christchurch clergy, investigating a psychic dog and Maori-language origins, visiting Sir Joseph Kinsey (patron of Scott and Shackleton), and receiving strong evidential sittings with clairvoyant Mrs. Roberts in Dunedin before battling a shipping strike to leave New Zealand.

Returning from New Zealand, Doyle learns of his mother's death, then journeys to Brisbane where he is warmly received despite vituperative clerical opposition, lays the foundation stone of a Spiritualist church, discusses Queensland's loan "repudiation" controversy with Sir Matthew Nathan, and encounters an inexplicably fogged official photograph of himself.

After visiting the Jenolan Caves and a giant fossil skeleton, Doyle tests medium Mrs. Foster Turner's psychometry and her famous 1914 war prophecy, holds a third inconclusive sitting with apport medium Charles Bailey, tallies his tour's financial and attendance success, and gives a final lecture in Perth before leaving Australia on the Naldera.

Sailing home via Ceylon (visiting Kandy and its Buddhist shrine) and Bombay (Elephanta caves), Doyle reflects on the Battle of Jutland while passing HMS Malaya, hears Lady Dyer's cross-medium spirit-communication case, and learns from Lord Chetwynd about the munitions work that nearly bombed Berlin, before reaching Marseilles.

In Paris Doyle visits Dr. Geley's Institut Metaphysique, examines paraffin-mould hand casts from medium Franek Kluski's materialisations and sits with the medium Eva under Madame Bisson, tours the ravaged Aisne battlefields with his family, attends his brother-in-law E. W. Hornung's funeral, and concludes his journey home to London convinced of divine guidance throughout the mission.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_war_in_so.plot: In a preface dated January 1902 at Undershaw, Conan Doyle explains why he wrote the book to lay Britain's case for the war before the world, and appeals for funds to translate and distribute it internationally.

Traces Boer history from the 1652 Dutch settlement at the Cape through the Great Trek and founding of the Transvaal and Orange Free State, the 1877 British annexation of the Transvaal, and the First Boer War culminating in the 1881 defeat at Majuba Hill and the resulting Pretoria Convention.

Describes the 1886 discovery of Rand gold and the resulting Uitlander grievances over taxation, disenfranchisement and corruption, the failed Jameson Raid of December 1895 and its aftermath, and the 1899 Uitlander petition to Queen Victoria for protection.

Covers the Bloemfontein Conference between Milner and Kruger over the Uitlander franchise, the breakdown of negotiations amid mutual arming, and the Transvaal's October 1899 ultimatum which Britain rejected, precipitating war.

Conan Doyle rebuts common accusations against Britain (Chamberlain's complicity in the raid, a capitalists' war, designs on the gold mines, monarchy vs. republic, refusal of arbitration, revenge for Majuba), citing testimony including Paul Botha's to argue the Boers had long planned aggression against British rule.

Recounts two rounds of peace negotiations: the March 1900 Kruger-Salisbury exchange rejecting Boer demands for independence, and the 1901 Kitchener-Botha talks at Middelburg where generous British terms were ultimately refused, while Boers such as Piet de Wet broke away to fight for the British.

themes: laws of war and the Hague Conventions
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_war_in_so.plot: Examines the escalating British policy of burning Boer farms in retaliation for sniping and railway sabotage, quoting the Roberts-Botha-De Wet correspondence, and argues the practice was a legally and militarily justified response to guerrilla tactics while acknowledging cases of excess.

Doyle defends the British-run Boer refugee camps against accusations of cruelty from Emily Hobhouse and W. T. Stead, citing testimony from soldiers, clergy and camp officials that conditions were as good as circumstances allowed, and argues the high child death toll came chiefly from a measles epidemic worsened by Boer mothers' resistance to medical care.

Doyle assembles testimony from foreign military attachés, correspondents, Boer women and clergy to refute claims that British troops committed outrages against women, and traces and debunks specific fabricated stories, including the 'Eloff myth' and a Dutch minister's slander, circulated in the continental press.

Doyle rebuts Stead's claims about expansive bullets used at Mafeking, defends British treatment of Boer prisoners of war with statistics and testimony, lists the small number of wartime executions and their causes, and justifies the placing of hostages on trains to stop derailing attacks.

themes: Boer misuse of the white flag
murder of black African scouts and servants
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_war_in_so.plot: Doyle documents Boer abuse of the white flag and disguise in khaki uniforms, then catalogues numerous documented murders of unarmed black Africans and of surrendered or wounded British soldiers by Boer commandos, including the killing of Lieutenant Neumeyer and the coloured blacksmith Abraham Esau.

Doyle answers the war critic Methuen's peace arguments, insists the war must be fought to a decisive finish, proposes a voluntary Boer reservation in the northern Transvaal, and closes with bitter reflections on Germany's hostile wartime press compared with the more sympathetic France and Russia.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: At Beaulieu Abbey the fierce novice John of Hordle is tried before Abbot Berghersh for drunkenness, striking a fellow monk, and flirting with a girl; sentenced to be whipped and expelled, he threatens the assembled monks with a prie-dieu and flees the abbey grounds.

Alleyne Edricson, raised at Beaulieu Abbey, is sent out into the world under his late father's bequest to spend a year outside the cloister before choosing between monastic and secular life; the Abbot blesses him and he sets off for his estranged brother's house at Minstead.

themes: first taste of the secular world
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: On the road Alleyne meets Peter the fuller of Lymington, who has been swindled out of his clothes by Hordle John under pretense of a monastic indulgence; Alleyne fetches replacement garments for Peter, but John reappears and steals those too, leaving the fuller comically stripped again.

themes: rough medieval justice and summary execution
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Alleyne helps an old woman cross a stream and then fights off two robbers who attack her; the bailiff of Southampton and his archers arrive, shoot the black robber dead and behead the other after a summary 'trial,' leaving Alleyne shaken by the brutality of the law.

themes: moral seriousness clashing with coarse humor
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: At the Pied Merlin inn Alleyne rejoins Hordle John among a motley crowd of laborers, foresters and travelers whose talk turns to peasant grievances against nobles and clergy; Alleyne's objection to the gleeman's bawdy song nearly sparks a brawl, interrupted by a dramatic new arrival.

themes: recruitment for the war in France
the glamor of the free companies
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: The boastful archer Samkin Aylward, freshly returned from France laden with plunder, wagers his prized feather-bed that he can wrestle Hordle John; John throws him unexpectedly, and Aylward, delighted rather than dismayed, recruits the giant into the White Company.

themes: worldly soldier's creed versus religious devotion
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Traveling together, Aylward reads a French letter for his illiterate comrades, the three encounter self-flagellating pilgrim friars whose penance disturbs Alleyne, and Aylward's irreverent tales of papal indulgences and battle spark good-natured debate about religion and war.

themes: national rivalries between English, French, Scots, Spanish and Flemish
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: The trio meet a border archer mutilated by the Scots who is training his young sons for future revenge; Aylward demonstrates his marksmanship and compares the fighting qualities of various nations before Alleyne parts from his friends to seek out his brother.

themes: first meeting of hero and heroine
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Alleyne encounters a vengeful outlawed serf and witnesses King Edward's hunting party, then finds his own brother, the Socman of Minstead, forcing himself on the noblewoman Maude Loring; Alleyne intervenes, drives his brother off, and escorts Maude to safety, the two parting with mutual admiration.

themes: introduction of the diminutive but formidable knight Sir Nigel
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Alleyne rejoins Aylward and John on the road to Christchurch, meets two bickering scholar-philosophers, and the three arrive at Twynham Castle, where the mild-mannered Sir Nigel Loring wins John's respect by casually testing the men's strength and then fearlessly facing down a runaway bear.

Inside Twynham Castle, Aylward and his old comrade Black Simon nearly duel over a years-old quarrel until Alleyne and John intervene; Alleyne is then reunited with Lady Maude in the great hall, and Sir Nigel and Lady Loring persuade him to become Sir Nigel's squire and Maude's tutor.

themes: tension between cloistered ideals and worldly desire
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Over weeks of preparation for war, Alleyne tutors the willful Lady Maude and finds himself falling in love with her despite his humble station, while fellow squire Peter Terlake confesses his own hopeless love for Maude, deepening Alleyne's private turmoil.

As the Company musters to depart Twynham Castle, Alleyne confesses his love to Maude, who gives him hope but no promise along with her green veil as a token, while Sir Nigel makes his own formal chivalric farewell to Lady Loring before leading the archers out toward France.

themes: comic mismatch between ideal and reality
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: On the road south, Sir Nigel repeatedly seeks knightly encounters in trivial situations, the party passes a grim display of a poacher's severed limbs and a blind beggar, endures Hordle John's mother scolding her son before he departs for France, and meets a sanctuary-seeking murderer being tracked by an avenger.

themes: contrast between knightly idealism and shipman's realism
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: The Company boards the merchant cog at Lepe and learns that two pirate galleys under the raiders Tête-noire and Spade-beard are terrorizing the coast; Sir Nigel resolves to fight them despite the shipmaster's misgivings, and battle stations are arranged as the ship sails toward Freshwater Bay.

The Yellow Cog lures the two pirate galleys into close action; English archers and boarders defeat the rovers in fierce hand-to-hand fighting, Hordle John disarms the pirate chief and Sir Nigel kills the Genoese leader, though Terlake is swept away aboard the escaping galley and the captured pirate chief drowns himself rather than hang.

The storm-damaged Yellow Cog nearly wrecks on rocks off the French coast; through Hawtayne's seamanship and the knights' steadfast calm amid the peril, the ship narrowly escapes the reef and safely crosses the dangerous bar into the Gironde estuary.

The company disembarks at Bordeaux, where Sir Nigel dons an eye patch as a chivalric vow to achieve some deed of arms in Spain; they pass through the bustling city to the prince's court, where the herald Pakington vets newcomers and the beloved veteran Sir John Chandos warmly welcomes Nigel and Oliver.

At the prince's court in Bordeaux, Edward rebukes a Navarrese envoy over blocked mountain passes, accepts Sir Nigel's and Sir Oliver's forces amid laughter over the 'White Company's' reputation, grants Don Pedro funds toward his restoration to the Castilian throne, and narrowly defuses a quarrel between English and Gascon lords.

themes: integration into a new social world
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Bullied and struck by the swaggering squire John Tranter, Alleyne duels him with swords, breaks his own blade but presses on until Tranter falls into the Garonne; Alleyne then dives in to save his drowning rival, earning grudging respect and acceptance among the squires of Bordeaux.

Walking through Bordeaux at night, Alleyne and Ford rescue the Italian glass-painter Agostino Pisano and his daughter Tita from harassment by drunken English archers; the grateful artist shows them his stained-glass masterpieces and praises Alleyne's own sketching talent, contrasting art's nobility with war's destructiveness.

themes: tales of plunder from the Poitiers campaign
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: At the archers' tavern the company celebrates news of an upcoming tournament; Aylward regales the men with tales of looting during the Poitiers campaign and his prized feather-bed, and Hordle John sings a ballad before the night ends in rousing toasts to the White Company.

Five English champions joust against five Gascon and continental knights before the prince's court; amid Don Pedro's cynicism and the prince's grandiose talk of conquering Jerusalem, Sir Nigel dramatically defeats a formidable German knight of the Teutonic Order, tipping the contest toward the English side.

An unnamed knight of France arrives at the last moment and defeats four English champions before Sir Nigel wounds and fights him to a draw with swords; the anonymous Frenchman bitterly rebukes the prince for the devastation of France before riding away, refusing all hospitality and reward.

themes: letter-writing and domestic devotion amid war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: Sir Nigel dictates an affectionate, muddled letter to Lady Loring which Alleyne helps compose; he advises Alleyne on pursuing a love above his station, and Sir Oliver arrives fuming over a perceived slight from the prince before the company sets off to gather the scattered White Company at Montauban.

Riding south from Bordeaux to rejoin the Company, Alleyne, Aylward and John pass through the Gascon countryside swapping stories, then are duped by a blind palmer who sells them fake holy relics (a nail, stones, wood) for twelve florins, only to learn from a blacksmith that the 'relics' are stolen junk and the pilgrim a sighted fraud who escapes into the woods.

themes: clash of merchant and knightly values
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: On the road to Cahors the party is joined by the blunt Norwich cloth-merchant David Micheldene, who they escort safely past the territory of the robber-knight Roger Club-foot, whom they find already hanged by the Seneschal's men; a pardoner selling indulgences over the corpse is then chased off after a furious quarrel with the outspoken, Wycliffe-sympathizing Micheldene.

Crossing into the ravaged borderlands of France, the company reaches a wayside inn where Sir Nigel unexpectedly encounters and befriends his famous adversary Bertrand du Guesclin and his wife Tiphaine, while Aylward and John comically string up a boastful local champion on a meat-hook before the whole party rides on together to the castle of Villefranche.

themes: cruelty of feudal lords to peasants
clash of chivalric and clerical values
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: At a feast in the castle of Villefranche, the harsh seneschal boasts of his oppression of the peasantry until the priest rebukes him; Lady Tiphaine then falls into a prophetic trance, foretelling French victory in Spain, the eventual loss of English France, the future greatness of Britain overseas, and unspecified danger closing in on the company that very night.

Alleyne sees masked men creeping through the woods at night and Ford has a ghostly vision of his sweetheart; that night the oppressed peasants ('Jacks') storm the castle of Villefranche, murder the seneschal and Ford, and the surviving knights and archers must fight for their lives amid the massacre.

Du Guesclin, Sir Nigel, Tiphaine and a handful of companions fight their way into the burning keep of Villefranche, hold off thousands of rebel peasants, blast a crowd of attackers with an improvised bombard, and are finally rescued by the returning archers of the White Company who lower a rope down the tower.

After parting from Du Guesclin, Sir Nigel takes formal command of the White Company at their forest camp, facing down the Gascon captain Sir Claude Latour who wants the men to stay and plunder Auvergne; most archers rally to Sir Nigel's call to march to the Prince's aid in Spain, while a small disloyal faction departs with Latour.

The Black Prince's vast Anglo-Gascon army crosses the Pyrenees through the pass of Roncesvalles into Navarre over several days, with Sir Nigel's Company in the vanguard, as Alleyne and Aylward watch the great columns of English and French chivalry file past toward the coming war against Castile.

Camped near Pampeluna, the English archers hold a shooting contest against a boastful Brabant crossbowman, with old Johnston and giant John triumphing in feats of marksmanship, before Sir Nigel arrives to announce that the whole Company has been chosen to ride into Spain to spy on the enemy.

Sir Nigel's scouting party crosses into Spain, spies on the vast Castilian camp near Burgos, captures the knight Don Diego Alvarez for ransom, and Sir Nigel disguises himself in Spanish armor to raid the royal tent itself, seizing a captive he mistakenly hopes is the king before escaping in the confusion.

themes: news of home and love confessed
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: News arrives that Alleyne's brother is dead and Twynham Castle survived a siege, prompting Alleyne to confess his love for Maude to Sir Nigel; soon after, the small English company is trapped in a mountain gorge by a huge Spanish and French army, and after Sir Nigel defeats a Spanish champion in single combat (fulfilling his vow) the massed enemy launches its assault.

Surrounded and besieged on their hilltop, the English fight off repeated Spanish and French assaults at terrible cost; Alleyne makes a desperate cliffside descent to fetch help after Norbury falls to his death, and though Sir Hugh Calverley's relief force arrives too late to save most of the Company, it finds Hordle John and a handful of survivors still holding out amid the slaughter.

Now knighted, Alleyne rides home to Hampshire believing Sir Nigel and Aylward dead, arrives just in time to stop Maude from taking her final vows as a nun, marries her, and then discovers Sir Nigel and Aylward alive and returning wealthy from captivity, bringing the story to a happy close for all the survivors.

themes: mustering of nations for war (Napoleonic coalition)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: This file contains only the chapter heading 'The Gathering of the Nations' (Chapter XI of 'The Great Shadow'), with no body text present in the source file; no narrative content is available to summarize.

themes: the climax of a storm or battle
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: This file contains only two chapter headings, 'The Shadow on the Land' and 'The End of the Storm' (Chapters XII-XIII of 'The Great Shadow'), with no body text present in the source file; no narrative content is available to summarize.

themes: a separate Brigadier Gerard adventure and a nautical tale beginning
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_white_com.plot: This file contains only closing chapter headings of 'The Great Shadow' ('The Tally of Death', 'The End of It') followed by the titles of two unrelated following stories ('The Crime of the Brigadier' and 'The Slapping Sal'); no body narrative text is present in the source file to summarize.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: The young emigre Louis de Laval sails from England back to France in 1805 on the strength of an invitation from his unknown uncle Bernac, who now holds the family estate of Grosbois, but is unsettled by a cryptic 'Don't come' scrawled on the letter's seal; he lands secretly by night near Boulogne, within sight of Napoleon's invasion camp.

Avoiding the coastal towns for fear of arrest, Louis struggles for hours through a treacherous salt-marsh in a gale, finally reaching a ruined cottage where a strange, refined young man named Lucien Lesage first violently refuses him shelter, hides something up the chimney, then abruptly invites him in.

themes: discovery of a plot against Napoleon
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Left alone in the cottage while Lesage goes to meet his confederates, Louis searches the chimney recess and discovers a bundle of letters addressed to top officials of the Empire along with a proclamation announcing that a committee has condemned Napoleon ('Buonaparte') to death, moments before powerful hands seize him from behind.

Seized by the giant conspirator Toussac and threatened with death for having discovered their secret, Louis is defended by the calm, enigmatic 'Charles', who argues down Toussac and Lesage's demands to kill him and begins a delaying interrogation, until the sound of an approaching hunting hound throws the plotters into alarm.

Toussac kills the pursuing hound but the police close in; 'Charles' reveals himself as an undercover police agent who coldly threatens to shoot the terrified Lesage, until hussars under Colonel Lasalle and General Savary storm the cottage, capture Lesage (Toussac having escaped), and leave Louis in the spy's custody.

themes: moral ambiguity of the secret agent
uneasy trust between rescuer and rescued
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Walking on through the night with his mysterious rescuer, Louis learns something of the fanatical Toussac's history and of his guide's contempt for conventional soldierly honour, before being led through a concealed, ancient underground tunnel into a fortified house where he is given a bedroom for the night.

Louis discovers that his sinister rescuer is in fact his uncle, Charles Bernac, and that he has been brought to his own ancestral castle of Grosbois; over breakfast he meets his hostile cousin Sibylle, who privately reveals that she was the one who wrote 'Don't come' and warns him that his uncle is dangerous, before the two reach a wary alliance.

themes: a daughter's hatred of her father
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Sibylle shows Louis around Grosbois and warns him that her father Bernac schemed to marry them to secure the estate and would have let him die otherwise; Bernac's arrest of Sibylle's lover Lucien is exposed, and Louis, summoned by Lieutenant Gerard to the Emperor's camp, breaks with his uncle before departing.

Escorted by the boastful young hussar Etienne Gerard, Louis rides from Grosbois toward the Camp of Boulogne, learning about the Hussars of Bercheny and the army's fervent confidence in Napoleon's planned invasion of England.

Louis waits in the crowded ante-room at headquarters, is singled out favorably by Duroc, Savary, and Talleyrand, watches Napoleon savagely rebuke Admiral Bruix over the fleet's failure to sail, and is then received and questioned by the Emperor himself about his loyalties.

themes: servants exhausted by a tireless master
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Over a hurried camp dinner, secretary de Meneval and household head Caulaincourt frankly discuss Napoleon's punishing work habits, his manipulation of everyone around him, and France's ambition to crush England as the last rival power.

themes: the workings of a restless genius
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Louis watches Napoleon dictate naval orders, needle Talleyrand and Berthier about loyalty, dismiss Louis's engagement to Eugenie as a matter for his own control, and then refuse Sibylle's desperate plea to spare Lucien, instead granting her one week to capture the fugitive Toussac in exchange for his pardon.

themes: a woman's resolve versus imperial ruthlessness
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: After Sibylle's failed plea, Louis and Gerard pledge to help her hunt Toussac; days later, at headquarters, Louis hears Napoleon muse expansively about world domination to Talleyrand before Constant announces, in near panic, that Josephine has arrived unexpectedly at the room where the Emperor is meeting another woman.

themes: the Emperor's contempt for ordinary morality
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Josephine arrives, discovers evidence of Napoleon's infidelity, confronts him, and is met with a furious public tirade about extravagance and his refusal to be bound by morality, before he abruptly softens and coaxes her back to good humor.

themes: a glimpse of the future (Fulton's inventions)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: At the Empress's reception at Pont de Briques, Louis is introduced to court figures, rebuffs Bernac's insincere overtures, meets the American inventor Robert Fulton, and is publicly claimed by Napoleon as his aide-de-camp before the Emperor humiliatingly scolds guests one by one, including Josephine.

themes: the hunt for a fugitive conspirator
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Sibylle leads Louis, Gerard, and Savary to the Red Mill where Toussac is hiding; after a chase through a windmill and a secret tunnel into Grosbois, they find Toussac has murdered Bernac in revenge, and after a violent struggle the three men kill Toussac, then discover a letter proving Bernac was also a poisoner.

themes: Napoleon's mingling of tyranny and grace
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/uncle_bernac/.plot: Napoleon exposes Lucien Lesage's cowardice before Sibylle, curing her infatuation, then insists Louis marry a lady-in-waiting of his choosing; the 'lady' turns out to be Eugenie de Choiseul herself, brought secretly from England, and the story closes with their marriage and reflections on Napoleon's downfall.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: Micah and Reuben, fishing off Langston Bay, witness a brig firing on a man overboard and rescue the loquacious old mercenary Decimus Saxon, who reveals he carries secret letters from Protestant exiles in Holland to Micah's Roundhead father, Joseph Clarke.

Saxon is welcomed into the Clarke household, where he delivers Rumbold's letter about Monmouth's planned invasion; Joseph Clarke, overjoyed at the news, resolves that Micah shall go to war in his place.

themes: the Rye House Plot and Monmouth's cause
duty to conscience versus loyalty to the king
village life and counsel from elders
the decision to go to war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: Micah reads Rumbold's letter revealing Monmouth's planned rising, debates the justice of rebellion with his father and neighbours (including old Zachary Palmer), and finally commits to join Monmouth's cause.

themes: the ethics of deception in warfare
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: Micah and Saxon are equipped with horses and armour; news arrives that Monmouth has landed at Lyme, and after a tearful family blessing the two set off by night toward the rebel camp.

themes: night ride through a country in alarm
encountering violent death on the road
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: Riding through the night past beacon-fires, Micah and Saxon discover a murdered traveller, hide the body, and press on toward Salisbury, learning en route of rebel movements and a skirmish at Bridport.

At the Blue Boar inn in Salisbury, Saxon disarms a young cornet in a card-game quarrel and befriends the King's officers over wine, after which Micah reads his mother's tender parting letter of advice before they resume their journey.

Reuben catches up with Micah and Saxon on Salisbury Plain; the trio are pursued by dragoons who loose bloodhounds on them, and after a desperate fight in which Micah accidentally shoots a bottle of elixir into one hound, they take refuge at a mysterious lit cottage on the moor.

themes: the cost of loyalty to a fallen cause
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: The travellers are given shelter by the alchemist Sir Jacob Clancing, a dispossessed old Royalist who tells his bitter history with Charles II; Saxon eyes his gold-filled chest with covetous intent, provoking Micah's anger.

themes: omens of death (the gibbet and the old woman)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: Sir Jacob sends the travellers off with gifts and a warning about their route; Micah and Saxon nearly duel over the gold-chest incident but reconcile, and after a grim encounter with a gibbet and a vengeful old woman they press on toward Bruton, sighting distant royal cavalry.

themes: the contrast of frivolity and coming war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: At the Bruton inn the flamboyant, penniless Sir Gervas Jerome talks his way into joining the party while Saxon flirts with the widowed landlady before abandoning the idea of settling down, and the group rides on toward Monmouth's camp.

Joining a column of Somerset peasants bound for Monmouth's army, the group is nearly attacked by suspicious rebels until the fiery preacher Joshua Pettigrue vouches for them, and Saxon is given command of the ragged company just as royal dragoons appear.

themes: the brutality and cost of skirmish warfare
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: Saxon organizes the peasant column into a barricaded defence against a troop of King's dragoons, provoking and then repelling a cavalry charge with volleys and stones, inflicting heavy losses and capturing prisoners and horses before pressing on toward Taunton.

themes: the fragile momentum of Monmouth's rising
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/micah_clarke/.plot: The victorious column marches into Taunton amid bonfires and rejoicing over news of a rebel success at Axminster, while Saxon maintains his pious mask before Pettigrue and the party learns how slowly Monmouth's campaign has progressed.

testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Tried before the Abbot of Waverley for debt and for assaulting a summoner, Nigel defies the court at sword-point until the archer Aylward joins him; the standoff is broken by the sudden arrival of Sir John Chandos, who reveals that King Edward himself wishes to lodge at Tilford.

themes: poverty and pride of ancient lineage
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Chandos brings word that King Edward will lodge at Tilford; Aylward enters Nigel's service, and the impoverished Lady Ermyntrude opens her treasure chest to sacrifice her husband's cherished relics so the household can honourably entertain the King.

themes: preparing arms and provisions for war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Riding to Guildford to sell the Lady Ermyntrude's treasures, Nigel and Aylward are tricked out of their saddle-bag by the 'Wild Man of Puttenham' and his wife before recovering it, then Nigel sells the jewels (helped by Aylward's bargaining) and arranges for his father's old armour to be refitted by Wat the armorer.

themes: debate on the Crusades and divine favour
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: King Edward, the Prince, and their retinue hawk across Crooksbury Heath, debating war, faith and falconry, until Chandos arrives and leads them toward Tilford bridge, where an armoured challenger awaits.

themes: coming of age as a warrior
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Nigel, in his oversized ancestral mail, challenges all comers at Tilford bridge; he unhorses two challengers and appears beheaded when struck by Manny, causing panic until it is discovered his helmet flew off empty, delighting the King and proving his mettle.

During the feast at Tilford, King Edward exposes Sir Aymery, Seneschal of Calais, as a traitor plotting to sell the town to the French, condemns him to death, then—at the Prince's urging—instead uses him to lay a trap for the French raiders, while Nigel is granted his wish to join the Calais expedition.

themes: lore of the hunt and chivalric etiquette
the ideal of woman in knightly devotion
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Newly armed for war, Nigel visits Cosford to bid farewell to the Buttesthorn family; flirtatious Edith asks him to assault a rival suitor (which he refuses), while old Sir John lectures him on hunting terminology and the grave, wise Mary quietly wins his admiration.

themes: rescue of a seduced woman's honour
trial by combat forcing a forced marriage
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Learning that Edith has run off with the manipulative, crooked-backed Paul de la Fosse, Nigel and Mary ride to Shalford where Nigel forces de la Fosse at knife-point to agree to marry Edith, but she rejects the coerced union herself and returns home with her sister.

themes: vows of love and honour before departure
the Pilgrims' Way as microcosm of England
ambush and pursuit by a jealous rival
farewell to homeland on the road to war
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Nigel and Aylward set out from Tilford for the wars, exchange vows of love and honour with Mary at St Catharine's shrine, survive an archery ambush set by the vengeful Paul de la Fosse, and after a comic misadventure with a runaway pack-horse reach Winchelsea near Chandos.

themes: single combat against an armoured foe
courage proven at great personal cost
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: When the French spy Peter the Red Ferret steals Chandos's dispatches and flees by ship, Nigel joins Cock Badding's crew in pursuit, leads a boarding party against fierce resistance, and after a grueling single combat with the armoured Ferret takes him prisoner, collapsing from his wounds.

themes: honour of one's plighted word versus royal will
mercy contested with a king's wrath
the first of three vows fulfilled
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Recovering from his wounds at Calais, Nigel learns of the successful ambush of the French raiders, then defies King Edward's order to execute his prisoner the Red Ferret because he had promised him his life; the King relents, and the freed Ferret carries Nigel's love-token message to Mary at Cosford.

themes: royal favour and rivalry among knights
preparation for new campaigns (Spanish fleet and Brittany)
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/sir_nigel/sto.plot: Nigel accidentally fires a bombard on the ramparts with Aylward, is lectured by Chandos on the changing nature of warfare, then serves at a lavish royal banquet where King Edward announces a naval expedition against a Spanish fleet and assigns Chandos and Nigel instead to reinforce the war in Brittany under Robert Knolles.

themes: proposed political solutions to the Congo atrocities
testi/conan_doyle/atomized/the_crime_of_.plot: In this closing polemical chapter Conan Doyle argues Belgium cannot be trusted to reform the Congo, proposes partition among the European powers or unilateral British action (blockade, outlaw-state declaration, free-trade caravans) as remedies, calls for compensation and punishment of the guilty, and appends documentary evidence of the chicotte whipping torture, followed by an introduction to his real-life investigation of the George Edalji case.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Sir Charles Repton, Warden of the Court of Dowry and a wealthy cabinet minister, breakfasts and walks to a board meeting of the Van Diemens company he secretly directs. His crowded day of political and financial engagements is laid out, and George Mulross Demaine is briefly flagged as a figure to come.

Struck by 'Veracititis' that makes him blurt dangerous truths about finance and politics, the raving Sir Charles is nursed by Lady Repton, who in desperation admits the American quack Dr Scipio Knickerbocker. Knickerbocker cures him with two lancet pricks behind the ears for a hundred pounds, restoring his discretion.

themes: decline and death of the old merchant
testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: The ailing Mr Burden is attended by three eminent doctors while his son Cosmo and the financier Barnett use his name to prop up the M'Korio Delta scheme; drugged, Burden overhears their scheming. Later the mad, abusive letter from his old friend Abbott arrives, and the broken old man sets out to Abbott's City office, feeling death upon him.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: At dinner the loud detective Mr Collop lectures the Home Secretary and his daughter Marjorie on the elaborate, costly method he insists on for searching the West Room for the lost emerald. Marjorie breaks down in tears afterward, and her father resolves to take Collop into the West Room where the jewel vanished.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: The deaf, methodical millionaire G. Quinlan Smith decodes a telegram announcing a coveted antique 'Spoon' available at Villefranche and slips away to catch the Riviera express, foiling his niece Mary's plan to introduce him to the Prime Minister Dolly. Dolly arrives too late for the crucial meeting he wanted.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Henry Bolter, a drug-steeped undergraduate obsessed with alchemy and the Philosopher's Stone, is contrasted with his robust family and his science tutor Charles Lexington. Exasperated by Bolter's cut lectures and mystical essays, Lexington summons him, gets a defiant archaic reply, and storms off to Brecon Street to confront him.

The fleeing Lexington, posing as destitute ex-officer Henry Romilly, is taken on as handyman by the thrifty Duchess of Aberavon and mends her lights and car. Tackling a jammed patent tap as a policeman closes in, he unleashes a flood, then escapes disguised in a woman's clothes across the grounds.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: After the celebrated Mickleton election, Charlie Fitzgerald sends his impoverished cousin Nobby to hint to the newly triumphant Mr Clutterbuck how honours are bought. Nobby's dinner-table talk of fixed prices for titles primes Clutterbuck, who soon hands the party organiser Delacourt an unsolicited £3000 cheque.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The old merchant Mahmoud tells his nephews how, in his destitute days, he schemed with a ragged shepherd to steal and sell a flock of sheep. The 'shepherd' was in fact the richest sheep-owner, who had disguised himself to trap thieves; Mahmoud is arrested, bastinadoed, and turned loose as a warning.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: Sir Robert Montgomery grants his daughter Belinda a conditional hope of marrying Horatio Maltravers, provided the youth take up a profession and endure a delay of trial, forbidding them to meet in his absence. He then labours over and writes a formal letter to Maltravers setting out these terms.

Sir Henry and the solicitor Fox (Portly) strangle each other to death; Sir Robert, as magistrate, takes cognizance of the ghastly scene. His cousin Miss Hackman persuades him to keep the tragedy and her lover's fate from Belinda and to carry her abroad, and the household sets off in procession toward Dover.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: The amnesiac millionaire Mr Petre, sickened by his Rotor fortune, orders Terrard to unload his shares at any price; Terrard and Charlbury arrange the sale to Trefusis, who regains sole control while Petre banks over two million in cash. Freed but still hollow, Petre sends his cook to arrange a secret consultation with a memory-loss specialist, Sir Henry Brail.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Betrayed by a peasant who sells him to the army for a substitute's name, Boutroux is press-ganged by a cavalry patrol, signs on as 'Perrin', and takes a jeering revenge on the peasant before swearing the recruit's oath. He is marched off with a motley band of pressed men and, proving able to ride, is set to stable duty on the march.

themes: satire of the Paris art world
testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Visiting his old Paris studio, the squire Delgairn and his friend Pailey find the starving young painter Bourrot menaced by his landlord, and Delgairn quietly pays the arrears. In gratitude Bourrot dashes off a garish symbolist canvas, 'L'Ame Bourgeoise', which he presents to Delgairn, who hangs it, baffled, in a dark corner at North Merton.

themes: the power and limits of money
testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Confronted by two identical 'Ames Bourgeoises', Sir Henry Bensington devises a scheme, planting one with his tame dealer Gabriel and using two wastrels to leak word to the gullible Duke of Emonsillado. The Duke rushes to Chelsea and, believing himself cunning, 'borrows' the picture from Gabriel for cash under written receipt.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: Fleeing the pressures of London, the naive envoy Richard Mallard reaches the Lakes and then Scotland, unknowingly trailed by Delisport's Sleuth A and Worsing's Sleuth B. The financier Angus Worsing befriends him at the Clan Tarroch Hotel and presses a large personal payment for the West Irania concession, which Mallard cautiously declines before agreeing to visit Worsing's house.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: The Man with the Broken Nose, having stolen the green overcoat, injures himself and sells it to the sinister moneylender Mr Montague for a single sovereign. Examining the coat, Montague finds the abandoned cheque book in its pocket just as violent knocking erupts at his door.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: John Maple discovers a ventriloquist's talent at sea and turns it into a stage living as 'Lieutenant Allegri' and then a performing-dog act under manager Spegel. Meanwhile his Aunt Hilda, deep in debt, feverishly fakes up Rackham into 'Rackham Catchings' to lure a rich buyer, while John dreams of the twenty thousand pounds that would redeem it.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_hedge_and_the_.plot: Rich, isolated New York usurer John Scott Guthrie settles a large tax-free allowance on his idle nephew Wilfred Straddle, exacting a pledge against drink and secretly hiring the informer Willis to watch him. Willis's lying reports of riotous living, the matchmaking of Lady Merriden and Lady Lodiham over the 'Guthrie millions', Joan Sable's refusal to be set at Wilfred for money, and a New York newspaper's lurid account of the Pillbox brawl push the misjudging uncle toward cutting the loyal, teetotal Wilfred off.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The panicked Postmaster-General Halterton visits the financier James McAuley at breakfast, begging for a duplicate of the incriminating undated letter he has mislaid. McAuley, all bland thanks for the awarded contract, denies all knowledge of any such letter and coolly advises Halterton to go home and write down what he wants.

themes: corruption of the machinery of state
the hunt to recover incriminating papers
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The Home Secretary Jack Williams uses his hold over the weak, indebted Gunter to make signed copies and photographs of the two damning documents that have passed through his hands. Meanwhile Halterton and McAuley each lie awake and set out at dawn to stealthily recover the papers that put each in the other's power.

Desportes' papers break the contract scandal, sending 'Billies' shares crashing, while Home Secretary Jack Williams engineers the prosecution of the moralist Reginald Butler rather than the press. In the House, Halterton rises to make a solemn, self-pitying statement affirming that he never received monies he had in fact not received.

themes: rival takeover of Durrant's and Reynier's
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The magnate Arthur Lawson pays the imperturbable go-between Guy des Cuoyes for a signed memorandum and secures Dow's Patent ahead of Durrant's. Lawson then instructs Guy to lure the Home Secretary Jack Williams and McAuley to a Palatine dinner, with an empty chair kept and Lawson's own hand concealed.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: The narrator explains how a rickety Mexican dam speculation (Popocatapetl) controlled by American financier Ole Man Benson is fatally exposed to a statesman's coming Washington speech. Two years earlier Mary Smith had married Benson's rich daughter Sudie to the penniless, well-born George Mulross Demaine, floating the young couple on Benson's money.

The recovered Repton is created a peer and, prompted by the Duke of Battersea, moves a Lords resolution that crushes the newspaper legend that peerages are bought, defeating the scandal. Meanwhile Demaine nervously survives his first question in the Commons, and the whole clan gathers at Mary Smith's supper party.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: Burden confronts the M'Korio Delta syndicate board over their abandonment of his friend Abbott, quarrels violently with Barnett and threatens to expose them, then collapses. He makes his way home broken and, tended by his servant Kate Hatteras, dies in the night; his son Cosmo inherits.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: The blustering detective Collop, hired by Home Secretary de Bohun, applies his 'negative evidence' method by ripping up the West Room's floor, gutting the furniture and smashing a mirror to prove the stolen emerald is not there. Finding nothing, he takes notes on the guests and settles down with whisky.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: An Anti-Bullfighting League deputation is fobbed off by the PM Dolly and Foreign Secretary Tallant, then flattered enthusiastically by Opposition leader Pongo. Mr Moss then hints his party is uneasy about the Indian loan, and Dolly plots to rush the loan through with an immediate closure before agitation can build.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: The mystic undergraduate Henry Bolter, having produced the Philosopher's Stone in a rite, demonstrates it to his skeptical science tutor Lexington by melting lead in a crucible and turning it visibly into gold. He gives Lexington a fragment of the cylinder to test privately for himself.

Lexington is arrested for a petty theft but Bowring springs him and, using the Waif's overheard testimony, blackmails Home Secretary Mills into cooperation. Together they invent the B.I.C.O., an international gold-control bureau at Geneva, and carve up its lucrative posts among themselves, applauded by a jingoistic press.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: Fitzgerald presses party headquarters and the Prime Minister to deliver Clutterbuck the promised knighthood, and plants a premature paragraph in the papers. But the New Year honours list omits Clutterbuck entirely; humiliated, he meets the eccentric William Bailey, who cryptically offers to help.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The merchant Mahmoud tells his nephews how, destitute, he gulled a wealthy young orchard-owner by posing as a pear-tree expert, extracted 500 gold pieces to buy stock, then sabotaged the wagon's wheel to slip away with the money. He rode off, traded up horses, and reinvested the capital in a date caravan to Laknes.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: Sir Robert Montgomery writes to the suitor Sir Henry Portly withdrawing encouragement, because his daughter Belinda now favours her childhood playmate young Maltravers. The scene then shifts to Portly's palatial Molcombe Abbey, revealing that its master is secretly a ruined dependant of the moneylender Lawyer Fox.

Sir Robert takes Belinda and Miss Hackman on a restorative journey across South England to Dover and over to Boulogne, and her health revives. But in the night a nightmare of Horatio departing as a ghost on a grey shore leaves her weeping in utter desolation before she sinks into dreamless sleep.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: The amnesiac millionaire Mr Petre gets nothing from two pompous Harley Street specialists. Walking away in despair he is hailed by an old friend, Buffy Thompson, as 'Peter Blagden', and his memory floods back; he is really a poor gentleman of Harrington who unwinds his three-million fortune and returns home content.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: A ragged detachment of revolutionary hussars, with Boutroux among the recruits, reaches Angouleme where officers have deserted. A swaggering Parliament commissioner with full powers promotes the sole remaining lieutenant to colonel on the spot, and the regiment's trumpet-call seals its adhesion to the Revolution under civilian command.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: The invalid heir John Delgairn discovers by accident an uncanny genius for exact copying, and perfects it by reproducing the obscure Bourrot painting so faithfully that even he cannot tell copy from original. Shortly after this triumph he dies; his father, secretly relieved, is left content with the healthy younger son Harry.

Art dealer Bensington plans to sell each of two identical 'masterpieces' at full price, drilling his colleague Gabriel in the contradictory perjured testimony they will give if it reaches court. He returns the Duke of Emonsillado's £20,000 cheque, declaring the Duke's picture a worthless copy, and sells the other to Lady Norbolt for £20,000.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: Rival ministers and tycoons set four bungling sleuths to trail the West Irania concession envoy 'Mallard' to Glenaber Castle, where the fanatical Arabella Slackett accosts him as a saviour. Terrified, Mallard bolts by train; then Lord Delisport lures him to dinner and, with a hidden stenographer, fabricates a signed admission that Mallard will grant him the concession.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Police 'find' and pocket the receiver Montague's hidden banknotes but really seek Brassington's Green Overcoat, which Montague secretly holds with its chequebook. Overcome by dread of prison and superstition, he passes the coat off to a street lounger and then to the Pole Lipsky, ridding himself of the accursed thing.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: Bo (Isabeau Hellup) coaches the impoverished John Maple to buy Rackham from his Aunt Hilda for a firm option of £20,000 he need not actually possess, drafting the offer and acceptance letters herself. She then reveals her plan to fake a haunting of the house to force Aunt Hilda's hand.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_hedge_and_the_.plot: After spies report his nephew Wilfred's dissipation, millionaire John Scott Guthrie crosses to London, disinherits him, and is then killed stepping into traffic. Meanwhile the sponger Bill Robinson fleeces Wilfred of £200 on worthless Kleindrift shares; left friendless and uncertain of his fortune, Wilfred is befriended by Joan Sable, who urges him to work.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Financier J. (McAuley) denies ever giving Postmaster-General Halterton the incriminating bribe letter, coaxing him to put his claim in writing; the anxious Halterton refuses and vows to find the letter. Back at the Commons, Honest Jack Williams watches the 'Billies' shares boom on the Television Contract and decides to hold.

Halterton and McAuley each set out to shadow the other around the Marble Arch and Bayswater Road, dodging rude policemen, an area maid's sooty brush, and each other's back-views in a comic dance of espionage. Both fasting and cold, they end up riding the same lift, Halterton trailing McAuley into his flats.

Halterton denies in the House that he took any bribe over the Television Contract, and the Opposition leader and Honest Jack Williams back him fulsomely (Williams having already sold his Billies). Reginald Butler is arrested for criminal libel and a heavily-loaded 'strong' committee is appointed, whose majority report exonerates everyone.

The immense magnate Arthur Lawson coldly demands from McAuley the letter stolen from Halterton; McAuley, calculating his advantage, reveals that Home Secretary Jack Williams now holds both fatal letters. Lawson has McAuley telephone Williams to arrange an immediate meeting, then goes to bring his full weight to bear on him.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: The Prime Minister tries to have the newly-mad financier Sir Charles Repton certified insane, but two vain, rival physicians instead pronounce him perfectly sane. His secretary Edward Evans then races round Fleet Street bribing and bullying editors to suppress every report of Repton's antics and of the missing Demaine.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: Barnett whips up a nationwide craze of art, press and pseudo-science around the M'Korio Delta company, then presents the wavering Burden to the grotesque explorer Major Pondo, which fills Burden with disgust. Burden goes to warn his blunt old friend Abbott, who roars that the whole scheme 'stinks'; Burden returns home at midnight to find Barnett waiting in his chair.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: The doddering Professor de Bohun buys an old scientific instrument, passes it off to his cousin Humphrey as a crystal-detecting 'talcometer' (secretly working its needle-locking stud himself), and convinces Humphrey that the journalist McTaggart is carrying the missing emerald in his pocket. Humphrey, tormented, resolves to warn and search yet another guest.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: Prime Minister Dolly dines with the financier Duke of Battersea to secure the Indian Loan, but the Duke lectures him on falling British credit and quietly imposes hard conditions, gripping control of the famine relief works. Humiliated and angry, Dolly drives to Mary Smith, who promises to arrange the loan elsewhere through her husband's uncle G. Quinlan Smith.

Walking to catch his train, Pennybunt (Pongo), Leader of the Opposition, is charged by a bull and trapped for hours in a shed on Mary Smith's estate, then manhandled by the bull-reeve's men. He borrows servants' clothes, races to London in rags, and reaches the House of Commons just as the fatal 'Division' is called.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Charles Lexington, disguised in wig and beard as a match-seller, wanders penniless and exhausted through London, is moved on by police, and is guided by a suspicious fellow-tramp to Old David's common lodging-house, where he eats, sleeps and learns the customs of the destitute before drifting on toward the Embankment benches.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: The Irish adventurer Charlie Fitzgerald becomes Clutterbuck's secretary, coaxes him into subscribing £1,000 to the National Party funds, and steers him toward the Mickleton candidature. Coached by Fitzgerald, Clutterbuck bumbles through the local committee's inquisition on Ireland, temperance and Offences Disfranchisement, and is duly adopted as Prospective National Candidate.

themes: public spirit as cover for greed
testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The rich uncle Mahmoud tells how he 'partnered' an old ferryman, then built a rival bridge that captured all the traffic and drove the ferryman into madness and death. He then whipped up a popular 'Free Bridge' campaign to abolish the tolls, and had himself voted 1,400,000 dinars in compensation, doubling his fortune.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: Walking from the high wood, Belinda and Horatio meet a majestic saffron-robed lady (Venus, seeking her boy with the bow), then part in wordless new-found love at the shrubbery gate. Belinda hurries to her father Sir Robert's study, where his grave and mournful manner warns her of a momentous communication.

Convalescing in his rescuer's French chateau, Horatio gazes across the sea toward England and vows never to return, while his mysterious hostess is stricken by the memory of her own youthful lost love. Meanwhile Sir Robert returns home to find Belinda wasting away, until she at last confesses in tears that the cause is her Horatio.

themes: the reputation of a financial genius
testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: The brokers Charlbury and Terrard plot to unload the worthless Paddenham Site onto the amnesiac millionaire Mr Petre, who, hiding that he understands nothing, nods his way through the pitch and commits to buy for over £800,000. His blind luck holds when the Education Department, prodded by a minor official, promptly decides to buy the site for millions.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Boutroux, blackened and disguised as a charcoal-burner while on the run, delivers a sack of charcoal to a farm girl and trades riddling talk of 'hunting' and love. She sees through his disguise, brings him wine and water, and agrees to hide and feed him in her father's charcoal hut.

themes: war seen by the bewildered soldier
testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Exhausted and soaked, the hussar Boutroux endures the long bombardment of Valmy sheltering with his old white horse behind a windmill, watching panics, cheers and Kellermann's rallying charge without grasping the battle. At evening a herald reads the order, and he learns it has been a great victory and that a Republic has been proclaimed.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Rival art-dealers Henri Caen and Signor Alessandria each deduce that the stolen 'Ame Bourgeoise' is hidden at Delgairn's North Merton house. Caen bribes the inn maid and her parlourmaid sister Millie to fetch the picture, then slips away by train with it under his cape, only for the suspiciously friendly Young Artist to leap into his carriage.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: Foreign Secretary Lady Caroline Balcombe drafts a memorandum on secretly securing the Eremin concession from the disguised envoy 'Mallard', and directs Prime Minister Bullar to make Home Secretary Hardham extract it. Over a carefully engineered dinner Hardham interrogates the wholly innocent tourist Richard Mallard, who understands nothing of the 'concession' pressed upon him.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: The dishevelled Professor Higginson returns home, fends off police by inventing a three-day loss of memory, then inflates the story into a lucrative tale of visions and communion with the dead. His colleague Garden gossips of it to the sinister Dr Babcock, who telephones his newspaper-baron master and awaits instructions by the evening train.

themes: the sensible ruin of an amiable man
testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: Squire Henry Maple of Rackham drifts ever deeper into debt to his methodical solicitor brother William, whose ambitious wife covets the estate. Over Sunday wine William lays out the £17,324 owed and gently persuades the vague, sentimental Henry to travel abroad with his son while William takes over and 'keeps up' Rackham.

Alone and nerve-shattered in his bedroom, the old ennobled parvenu 'George' is unnerved by phantom knocks, then by a voice mimicking his dead mother pleading against his 'pison' whisky, and by a ruffed, faceless figure by the bed. He shrieks and crashes to the floor as his wife Amathea and the guests rush in to find him breathing but stricken.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: A character portrait of Home Secretary 'Honest Jack' Williams at breakfast in his modest villa: a mill-boy risen through union and Parliament to office and a quarter-million fortune, reading the news aloud to his equally shrewd wife Martha, whose steady negative judgements have helped make him.

Williams goes home by train while the anxious Postmaster-General Halterton just misses catching him at the Club. Preparing for bed, McAuley discovers the two crucial envelopes have been filched from his coat pocket, leaving only the metal clip; he rushes back to the Club to ask the porter, glimpsing Halterton across the road.

A flashback explains how Halterton twice helped Jacob (Arthur) Lawson's brother into Cambridge and a Fellowship, rooting Lawson's lifelong devotion despite their distance. Meanwhile Lady Papworthy, fed gossip by the crusading poet Reginald Butler, hears of the corrupt Postmaster-General/McAuley contract deal that has secretly promised the contract to Durrant's.

themes: corrupt bargains between politics and the City
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Arthur Lawson calls to congratulate Halterton but finds him broken and haggard. With unaccustomed warmth Lawson urges him to speak and confide everything, and Halterton at last pours out the whole tale of the corrupt contract agreement, the stolen letter, and his bitter dealings with Williams and McAuley.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Demaine, a stowaway Cabinet minister, escapes the ship the Lily by swimming ashore at Parham and blunders into a house that turns out to be his eccentric cousin William Bailey's. Bailey hides him up a chimney and then disguises him as a woman named 'Rebecca' to fool two searching policemen.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: At Norwood the drowsy financier Barnett, backed by Cosmo, presses on Burden that Abbott 'must come in' and hints they will use 'pressure'. Later, at the magnificent M'Korio Delta offices in Broad Street, Barnett, Burden, Harbury and Lord Benthorpe read over and pass the company prospectus for the press.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: A blunt policeman calling himself 'Mr Collop' arrives at the Home Secretary's house posing as a diplomat back from 'Bogotar', to the dismay of de Bohun and his daughter Marjorie. The journalist McTaggart, prompted by his guardian Angel, slips the stolen Emerald into Collop's evening tail-coat pocket.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: Mary Smith bellows into the ear of her deaf, immensely rich uncle G. Quinlan Smith and coaxes him into agreeing that his firm, Smith and Fischer, will float the Indian loan. She then tells the anxious Prime Minister Dolly the deal is fixed, to be settled the next morning.

In a carefully rehearsed Commons debate on the Indian loan Dolly slangs the absent Pongo for hours, but Pongo never arrives (trapped by a bull in Somerset), the half-wit Capthorpe carries the House, and the Government is defeated by thirty-seven. In the epilogue Dolly dissolves Parliament and wins a huge majority that routs the Relief Works.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: The destitute fugitive Lexington is taken in off the Embankment by the charitable Rev. Arthur Bootle to St Dives' Hostel, where he is numbered and confined. Terrified that a job with Lord Taylor will expose him, he steals a pound note Bootle dropped and escapes at night down knotted sheets before the theft is discovered.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: A wharf quarrel between Harman and the workman Peake escalates into a strike, and the jailing of Fishmonger and Bebb under a harsh judgment by Justice Hunnybubble inflames London. Fitzgerald tours Mickleton's pubs, gauges the popular fury, and rewrites Clutterbuck's election manifesto to champion the imprisoned workmen.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: Retiring for ease, the merchant Mahmoud lends his million dinars to the island kingdom of Izmat, secured on its Salt Tax, and enjoys wealth alongside the demagogue-tribune Tarib. But Tarib whips up popular agitation against the salt tax and the alien rich, and a creeping series of graduated taxes aimed squarely at Mahmoud reduces him to under a thousand dinars.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: Sir Robert solemnly urges his daughter Belinda to consider marrying the eligible neighbour Sir Henry Portly, whom she recoils from with loathing. When she confesses her heart is plighted to the penniless Horatio Maltravers, her father erupts in fury and she swoons upon the carpet.

Enraged at the silence from Horatio, Sir Robert storms to the Maltravers house to find it shut and Horatio gone, and learns from a servant that Horatio's letters to Belinda were handed to Miss Curll. He returns and interrogates Miss Curll, who, cornered, is about to confess intercepting the lovers' correspondence.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: An Anonymous Benefactor loses the bid for the Paddenham Site, which is sold instead for the Education scheme, enriching Terrard and his hangers-on at Petre's expense. When the Bank Manager pushes Magna Development shares, the reclusive Petre curtly refuses; his refusal is misread as secret dealing, and both Terrard and the Manager profit as Magnas rise.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: In hiding in a shed, the fugitive Boutroux is secretly tended and fed by the peasant girl Isabel (nicknamed Joise). Coming to him by night she warns that the charcoal-burners and, worse, armed men sent by the Commune are hunting the man who killed a man in the city, and promises to smuggle him away when the moon darkens.

After the cannonade at Valmy the regiment is told it has won a great victory and marches off eastward in what Boutroux privately reads as a retreat. At the gates of Ste Menehould his exhausted old white horse collapses under the shock of a runaway artillery battery and falls on his leg, crushing him under the limber's wheels into unconsciousness of pain.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Charming his host Delgairn, the picture-dealer Alessandria locates and steals the 'Ame Bourgeoise' from the lumber-room by night, then races off, unaware the Temporary Odd Man clings to his car and corners him at his cottage. In a parallel thread the Young Artist has fastened himself onto the rival thief M. Caen aboard the train and steers him and the same disputed masterpiece toward Bensington.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: The bewildered visitor Richard Mallard, tailed by clumsy plain-clothes men Chinny and Corbould, finally thrashes them in Trafalgar Square and is praised by magistrate Service, who denounces the police. The Prime Minister Mary Bullar then sends her secretary Delavere to sound Mallard out over the Piraeus Concession, but the uncomprehending Mallard only bewilders him.

themes: a lie spun out of control
testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Pressed by the sceptical Babcock to prove his ghost story, Higginson invents an armless, seaweed-smelling drowned figure in dark blue. Babcock phones the news to The Howl, and next morning a report of an armless nobleman, Count Michaelis, found drowned on the Breton coast matches the fabrication exactly, terrifying Higginson as the papers trumpet his 'proof of a future life'.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: In wartime exile in the Jura, the gentle Henry Maple slowly declines while his brother William, then William's widow Hilda, absorb the mortgaged Rackham against a debt inflated to £20,000. Dying, Henry tells his son John the truth; John, seeing the vulgarised, renamed 'Rackham Catchings' and refusing Hilda's charity, vows to find the £20,000 and reclaim the house.

The night after the peer George Huggins is prostrated by seeing the headless ghost, Lord Hambourne secretly sells the story to The Howl for cash while Hilda tries to keep it out of the papers. At dawn the press photographer 'Columbus' outwits the detective Pretherton (whom Bo's bulldog chases off), and Bo bribes Columbus to splash the picture, ruining the Rackham market.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Over breakfast the 'Honest Jack' Williams spots that Durrant Imperial Telegraph shares (Billies) have jumped in New York while keeping up an idle conversation with his wife about buying a cottage. He hurries to the telephone and orders his broker Gunter to buy fifty thousand under an agreed second name.

McAuley tracks the missing incriminating envelopes to the billiard-room and concludes Halterton has taken them, gaining new respect for the Postmaster-General's cunning. In fact Jack Williams has them: on his train home he transfers them to his breast-pocket, then steams the envelopes open and irons the creased letters flat in folded flannel.

Fired by his beloved Lady Papworthy, Reginald Butler tips her about the Television contract and she rashly buys five thousand Billies she cannot afford, late and at a loss. Butler, convinced Halterton took a huge bribe though he has no legal evidence, resolves against his usual caution to put the accusation into dangerous print.

Arthur Lawson (Aaron Levina) pledges to save the grateful Halterton, sealing it with an unusual gesture of both hands. Back home he questions his scientist brother Jacob about the indispensable Dow's Patent and whether Reynier's control it, then, his plan forming, telephones for a young man, Guy des Cuoyes, to set the first step in motion.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: The young Prime Minister fends off dangerous parliamentary questions about his missing minister, then Demaine reappears absurdly dressed with a fabricated shipwreck tale written for him by William Bailey. Edward quietly reconstructs the real story and coaches Demaine to keep the invented version.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: The M'Korio Delta company's shares are allotted and then soar and change hands in feverish speculation while old Burden sickens with vague suspicion. Cosmo forces his way into the resistant Mr Abbott's office and threatens to 'freeze him out' unless he joins the scheme, provoking a furious scene.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: The nervous Home Secretary privately briefs the coarse detective Collop and then confronts the journalist McTaggart about the missing emerald; McTaggart denies it and accuses Collop instead. Meanwhile a Devil and an Angel brawl over who is responsible for slipping the jewel into pockets.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: Three professional art thieves burgle the Duke of Battersea's Riviera villa Les Charmettes, taking a spurious Disraeli spoon and other objects; their unlit car crashes, killing two, and Bertot flees into the hills with the loot. The aged Duke, told by telegram, chiefly bemoans his run of bad luck.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: At a university lecture on the transmutation of metals, the banker Lord Taylor attends anxiously, fearing that cheaply manufactured gold could crash the banks. The lecturer Charles Lexington cautiously equivocates on whether gold can actually be made, leaving Taylor uneasy and no wiser.

While the browbeaten Rev. Bootle is set tasks by the domineering Sister Frideswied, the fugitive Charles Lexington disguises himself as a blackface minstrel banjo-player and is dragged to the races. Unable to sing his solo, he flees a mob, swims the flooded Thames, and lands on a great estate.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: Clutterbuck's campaign rides the mob's enthusiasm for the jailed 'Fishmonger' cause through meetings, voice-coaching, canvassing and bribery, despite setbacks over his host Stephens and forced teetotalism. On a heavy poll he defeats Lord Henfield by 1028 and becomes a Member of Parliament.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: Mahmoud tells his nephews how a lawyer, Kazib, bled him of fee after fee over his charter claim against the King, then how at trial the pleader Selim and the Judge farcically destroyed his case by quibbling over the word 'AND.' Ruined and mocked, Mahmoud flees the island penniless by ship.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: After Belinda faints, Sir Robert and his cousin Miss Hackman resolve to leave for London on urgent legal business, arranging for the impoverished Miss Curll of Bath to come as companion and chaperone. Sir Robert gently reassures his daughter of the plan at her bedside.

The wretched Miss Curll confesses she was bribed by Lawyer Fox, at Sir Henry Portly's instigation, to intercept Belinda's letters; Sir Robert dismisses her and dispatches stern demands to both men. Fox, panicking, rides to Molcombe Abbey to confront the equally suspicious Portly.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: Charlbury schemes to exploit the mysteriously passive millionaire Petre's name to bluff the Trefusis brothers' Rotor monopoly into a combine. Terrard coaxes an incriminating note out of the terrified Petre and pressures Henry Trefusis into a hasty deal, which Trefusis then resolves to turn into an even larger raid.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Joyeuse leads the fugitive Boutroux by night through the woods to the cottage of the hard old peasant woman Perrin, and by dawn he sees her face at last. Perrin, having spirited Joyeuse away, coerces the disguised Boutroux into the cart to be sent off to the armies, and he departs cursing her.

The wounded Sergeant Boutroux lies dying in a military hospital set up in a dissolved convent, tended indifferently; an opiate brings a vivid vision of Joyeuse and his old horse Pascal. He asks for a priest, murmurs about the rain, and dies.
