testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Dealer Bensington receives, one after another, two rival 'recoverers' of his picture, M. Caen and Signor Alessandria, each bearing a canvas. He tells each that it is a worthless copy lacking his secret hidden mark, pays each £500 against a signed receipt, with his agent concealed behind a curtain as witness.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: Newspaper-magnate Lord Delisport plots to secure the Eremin monopoly and uses his old railway mate Tommy to bribe petty officials for information on the incoming agent Richard Mallard. He ambushes the baffled Mallard at his hotel to fish for a deal, then briefs his private sleuth to shadow the man to Scotland.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Overwhelmed by sacks of fan mail after his faked psychic 'revelation,' Professor Higginson is taken in hand by the worldly Babcock, who sorts the letters and steers him into a lucrative exclusive article and a career-making invitation to address the influential Research Club, 'where men are made.'

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: The chapter introduces the American millionaire Hamilcar Hellup, whom Lady Pattle at last persuades to buy a peerage, and his daughter Bo, who is falling for the penniless John Maple. Meanwhile Aunt Hilda buys a fraudulent 'Ancestor' portrait and other fakes to gentrify Rackham into 'Rackham Catchings.'

With the house discredited by the staged 'haunting,' the servants quit and the enraged Amathea (Mattie Huggins) storms off as her husband is stretchered away. Bo and John pressure the ruined Aunt Hilda—clinched by a voice thrown through the Ancestor's portrait—into signing Rackham over to John, and Lord Hellup comforts her.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Walking to Whitehall, Home Secretary Jack Williams reasons out that the Television contract has been swung to Durrant's because McAuley bribed the Postmaster-General, sending 'Billies' shares soaring. Meanwhile the anxious Halterton repeatedly telephones the evasive McAuley to clear up a growing misunderstanding.

Having personally stolen the two incriminating letters—Halterton's typed contract promise and McAuley's handwritten bribe offer—Jack Williams gloats that he now controls the whole Television deal. He plans to keep and cut in McAuley while discarding Halterton, waiting for the right moment to strike.

The crank MP Reginald Butler, inflamed, writes a wild libellous letter naming Halterton, McAuley and two ministers as bribe-takers and takes it to the disreputable Rashdell's obscure sheet the Oriflamme to be printed. The narrator marks this as the reckless step leading Butler to his doom.

The chapter sketches the polished investigator Guy des Cuoyes, bought over by Arthur Lawson to find things out. Lawson urgently dispatches him to discover who really owns Dow's Patent (Television) and to buy it at any price by Monday night, and to probe Durrant's contract.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Ole Man Benson (Theocritus C. Benson) is ruined when a Mexican earthquake wrecks his Popocatapetl speculation, so he cuts off his daughter Sudie and son-in-law George Mulross Demaine's income. Mary Smith and William Bailey then quietly scheme to push the impoverished George into a salaried government post.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: The narrator delivers a pompous mock-biographical introduction to the life of the pious merchant Emmanuel Burden, tying him to the M'Korio Delta Development Company and its financiers (Barnett/Lord Lambeth, Lord Benthorpe). He explains his sources, his sense of a providential imperial 'Destiny', and his grievances against Mr Abbott.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: Belloc's dedicatory preface to Maurice Baring, explaining why he dedicates this fourth book to him and joking that he promised to write a detective story on condition there was nothing to find out.

The drunken detective Mr. Collop is jabbed awake by the missing emerald hidden in his coat pocket, and conceives a scheme to frame someone. He captures the parrot Attaboy, carries it into the moonlit snow, and presses its claw-prints in a trail to an old oak where he hides the stone as false evidence.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: The deaf aged millionaire-collector G. Quinlan Smith pursues a burly mysterious woman off the Riviera train because she dangles a silver teaspoon supposedly used by Disraeli. When she spots a policeman she seizes the hired carriage, drives it furiously into the hills, ditches it down a ravine to throw off the mounted police, and leads Smith on foot to a disreputable house.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Henry Bolter takes a final fatal dose of his drug and dies in bliss in his lodgings. Meanwhile the tutor Charles Lexington, obsessed, secretly repeats Bolter's transmutation and turns lead to real gold; rushing to Bolter to learn the reagent's source, he finds the young man dead.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_romance_of_tri.plot: The childhood of Tristan: orphaned son of Rivalen and Blanchefleur, reared by Rohalt and Gorvenal, he comes to King Mark's court, slays the Morholt of Ireland, wins Iseult for Mark, and on the voyage he and Iseult mistakenly drink the love-philtre. Their secret love is spied on by the four felons and the dwarf Frocin; caught by the blood on the flour, Tristan makes the chantry leap, rescues Iseult from the lepers, and the lovers flee into the wood of Morois.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: A portrait of the wealthy, feckless eccentric William Bailey, whose obsession is seeing a universal Jewish conspiracy everywhere. The anxious Mr Clutterbuck, fretting over an uncertain deal, consults Bailey, who is compiling a 'dictionary' of supposed Jewish origins and finally gives him a cryptic tip: try the Anapootra Ruby Mines.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The rich uncle Mahmoud tells his nephews how, arriving with camels laden with dates, he was gulled by the great merchant Yusouff-the-Triumphant into selling his dates for a third of their value on a false tale of a date-glut. Trying to imitate Yusouff, Mahmoud then rushes camels to a town he overhears is desperate for them, only to find the king seizing every camel for war, leaving him ruined again.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: It is explained how Sir Henry Portly's father Sir Orlando ruined the family speculating on the Rothschild-spread false news of Waterloo, leaving Molcombe Abbey near foreclosure, which Sir Henry hopes his marriage to Belinda will repair. On receiving an alarming letter he gallops to Bath and orders his creditor, the sinister Lawyer Fox, to make the spinster Miss Curll their agent and quash the threatening accident.

Sir Robert resumes the journey through France with Belinda and Miss Hackman, but a postillion's blunder wrecks a chaise horse and the axle in a deserted district. Sir Robert walks to a nearby château for help and is visibly shaken when the major-domo names his mistress as the Marquise de la Ferronnière of the Château de Rosny.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_1.plot: The real millionaire John Kosciusko Petre discovers he has been impersonated in London by Peter Blagden, who made a fortune under Petre's name, and launches the suit Petre v. Blagden. Through mock-legal Latin technicalities the case runs through the courts and the House of Lords; Petre loses and cannot recover a penny, while the weary Blagden pays up and resolves to buy a boat and seek only peace.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Boutroux, under the alias Perrin, is made a sergeant in the ragged revolutionary cavalry chiefly because he can read and write, and marvels at the makeshift army as it marches to Poitiers. In a coffee-house a fanatical Royalist stranger confides that they mean to kill the 'traitor' Georges Boutroux hiding in the regiment; Boutroux, the very man, coolly plays along and sets a trap to deflect the hunter.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: A biography of the great art-dealer Sir Henry Bensington, whose gift is switching aesthetic fashions to suit the market and whose fortune was made by the New York Customs ruse of over-painting and re-revealing a Rembrandt's signature to ruin then enrich a picture. A later coup, discrediting and then re-authenticating a Claude in the National Gallery, cements his rise toward a peerage.

Puzzled by Bensington's returned cheque, the Duque de Emonsillado gets Lord Borstal to plant a press paragraph claiming he owns the recovered Bourrot masterpiece. The two halves of the gossip-columnist 'Lothario' write contradictory paragraphs giving the picture to two different owners; when The Howl prints both, the Duke reads that Lady Norbolt also 'has' it and explodes in fury, vowing to prosecute.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: The four English sleuths and the French agent Hippolyte Dubois (Armand de Berensac) hunt the harried fugitive Richard Mallard across France, cornering him at a rural inn. Hippolyte arrests him and escorts him back to London, where after a scuffle at Trafalgar Square Mallard is jailed once more, protesting he never tried to escape.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: The petty informer James tries to sell the stolen green overcoat to Lipsky the Pole, but both men are seized by an inexplicable supernatural dread around the coat. Lipsky first refuses, then greedily buys it and falls ill with unaccountable fever until, days later, Mr Kirby arrives at the shop directly asking for the green overcoat.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: The life of the costermonger George Adolphus Huggins, who parlays a Goose Club's entrusted money and a series of speculations into wealth, crowned by acting on a wrong-number telephone tip on the eve of the Great War to make a huge fortune. Guided by his shrewd wife Matilda, he becomes Sir George and finally Lord Mere de Beaurivage, retiring to a Berkshire house and befriending Hilda Maple's circle.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Postmaster-General Wilfrid Halterton nervously awaits the financier James McAuley in his flat to sign the arranged letter over the coming television monopoly contract. The chapter lays out the rival Durrant's and Reynier's groups competing for the charter, and the 'modified public control' by which whichever monopoly wins is guaranteed profit.

In the Commons, Halterton fields evasive supplementary questions and the Fine Arts minister Lord Papworthy is heckled over pictures going to America. Anxious about a hitch with Durrant's, Halterton slips out to the Home Secretary Jack Williams's room to confide that he does not feel happy about 'J.' (McAuley).

Halterton flees from McAuley's flat and the two men comically shadow one another to Victoria, each hiding in telephone boxes and dodging round corners. Honest Jack Williams stumbles onto the scene, links arms with Halterton, and bursts out laughing on realising each man is spying on the other because each thinks the other holds the letters.

The disgraced idealist Reginald Butler seeks comfort from Joan Papworthy, only to be savagely abused and driven out; she then collapses in tears and finds her Billies shares have crashed. Meanwhile Halterton, publicly exonerated by the committee, is more wretched than ever, and Lady Papworthy must confess her speculative losses to her husband.

The financier Arthur Lawson calls on Home Secretary Jack Williams and coolly demands the two documents (Halterton's contract pledge and McAuley's managership letter); Williams denies holding them, then, stung by the word 'lie', flatly refuses and declares himself impregnable. He dismisses the matter, unaware that a dinner invitation from des Cuoyes is drawing him and McAuley into a new move.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: The financier Sir Charles Repton, nursing a head injury from a barber's chair, manoeuvres the Van Diemens board into a fresh capital issue dressed up as an imperial railway through the unexplored 'Out and Out', overcoming the tiresomely practical Bingham. He then lunches a foreign agent into ordering a useless bridge and answers questions in the House.

themes: the influence of the City merchant
testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: A memoir-style account traces the Burden family from obscure Suffolk origins to the City ironmonger's fortune of the late Emmanuel Burden, chronicling his marriage, children and household. Special emphasis falls on his soft, gentlemanly son Cosmo, whose social connections (notably with Mr Harbury) draw the merchant toward the fatal forces of the modern world.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: A Lincolnshire brig-master, William Bones, wins a huge emerald from the Empress Catherine and rises into City wealth, his descendants inflating the name to 'de Bohun' and treating the jewel as the tutelary heirloom of the house. The line descends to Humphrey de Bohun, Home Secretary, who ceremonially gives the re-set emerald to his daughter Marjorie on her eighteenth birthday.

Over a strained country-house breakfast the guests gossip about who stole the emerald, while the pompous policeman Collop announces to Humphrey de Bohun that he has 'found' it and interrogates the terrified boy Ethelbert about an open window. Collop marshals all the guests into the West Room around the parrot Attaboy's cage to stage his grand revelation.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: The aged, deaf millionaire George Quinlan Smith spends a wretched night in a criminal den where his cross-dressing companion turns King's evidence; a police raid sweeps them all up. Marched to Tarascon and jailed after weary formalities before magistrates, he settles to sleep and discovers the fateful spoon still in his pocket.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: After the earlier death, the chemistry tutor Lexington secretly repeats his transmutation and produces more gold, then confides the secret to his antiquary friend Bowring over dinner. Bowring, appalled at the danger, dissuades him from publishing and proposes a secret alliance to launder the gold through his art-and-plate trade, Lexington keeping the reagent's nature to himself.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_romance_of_tri.plot: Tristan and Iseult live as hunted exiles in the wood of Morois until King Mark, finding them asleep with a naked sword between them, spares them and leaves tokens; moved, Tristan resolves to yield the Queen back. Through the hermit Ogrin peace is made and Iseult restored, and she later clears herself before Mark and King Arthur by seizing red-hot iron unharmed in the ordeal.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: Bailey urges the baffled Clutterbuck merely to 'talk about' the Anapootra Ruby Mines, and the mention alarms the financier Duke of Battersea, whose whitewashed concession Belloc satirically defends. Meanwhile Clutterbuck learns a petition disputes his election, and as press notoriety over the mines grows he swings between terror and vain public pride.

themes: buying and selling the same goods
testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The old merchant Mahmoud tells his nephews how, ruined and suicidal, he seized a runaway horse, sold it to a fleeing fugitive for gold, then reclaimed it in court as 'stolen' and was paid compensation. Recovering the horse yet again, he sells it a third time to the dealer Abd-ul-Eblis, moralizing that one should reckon what sums one has subtracted from a town on leaving it.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: The lawyer Mr Fox visits the impoverished companion Miss Curll and, with a twenty-five-pound note and promise of more, bribes her to prevent Belinda and young Maltravers from even corresponding during Sir Robert's absence. Sir Robert then departs happily, leaving Miss Curll installed as the assiduous, reins-taking guardian of his daughter.

After a carriage mishap Sir Robert, stunned by hearing the name Ferronniere, leads his party to the chateau of the English-born Marquise, an old love of his, who shelters them. Belinda, resting below, hears the voice of her estranged Horatio, the young Englishman lodging there, and he enters to confront her with disdainful, angry pride.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: In Bordeaux the wine-merchant Boutroux lectures his flippant nephew Georges over dinner about debts and a forbidden love affair, forbidding him to go out. Georges, hinting that the girl's Jacobin brother plans an attack on the house that night, defies his uncle's curse and steps out along the fevered quays with his little dress-sword.

Sergeant Boutroux stages an elaborate joke, handing a bewildered German soldier to a cloaked Royalist visitor and sending a quick-witted Parisian hussar to shadow them. The Parisian's fake sentry-pacing rouses a courtyard mob, an 'Austrian conspirators' scuffle ensues, and Royalists, mob and German are all hauled before the guard, the colonel judging everyone fools.

themes: satire of modern art and critics
testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Belloc mocks the sudden fame of the painter Bourrot, launched by the critic Cresk with a black canvas 'Le Neant', and the dealer Bensington signs the dying artist to a contract while fishing for a lost 'Masterpiece'. Tracing it to young Delgairn's billiard-room, Bensington buys the priceless canvas for a mere 550 guineas from the squire, who is delighted only that it settles his dead prize boar's debts.

themes: class and money in the witness box
testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: The lawsuit Emonsillado v. Norbolt over which of two 'Ame Bourgeoise' canvases is genuine opens with contrasted counsel Atterleigh and Hawlboy before the passionless Justice Dove. Sir Anselm lays out the picture's disappearance and double recovery, the dealer Gabriel withstands cross-examination, and the racy, wealthy Duke of Emonsillado testifies before the great expert Dr Mowlem is called.

themes: political satire of women in power
testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: The real West Iranian envoy surfaces in Devon offering the Eremin concession direct, revealing that the jailed Mallard was the wrong man, so Caroline Balcombe and the Prime Minister Mary Bullar buy Mallard's silence with a life annuity and ship him back to Havana. In the epilogue Mary Bullar crushes Cannock of Cardiff's righteous but garbled accusation in the House, announcing the concluded Eremin concession to roaring cheers.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: The amused solicitor Kirby humours the raging landlord Postlethwaite over the wrecked Greystones, pockets a dropped professorial memo, and begins piecing the puzzle together. When Brassington bursts in over a forged cheque bearing James McAuley's name and his missing green overcoat, Kirby quietly telephones his underworld contacts and gathers all he needs, inviting Brassington and his son to a London dinner.

themes: social satire of peers and dons
testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: John Maple comes down to his aunt's mangled old home Rackham Catchings determined to buy back Rackham for twenty thousand pounds, while Aunt Hilda, pressed by her creditor the 'Esthonian', means to sell to a rich guest for fifty thousand. They clash over the price at tea, then at dinner spar over the assembled guests, the impoverished don-journalist Lord Hambourne and the ennobled financier de Beaurivage.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Belloc explains the contest between Durrant's and Reynier's for the long-range Television charter, hinging on who secures Dow's Intensifier, with James McAuley the master of Durrant's and their shares ('Billies') buoyant. The nervous Postmaster-General Halterton awaits McAuley, who arrives and spreads out the decisive typed letter on the official paper to conclude their corrupt bargain.

Halterton confesses to the astute Home Secretary Jack Williams that McAuley's acknowledging letter, with his own damning pencil note on it, has vanished and that McAuley now denies ever giving it. Williams deduces at once that McAuley has recovered and kept the letter, precisely because Halterton's pencil note gives the financier a hold over him.

Having steered Halterton away from brooding on McAuley, Jack Williams watches the 'Billies' shares soar and orders his man Gunter to sell the lot at a fat profit, then feeds cronies a hint that Halterton and McAuley have quarrelled. He writes gleefully to Lady Caroline Balcombe, who promptly invites both antagonists down to her house Sandlings for the weekend.

With the Butler scandal blowing over and 'Billies' climbing, the Home Secretary Williams times his move and accosts McAuley in the Park, flourishing first photographs and then the original incriminating letters. Cornering the sickened financier, Williams makes clear that he now holds the whip hand and that 'poor old Wilfrid' Halterton is cut out of the deal.

The smooth des Cuoyes hosts McAuley and Williams at a restaurant to broach Dow's Patent now that Durrant's has the contract, with McAuley bringing in his brother the Attorney-General Sir Andrew. Just as terms are floated, des Cuoyes ushers in the unexpected 'friend' who really controls matters, the tall dark figure of Arthur Lawson, leaving the three men appalled.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: At the Petheringtons' crowded party Mary Smith corners the young Prime Minister 'Dolly' and lobbies him to find a government post for her hapless cousin-in-law George Mulross Demaine, now that Ole Man Benson is broke. She hustles the flustered George out into the night and lands on the plan to shunt Sir Charles Repton into the Lords to clear a place.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: The innkeeper Mr Capes extorts 750 pounds from young Cosmo Burden over his letters to Hermione; the smooth Mr Harbury rescues Cosmo with a loan arranged through the moneylender Ashington, then draws him into the imperial-finance set around Mr Barnett and first names the M'Korio Delta scheme that will ruin Cosmo's father.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: The chapter surveys the country house Paulings and its deserted West Room with the parrot Attaboy, then gathers the de Bohun family at tea. The awkward journalist Hamish McTaggart is awaited, and on arrival mispronounces the Home Secretary's name, winning Victoria Mosel a bet with Tommy Galton.

The detective Collop marches the frozen guests outside and 'proves' by induction that a jackdaw stole the emerald, recovering it from a hollow branch and restoring it to Marjorie, though Victoria Mosel privately reveals she saw it in his hand beforehand. The Home Secretary courts the once-suspected McTaggart with promise of patronage.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: The Prime Minister Dolly and his 'opponent' Pongo hunt frantically for the vanished financier George Quinlan Smith, whose loan Dolly's government depends on, while the Duke of Battersea leaks the Indian Loan story to the papers to squeeze him. Peggy lets slip that Smith bolted to Villefranche after a relic spoon, and Pongo is dispatched to fetch him.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Bowring watches Lexington transmute lead into gold in a crucible and the two agree a fifty-fifty partnership, delivering the gold weekly. Brooding over how much more Bowring makes reselling it as antique goldwork, Lexington nurses a grievance and secretly begins skimming extra gold for himself.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_romance_of_tri.plot: Exiled, Tristan wins a fairy dog with a sorrow-charming bell for Iseult and later weds Iseult of the White Hands, though he keeps faith with the true Iseult; disguised as a madman he visits her at Tintagel. Mortally wounded, he begs Kaherdin to bring Iseult by ship with a white sail, but his jealous wife lies about the sail's colour and Tristan dies, Iseult the Fair dying of grief beside him.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: An election petition unseats Clutterbuck after Fitzgerald's treated voters are exposed, and William Bailey plans a protest meeting on the Anapootra Ruby Mines. The Duke of Battersea hires the detective Bevan to shadow Bailey but Bevan trails the drunken valet Zachary by mistake; armed with the gossip anyway, the Duke silences Bailey with a threat of exposure.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The old millionaire Mahmoud tells his nephews how he worked a shrine, buying worthless objects cheap from departing pilgrims and selling them as sacred relics to arrivals. The saintly Holy One, himself a shrewd trader, catches him and takes half the takings as sleeping partner; when the Caliph's men force him to raise Mahmoud's cut to three-quarters, Mahmoud loads his gold on a mule and slips away, evading the assassins sent after him.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: The companion Miss Curll intercepts a note from Horatio Maltravers meant for Belinda (Miss Montgomery), and, overcome by curiosity, secretly opens and reads his impassioned love-letter before hiding it away. She returns to the sleeping Belinda, who wakes and gazes wistfully toward the Maltravers house.

Belinda and Horatio meet, discover their estrangement rose from letters each thought unanswered, and are reconciled just as Sir Robert and the Marquise enter. In conference Sir Robert repents having designed a richer match for his daughter, while the Marquise Esmeralda resolves to adopt Horatio as heir to her vast wealth, and Sir Robert renews his own old love for her.

themes: the French Revolution as new religion
testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Georges Boutroux finds the plebeian Henri Sorrel (renamed 'Miltiades') and accompanies him to a Jacobin Section meeting on the eve of insurrection. When Miltiades denounces a plot involving Boutroux's uncle's house, Boutroux coolly buys guarantees of the property's safety, paying a thousand livres to insure his uncle against being treated as a traitor.

Now a cavalry sergeant under the name Perrin, Boutroux is accosted in barracks by an ostler bearing the Club's password, who reveals the Society is hunting the man Boutroux (himself) for betraying the Bordeaux club and killing a guard. Playing along as the loyal Brother, Boutroux secures night leave to be taken to the Society's meeting.

themes: press manipulation and the publicity boom
testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Press magnate Henry Bensington choreographs a newspaper 'boom' around the dying painter Bourrot and his lost 'Masterpiece,' coordinating rival papers, obituaries and captions. The two-bodied hack 'Lothario' pumps out the paragraphs, and the exhibited 'Ame Bourgeoise' becomes a sensation, drawing queues down Bond Street until Lady Norbolt makes a bid.

At the libel trial over which copy of the 'Ame Bourgeoise' is genuine, the learned expert Mowlem is demolished by Sir Rory Hawlboy for never having seen the original, and young Delgairn is tricked into swearing to the wrong canvas. The jury absurdly awards both Lady Norbolt and the Duke twenty thousand pounds each, and the rival experts Mowlem and Dacy brawl in the corridor.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: In a burlesque dedication to Maurice Baring, Belloc spins an elaborate mock-logical comparison between an overcoat and an elephant, and confesses he titled the book 'The Green Overcoat' to be confused with Baring's play 'The Green Elephant' and so get it boomed by mistake.

Professor Higginson returns to the empty 'Accursed House' to recover a lost memorandum with a phone number, is chased off by the caretaker, and learns the agent is Mr Kirby. Calling on Kirby, he tries to disguise his interest as a 'subliminal vision' of the house, but Kirby toys with him and steers him off with an invitation to dine, extracting his self-betraying admissions.

themes: a fabricated ghost to raise value
satire of impoverished dons and war profiteers
testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: The guests arrive at Mrs Hilda Maple's Rackham Catchings for a weekend engineered to sell the house: the poor psychology don and secret gossip-columnist Lord Hambourne, the American Hellups with John and Bo, and the vulgar new-rich Mere de Beaurivages. Aunt Hilda pads her false history of the house with an invented headless ghost to inflame the rival would-be buyers, while John and Bo quietly plot.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The financier McAuley presses the dithering Postmaster-General Halterton to sign a memorandum awarding his company the contract against the Committee's report. Halterton stalls, wanting a simultaneous written promise about his own future reward in the Company, and McAuley weighs how much such a signed record would tie him.

The Home Secretary Williams coaches Halterton on exactly where McAuley keeps the compromising paper (his left-hand breast-pocket) and why. The section then turns to a satirical portrait of the young, mysterious Lady Papworthy, wife of the aged Fine Arts minister Lord Papworthy, whose origins none of the town gossips can agree on.

Driving Halterton down to Sandlings, Lady Caroline Balcombe gently probes for the truth of his rumoured quarrel with McAuley, learning only that he is deeply anxious. She lodges the two rivals in adjoining rooms with a maid set to watch, and springs the younger McAuley on Halterton at dinner, but the wary pair only eye each other's coat-pockets and never confer.

Williams forces James McAuley to accept fifty-one per cent control terms for the flotation, and the photographs go back into the locked cupboard. The narrative turns to the criminal-libel trial of the hapless Reginald Butler, introducing with heavy irony the wealthy, landed, devoutly anti-Roman judge Sir Henry Chasible who is to try him.

Arthur Lawson confronts Williams and the McAuleys, reveals that he owns Dow's Patent and holds proof of their document-thefts, and compels them to hand over the two envelopes. Williams gets home to find his cupboard of photographs already emptied, and next morning Lawson calmly plans his next move on Halterton and Williams.

themes: women manipulating politics from behind the scenes
testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Mary Smith engineers George Mulross Demaine's sudden public prominence through planted newspaper notes and scripted parliamentary questions. She then maneuvers to have the dim Demaine appointed Warden of the Court of Dowry, a lucrative sinecure, once Charles Repton vacates it, pressing the reluctant Prime Minister to sound Repton about accepting a barony.

themes: the alien financier and English prejudice
small good deeds and their consequences
testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: The narrator recounts the 'discovery' and imperial partition of the M'Korio Delta, then introduces the financier I. Z. Barnett, sketching his origins and the fraudulent collapse of his Haymarket Bank. Cruising the African coast, Barnett conceives the Delta scheme and learns that the merchant Burden and shipowner Abbott hold the key to launching it.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: As Marjorie shows off the emerald brooch it slips from her hand and vanishes into the polar-bear rug. The three guests, McTaggart, Lord Galton and the Professor, grope for it in vain, each secretly convinced he is the suspect, while unknown to them the jewel is lodged in the stuffed bear's ear.

The butler George Whaley theatrically accuses his master Humphrey de Bohun of having pocketed the lost emerald; de Bohun erupts and kicks him out, and Whaley then chases the boy Ethelbert, who reveals the gem has been found. A closing 'tale-piece' narrates the later fates of all the characters and discloses that the emerald was paste, later given to the nation.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: At Tarascon the aged American banker G. Quinlan Smith is interrogated by the Juge d'Instruction, who reads out a wholly fabricated criminal record and, taking Smith's English and apparent deafness as proof of guilt, constitutes him a prisoner. Smith manages to have a telegram sent to Mary Smith in London begging for legal aid.

themes: alchemy and the transmutation of metals
testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Lexington quarrels with his partner Bowring over a fairer share of the freely-made gold and storms out. Colliding in the street with the wealthy banker Lord Taylor, he is taken home to dine, warned against Bowring, and confesses that he can make gold, demonstrating the transmutation for the astonished old banker who locks the new gold away.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: The book's dedication page, dedicating Mr. Clutterbuck's Election to Gilbert Chesterton with the motto 'Idem Sentire de Republica', accompanied by an editorial note on the Belloc-Chesterton ('Chesterbelloc') partnership.

The fanatical William Bailey borrows Clay's shed for a meeting then capriciously cancels the hired hall, causing the financier Duke of Battersea and Mr Kahn of the Anglo-Saxon Exchange much trouble as they have the hall dismantled. Meanwhile Charlie Fitzgerald deliberately drives Mr Clutterbuck on a long, wandering, breakdown-plagued motor run to keep him from the London meeting.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: Mahmoud tells his nephews how he financed an idealistic young engineer's marsh-drainage scheme on ruinous terms, then took over the reclaimed land for nothing, cultivated the city's magistrates with rigged wheat deals and cheap building plots, and finally sold the whole new quarter back to the town for two million gold pieces, leaving the engineer a menial pittance.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: The ailing Belinda, distressed by Horatio's silence, writes him a tender letter and entrusts it to her companion Miss Curll to send; Miss Curll instead secretly breaks the seal and pockets it. Horatio, having heard nothing, agonises and writes to Belinda once more, imploring any reply.

An aged pair, Belinda's father and the Marquise, tenderly renounce a rekindled old love, settling for decorous friendship. The next dawn is Belinda's wedding morning, and she and Horatio are married by the Reverend Mr Atkins, attaining at last their wedded happiness as the novel closes.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: On an August 1792 night a revolutionary crowd gathers at an inn to hear news from Paris and, worked up, marches on the wealthy Boutroux house. Old M. Boutroux calmly answers the mob's improvised committee from his balcony, agreeing to furnish a list of his guests, while his nephew Georges quietly slips away in the shadows.

Disguised as the hussar Sergeant Perrin, Boutroux harangues the Poitiers Jacobin club and cunningly incites them to send a deputation to destroy the real Boutroux household, his stepmother and the man now bearing his identity, and to ruin the Bordeaux society's president. Afterwards he deflects a police murder inquiry onto an innocent old carter.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: A satirical profile of the immensely rich Verecundia, Lady Norbolt, her two penniless well-born companions Ardee and Elless, and her enemy Hardham, Duque de Emonsillado, a childhood associate and son of her father's partner. Snubbed out of London society by Vurry, the embittered Hardham nurses a dull revenge with his own millions.

themes: forgery and authenticity of a masterpiece
testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: The destitute Goatcher spots the lost 'Ame Bourgeoise' hanging in a pub and tips off the dealer Bensington, who buys the picture for fifteen pounds. Bensington then offers this 'original' to the Duke of Emonsillado, who refuses, and finally sells it to Lady Norbolt for twenty thousand pounds.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Caught in the rain leaving a party, the timid Professor Higginson yields to temptation and steals a magnificent green overcoat. Hailing a taxi, he is seized, gagged and driven to a derelict house by two young gentlemen-kidnappers, Jimmy and Melba, who, taking him for 'Brassington', demand money and a signed letter.

The shrewd lawyer Kirby tracks Brassington's green overcoat through the fence Montague to the pawnbroker Lipsky, recovering it with the tell-tale cheque-book still in the pocket. He then arranges a London dinner after Professor Higginson's lecture, telephoning young Jimmy McAuley to invite him and a friend.

themes: faking a haunting to wreck a sale
satire of the nouveau-riche and academics
testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: While their elders discuss the sale of Rackham Catchings, the lovers Bo and John plot to 'haunt' the house and frighten the prospective buyers off, spoiling Aunt Hilda's market. During a garden walk John, a ventriloquist, unnerves the old Lord Mere de Beaurivage with whispered words from the shrubs and a childhood headless-ghost tale, leaving the peer shaken.

themes: a sinecure managership as disguised payoff
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The financier James McAuley drafts a flattering letter offering the retiring Postmaster-General Halterton the managership of his Corporation, adding by postscript a ten-thousand-pound tax-free salary. Each man seals his copy of the corrupt bargain into an envelope to keep as security.

themes: satire of the art-minister and connoisseurship
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: A satirical portrait of Lord Papworthy, the perennial Minister for Fine Arts, and his enigmatic salon-ruling wife Joan, whose background is a blank. It introduces Butler, a romantic-looking 'Anarchist' MP whose safe seat rests on his genuine popularity with his working-class northern constituents.

At Lady Caroline Balcombe's country house each of McAuley and Halterton tries to sneak into the other's room to steal the incriminating envelope; her paid servant reports the farcical failed raids. Lady Caroline uses the tip to sell her crashing 'Billies' shares in good time and make a packet.

themes: party secret funds and their corrupt uses
family loyalty versus self-interest at the Bar
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The hopeless Reginald Butler is tried for having accused Halterton of selling a contract; despite his brother's involvement, Sir Andrew McAuley prosecutes to crush the rumours about James McAuley. Mid-peroration his junior Tartle receives a startling secret note bearing very private information about the party funds.

Lawson finally persuades the relieved Halterton to accept shares held secretly in trust in his favour. Meanwhile at the Home Office, John Williams, cornered by Lawson's proof of the stolen documents, suddenly recalls an old altered-cheque crime tying him to Lawson and, panicking when Lawson's card is brought in, slips out by a side door to avoid him.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: The financier Charles Repton weighs commerce against politics; the Prime Minister, walking him to Westminster, offers a peerage, which Repton accepts on strict conditions of no office and an unchanged party subscription. That afternoon the Prime Minister sounds out the timid Demaine for a cabinet post.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: The narrator describes old Mr Burden's stubborn patriotism and refusal to mix finance with politics, and his small dwindling trade in the M'Korio Delta. He contrasts this with Barnett's quiet, growing influence over the Press, marshalling brilliant young journalists to prepare public opinion for the Delta's development.

themes: theft and fear of the law
the poor man's dread of justice
testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: The boy Ethelbert, shaking the polar-bear rug, finds the dropped de Bohun emerald and, terrified of the police, slips it into Lord Galton's trouser pocket. Galton discovers it, and after breakfast contrives to drop the perilous gem into the old Professor's overcoat, freeing himself for the moment.

themes: national credit and the Indian loan
testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: At a country-house weekend Prime Minister Dolly confides to Pennybunt, Leader of the Opposition, that the grave Indian crisis requires a loan he cannot float, and fears his absent wife Peggy and the Socialist 'Straights' may force a dissolution. Both men conclude they must appeal to the aged financier the Duke of Battersea.

Stranded three hours at Tarascon, Pongo kills time watching a shabby, half-empty bullfight of a bored bullock. Leaving, he spots the aged G. Quinlan Smith being marched off handcuffed by gendarmes, blunders into the arrest trying to intervene, and is himself seized, bound, and locked in the Palace of Justice.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Lexington, having briefly mislaid then recovered the cylinder of gold-making material on which his fortune depends, resolves to analyse it and takes it to a wood to apply Barlow's electrical test. The switch triggers a violent explosion that annihilates the substance, blows him against a tree, and leaves him irretrievably ruined.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: The ailing Boyle asks Clutterbuck for a small advance covered by a million war-supply eggs stored at the docks. When Boyle suddenly dies and the eggs seem lost, the suave Baron de Czernwitz reveals Boyle was a discredited debtor but generously sells Clutterbuck the million eggs for a nominal sum, founding his fortune.

The great election meeting at Mickleton collapses into a riot when the candidate Clutterbuck fails to appear, the platform stormed and the police called. Afterwards William Bailey coolly persuades the young Prime Minister to grant Clutterbuck a knighthood on a wholly invented pretext, and Sir Percy Clutterbuck duly gets his honour.

themes: wealth and the peace of the soul
testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The old merchant Mahmoud recounts to his nephews how he amassed vast wealth by floating loans, selling insurance for more than it was worth, and unloading real or imaginary estates on the gullible via share-mania, then prudently liquidated and fled before the ruined state collapsed. His youngest nephew forges his signature for 20,000 dinars, proving worthy of the trade and inheriting all.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: Belinda and Horatio each pen despairing farewell letters, both intercepted and locked away by the treacherous Miss Curll. Believing himself spurned, the feverish Horatio saddles his horse and rides out by night, journeying for two weeks across England to reach the storm-lashed haven of Dover.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: An Englishman returning from America loses on the train all memory of his past self; checking into the Splendide, he is taken for the fabulously rich American financier John K. Petre. Two journalists scheme over the famous name while a Mrs Cyril telephones and writes inviting him to lunch, and he resolves to reconstruct his identity in secret.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Barred from his uncle's house by two Revolutionary sentries, Georges Boutroux provokes and fatally runs through the Jacobin Miltiades in a rapier-versus-sabre duel, then routs the second sentry. Wounded and refused entry even by the loyal old porter Nicholas, who gives him money and food, he flees Bordeaux at dawn by boat.

As the regiment marches toward the frontier amid desertions, shootings, and the news that Verdun has fallen, Sergeant 'Perrin' (Boutroux) is ordered to requisition five horses from the suspect Spinster de La Roche. He rousts a grumbling old townsman at midnight to guide his squad to her dilapidated château, where the servants at last admit them.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Bensington refuses to sell the 'Ame Bourgeoise' to Lady Norbolt in order to drive the price up, and, spurred by a threatening letter from young Delgairn, decides the masterpiece must be 'stolen.' He summons his degraded, drink-ruined slave Chas. Goatcher and drills him to guard and conceal a sealed wrapped parcel.

Verecundia stages a grand black-draped unveiling of the masterpiece with the charlatan critic Vavassour pontificating, until Dr Mowlen bursts in denouncing it as a forgery and blurts that the Duke of Emonsillado holds the original. In the epilogues the Duke resells his copy to her for twenty thousand, and the rival experts discover Bensington's secret marks are gone, proving every version a fake.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: The kidnappers Jimmy (James McAuley) and Melba, convinced that Professor Higginson — wearing John Brassington's green overcoat and carrying his cheque-book — is Brassington, demand he sign a cheque for two thousand pounds. Higginson attempts a fake signature, is exposed by a genuine specimen, refuses, and is left bound in the dark.

Jimmy and Melba entertain young 'Booby' Brassington at Bolter's and drunkenly confess they forced his father to sign the cheque. A telephone call from the lawyer Kirby summons Jimmy urgently to Ormeston about the house Greystones; seized by panic over 'duress' and old Brassington's fate, he invents an excuse and rushes off north by night train.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: Hilda Maple works both the Baroness de Beaurivage and the American Lord Hellup toward buying Rackham, each of them feigning reluctance to part with the beloved place. Alone afterwards, both women coldly calculate prices, and the debt-ridden Hilda telephones the moneylender de Vere, stalling him with talk of her imminent sale.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: McAuley deftly pockets the incriminating envelope from Postmaster-General Halterton. Left alone, Halterton exults at having secured, in return for his political services, a lucrative future post at the head of the new Television Corporation, and carefully calculates the decorous interval of some eighteen months before he may cash in.

A satirical sketch of Reginald Butler, the harmless scandal-hunting MP always defeated and forgotten, and his devoted admirer Joan Papworthy. It then turns to the art-loving Lord Papworthy, indifferent to money and the market, and recounts how the Ministry of Fine Arts was created to satisfy the young art-mad Duke.

The Prime Minister Mrs Boulger gloats over her profitable exit from the collapsing 'Billies' shares. The narrative then introduces the great financier Arthur Lawson, telling how, as the poor scholar's son Aaron Levina, he survived a murderous pogrom in Russia and was brought with his baby brother and the devoted Aunt Reba to shelter in London.

The Prime Minister's chief secretary Danver is convulsed with helpless laughter on learning that the Chancellor and Chief Whip ('the Heavenly Twins') used secret party funds to rig the market in Billies. He sends the junior secretary Bill to carry a note of the discovery to the prosecuting counsel at the Old Bailey trial.

Lawson intercepts the fleeing Home Secretary John Williams, cows him with the Katanga affair, and marches him to obtain a signed share-allotment note from McAuley. He then dictates terms to Williams and Halterton: Halterton to take twenty thousand pounds compensation instead of the general managership while Lawson secures the shares against his Dow's Patent.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Sir Charles Repton, stricken by a strange affliction behind the ears, behaves with childlike candour and cruelty after resigning his post for a peerage to save his Company. His loyal admirer Withers vainly tries to get him to the Commons divisions, while at Westminster Demaine is quietly confirmed as his successor.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: Young Cosmo Burden, living beyond his means, is repeatedly rescued from debt by Harbury and the financier Barnett, drawing him into their M'Korio Delta circle. A long biography traces the ruin of the impoverished peer Lord Benthorpe, whose estate has been taken over by Barnett's loan company, and who Barnett means to pair with old Burden as the two pillars of his African development scheme.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: Lord Galton convinces the Home Secretary that Cousin Bill has the stolen emerald and dramatically searches his overcoat, finding nothing. In fact the absent-minded Professor found the jewel in his own pocket and, egged on by a wandering Minor Devil, plants it in the young journalist McTaggart's coat during billiards; an Angel stops McTaggart from exposing it, and he hides the emerald in terror.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: At luncheon the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition (Pongo) fret over the dissolution and the news, dropped by Victoria Mosel, that Peggy is back at the Duchess of Battersea's. The immensely rich, stone-deaf financier G. Quinlan Smith pores over a map of India amid rumours of famine and unrest, while Dolly resolves to go to town to see the Duke of Battersea.

Held by French police, Pongo is examined by a fussy little English doctor; the American financier Smith has been arrested with a stolen silver spoon. Pongo has Smith turn King's evidence against his accomplice Bertot, and a flood of telegrams frees the millionaire; grateful, Smith lets Pongo broach and settle the great loan on the train to Paris.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Lord Taylor lies awake plotting to control the secret of manufactured gold, then tries to force his way into Bowring's business and is coldly refused. He goes to the Home Secretary Jack Mills, who calmly resolves to seize and silence Lexington and suppress the secret entirely, using the department's card-index to fabricate a hold over him if needed.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: The sudden peace ending the Boer War at first ruins Clutterbuck's speculation in a million preserved eggs stockpiled for the army, and police call about the absconded Boyle. But the Government generously buys up the eggs and a lucky Curicanti Docks investment follows, so that by 1910 Clutterbuck has amassed over £60,000 and the manners of a prosperous man.

themes: the mercy of Allah as fortune
testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The vastly rich Baghdad merchant Mahmoud gathers his surgeon-brother's seven nephews to recount how he made his fortune. Kicked out of home with a hundred dinars, he stows away on a ship stealing food by trickery, then swindles a carpet-obsessed merchant out of his jewels and cash and flees down the Gulf, multiplying his capital fifteenfold by shameless cunning and luck.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: In mock-sentimental style the tale introduces the peerlessly beautiful and pious Belinda, cherished only daughter of the prosperous baronet Sir Robert Montgomery. Across the road lies the neglected, decaying estate of the last of the Maltravers, young Horatio, the two properties sharply contrasted in order and ruin.

Grief-stricken Horatio reaches Dover, tenderly gives away his faithful horse to an innkeeper, refuses food, shelter and delay, and embarks on the Boulogne packet. In a violent hurricane the vessel pitches out of harbour while Horatio stands unappalled, gesturing back at the receding shores of England he means to leave for ever.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: A worshipful society luncheon awaits the fabulously rich, amnesiac Mr Petre; talk turns to Touareg shares, and when Terrard presses him Petre blindly says he will "buy largely," sending the guests scrambling to their telephones. Terrard walks him off to buy fifty thousand shares in his name, while Petre, terrified of exposure, flees London in a panic.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Wounded and on the run after a killing in Bordeaux, Boutroux hitches an ox-cart with a lying tale of robbery, then reaches a village inn where he signs a false name and hears the locals debate the murder and old Boutroux's innocence. Spotting a lawyer's chaise outside, he slips off and bribes the young postilion to swap clothes so he can escape northward.

Sent to requisition five horses, Boutroux is received by a gracious, ironic old chatelaine who submits charmingly, gives him wine, and draws out his sentimental life-story on the dark terrace. After an intimate, teasing interval she signs the receipt, and he rides off on the horse the sullen groom had falsely called lame.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: The two flattering companions coax the rich Verecundia into a mock-mediumistic resolve to offer £20,000 for the masterpiece, while dealer Henry Bensington gleefully receives a rival bid from the coarse Duque de Emonsillado. Bensington tells both parties the picture has been stolen from his safe, and Verecundia faints away when she hears the news.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: In New York a scar-faced man and his slouch-hatted companion, trailed by a detective of the Truth and Justice agency, quietly change their steamer berth; the detective is killed crossing the street before he can report. The agency sends Merriman, who photographs and bribes the wholly innocent young traveller Richard Mallard aboard the boat, obtaining the name attached to the watched cabin.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Wealthy leather-merchant Brassington, who secretly worships his recurring Green Overcoat as a luck-charm, tells his lawyer friend Kirby that he refuses to pay his son Algernon's latest gambling debt. Leaving Perkin's party, he finds the treasured coat gone from its peg and, stricken, walks home through the storm while Kirby quietly resolves to trace it.

Kirby lures young McAuley to Ormeston by telephone and, feigning talk of a trivial damages claim, drops that Brassington's cheque is deemed a forgery. Stung, McAuley blurts that the cheque was made out to him in payment of Brassington's son's gambling debt, extracted the night of the party from the man in the Green Overcoat, letting Kirby deduce the coat impostor.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: John Maple recruits the butler Corton into a scheme to fake a headless ghost and frighten the millionaire buyer off Rackham so John can keep his birthright. Meanwhile Hilda Maple plays her two rich guests, Lord Mere and Lord Hellup, to fix a price of fifty thousand guineas, and Bo assures her bewildered father that Jacko will buy the place cheaply himself.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The financially embarrassed Postmaster-General Halterton, gloating over McAuley's lucrative offer, discovers the vital envelope has vanished and frantically searches his study on hands and knees. Telephoning McAuley's flat, he thinks he hears the man's evasive voice, is told he is out, and is left in agony resolving to write to him at once.

A satirical history of the Ministry of Fine Arts, whose holder is expected to lavish his own money buying art for the nation, so that only the rich Lord Papworthy can fill it. To keep him in office through every change of government he simply switches between Socialist and Anarchist parties, until a constitutional fudge lets him sit permanently as a member of the government whether in power or opposition.

The backstory of Aaron Levina, an immigrant scarred by a pogrom, who toils in London to build a small dealing business while devotedly raising his gifted younger brother Jacob toward a career in science. As Aaron expands into precious metals, Jacob is knocked down by a car in the Mile End Road, the driver being the young, then-wealthy Wilfrid Halterton.

At the climax of the criminal-libel trial the journalist Butler, who confessed he had only Fleet Street gossip against the statesman Halterton, is undone by the Attorney-General's tearful peroration and Judge Chasible's solemn charge on the sanctity of public men. The jury convicts without leaving the box, and the judge sentences the offender to a mere fifty-pound fine.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Struck by a malady of total candour, Sir Charles Repton brawls on a bus, then openly tells a Van Diemens shareholders' meeting that their stock is worthless and the promised railway a pure swindle to ramp the price before unloading. He then answers Commons questions with damning frankness, and the Prime Minister scrambles to have him confined and certified before naming Demaine as successor, only to learn Demaine has mysteriously disappeared.

testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: Cosmo subtly saturates his father's household with talk of the M'Korio Delta until Mr Burden proposes developing it, and on Cosmo's suggestion writes to Lord Benthorpe for advice. Burden travels to Placton, dines with Benthorpe and Mrs Warner, and is flattered into committing his judgment and reputation to Barnett's African syndicate.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: The boy Ethelbert, who himself planted the stolen emerald in a nobleman's pocket, tries to confess cryptically to the butler Whaley, who silences him. Whaley concludes his own master, Humphrey de Bohun, stole his daughter's Emerald, and rehearses how to reveal his 'knowledge' and extract a grateful reward.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: The narrator recounts the Franco-Dutch banking origins of Peggy (Margaret de Villon), the Prime Minister Dolly's forceful wife, and her political triumph in discovering and financing the socialist 'Straights' who now sustain his government. Amid an Indian famine and loan crisis, Peggy barges into Dolly's room with the Straights' Whip Mr Moss, and Dolly fakes a telephone call to escape the interview.

Pongo secures the loan in Paris, reads the rival Moon and Capon papers, and hurries home worried the public wrongly believes the Indian Loan is earmarked for relief works. That evening at Habberton, Mary Smith coaches Dolly step-by-step on how to stage a bogus Commons debate, complete with a planted fool, so that Pongo's party is stampeded into backing the loan.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Home Secretary Jack Mills visits Bowring's shop, first trying to plant his nephew as a partner and then threatening ruinous legislation, to force a share in Bowring's suspected gold-making secret; Bowring flatly refuses. After Mills leaves, Bowring discovers a terrified waif hidden in a coffer who overheard everything, and drills him into a paid, word-perfect witness to the bribery attempt.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: As the Manatasara Congo concession seeks capital under a veneer of freeing the natives, the ailing Clutterbuck leaves garbled instructions; his confidential clerk misreads a shorthand word as 'Manatasara' and applies for 60,000 'Congoes'. Recovering, Clutterbuck finds himself accidentally worth a quarter of a million, sells near the top, and his legend as a financier launches him toward public life.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: The merchant uncle tells his nephews how, given a stranger's purse of coins by a corrupt magistrate, he was offered the magistrate's pearls cheap, sold them to a jeweller for 10,000 dinars on a false tale, and pocketed the lot. He then sent the real purse-owner to the magistrate with a phrase that got the innocent youth arrested and beheaded, while the pearls proved false and the jeweller was beaten, all of which he ascribes to the Mercy of Allah.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: The narrator recounts how the impoverished but accomplished Horatio Maltravers, heir to a mortgaged estate, was in childhood the intimate playmate of the heiress Belinda, and how their meetings grew rare and formal as they came of age. Sir Robert Montgomery holds a grand ball, arranged by his cousin Miss Hackman, to present Belinda as the queen of Wiltshire society.

Horatio, exiled and heartbroken, apostrophises the cliffs of England, crosses to Boulogne, and strides off southward. On the lonely road at nightfall he single-handedly beats off a band of brigands attacking a carriage, rescuing a stately English-born Marquise who binds his wounded arm and insists on taking him up beside her.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: The press-baron Duke, once the match-selling orphan Higgs, learns the untouchable millionaire John K. Petre is in London, sacks his agent Batterby for not reporting it, then is warned by his secretary that printing anything about Petre is ruin. The disgraced Batterby drifts to a pub, is picked up by the rival editor Sir Jeremiah Walton, and sells him a stolen Foreign Office note; meanwhile secret officials quietly place Petre under surveillance.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Disguised as a postilion, Boutroux drives his lawyer passenger off the highroad into the muddy back-country, feigning religious madness and threatening to deliver him 'bound and delivered' beyond the Hills of Gold. Halting at dawn, he lets the terrified lawyer stumble off toward peasants for help, then rides away into the woods and escapes.

A ragged, exhausted cavalry column marches eastward through pouring rain, turned away from Bar-le-Duc and doubling back to St Dizier, starving. Boutroux breaks into a shuttered butcher's shop to feed his men and comforts his failing horse Pascal, before the troop pushes on to join Kellermann's mass of soldiers gathering, unknowingly, for the battle against the invading armies of Europe.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Charged by his master Bensington to lock up a sealed parcel, the alcoholic Chas Goatcher instead goes on a pub crawl and loses it. In a third pub he drunkenly fixes on a ranting thief, Bill, who carries a newspaper parcel (in fact a stolen silver tray), accuses him of taking 'his Thing', gives chase, falls bloodied on the pavement, and staggers home to oblivion.

themes: futuristic geopolitics and a rare mineral
testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: The chapter tells how Richard Mallard, adopted heir of the maniacal old William Mallard and butt of the 'Mallard Millions' joke, was hounded across America by reporters and fled aboard the Zeeland to a longed-for quiet England. Meanwhile the spy Ethel (Giva), Baronne de Larance, relays his movements to an intelligence network, and the real quarry, the marooned West Iranian agent 'Chap 1', sits shipwrecked on the Labrador coast holding the fate of the priceless Eremin/Durandite concession.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Bound to a chair in the stolen Green Overcoat and mistaken for the merchant Brassington, Professor Higginson works free enough to trace and forge Brassington's signature onto a cheque. The young men Jimmy and Melba return, make him sign the accompanying letter authorising payment of a 2,000-pound debt, then carry him off and lock him in a comfortable room until the cheque clears.

About to deliver a lecture at Galton's before a room of grandees, Higginson spots Jimmy, panics, and bolts, sparking a hatless chase through London until he takes refuge in a squalid pub. Jimmy corners him, smooths over the policeman, and takes him to the Rockingham, where the solicitor Kirby joins them and announces he will fetch the real Brassington and his son.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: Bo rigs up the boy John as a headless spectral cavalier to haunt Lord Hellup, while Hilda Maple manoeuvres to sell her 'haunted' house at the best price. The self-made peer George Huggins (Lord Mere de Beaurivage) is browbeaten by his wife Amathea into agreeing to buy it, and beats Hilda down to fifty thousand pounds flat.

themes: a financial leak and insider dealing
testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: The Postmaster-General Wilfrid Halterton writes to McAuley begging him to replace the letter bearing his compromising signature, then frets over a newspaper leak that the Committee has reported for Reynier's against Billies. The narrator traces the leak through a page boy, porter, and journalist Gamble, all fed by bribes from McAuley's secretary Rose Fairweather, while Halterton fails all morning to reach McAuley by phone.

The narrator sketches the Papworthys' brilliant Ministry-of-Fine-Arts circle and the meddling reformer Reginald Butler, then turns to Home Secretary Jack Williams, who telephones McAuley for an evening of billiards. Williams has deduced the incriminating documents sit in the inside breast-pocket of McAuley's coat, and sets up the game so as to hang that coat within reach.

The young Wilfrid Halterton's car knocks down a poor Jewish schoolboy, Jacob Levina, in the Mile End Road; stricken with compassion and shame, he abandons his journey, follows the boy to the London Hospital, and waits at the shop to see the brother Aaron. He writes Aaron a heartfelt note promising to do everything in his power, while Aaron, already at the hospital, weeps over little Jacob in bitterness.

Disgraced and friendless after impugning public men, Reginald Butler resigns his seat and sinks to writing drama criticism for the Gaper under the pseudonym 'Dr. Johnson'. The narrator then introduces the immense financier Arthur Lawson, head of the bank Schwartz, lonely amid his wealth, whose lifelong gratitude to Halterton now centres on doting on the grown Jacob, whom he brings down from Cambridge every week.

testi/belloc/atomized/a_change_in_the_ca.plot: Leaving the Prime Minister at midnight, the newly-promoted George Mulross Demaine gets lost in the East End, is robbed and stripped by a slum gang, and blunders aboard the tramp steamer Lily. Mistaken for a stowaway, he is sentenced by the pompous Captain Higgins, clapped in 'irons', and set to scrubbing decks as the ship sails for Parham.

themes: a father persuaded by his son
testi/belloc/atomized/emmanuel_burden_me.plot: After weeks of engineered delay, Mr Burden is charmed by the financier Mr Barnett at a club luncheon and pledges himself to the M'Korio syndicate. At the Plantagenet Club he and his colleagues fix the sum to be subscribed; goaded on by Cosmo, Burden raises the capital and finally pays over twenty-five thousand pounds.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_emerald_of_cat.plot: Marjorie badgers her father, the Home Secretary de Bohun, into hiring a detective over the stolen emerald and stages a fake telephone summons to get him up to town. At Whitehall his fixer Morden recommends the discreet agent Brailton, who is dispatched down to Paulings to investigate in disguise.

testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: The chapter traces the origin of the deaf American millionaire G. Quinlan Smith's obsessive collection of Disraeli relics, begun with a forged illuminated address bought in Cherbourg. In the present, Peggy stumbles on him in Pickles' silver shop where, calling himself 'Mr Kew', he is trying to obtain the Disraeli Bat-tail Spoon owned by the Duke of Battersea.

themes: party collusion behind a sham fight
testi/belloc/atomized/pongo_and_the_bull.plot: While Mary Smith drives her guests to church to leave them alone, the Prime Minister (Dolly) and the Opposition leader (Pongo) rehearse a fake Commons debate — cue 'morally guilty of assassination' — to save Smith's Indian loan against the Duke of Battersea. Meanwhile a nervous press interviewer is bounced uselessly between the two Ludlow brothers, extracting nothing.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_man_who_made_g.plot: Reading the newspapers' hysterical coverage of the man who made gold, Charles Lexington panics, buys a match-seller's costume from a theatrical costumier and disguises himself in a Wimbledon Common thicket. When he returns famished from a failed attempt to buy food, he finds his own clothes — and all his money — have been stolen from the clearing.

testi/belloc/atomized/mr_clutterbucks_el.plot: The newly rich Clutterbucks, who have overbuilt a vast Surrey mansion, receive an invitation from the society hostess Mary Smith, who plans to attach one of her impecunious protégés to Clutterbuck's fortune. At her dinner Clutterbuck, dazzled by the Duke of Battersea and the smart set, strikes up a warm friendship with the charming secretary-for-hire Charlie Fitzgerald.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_mercy_of_allah.plot: Uncle Mahmoud recounts to his nephews how, in a simple valley, he cornered the pottery trade by selling below cost, manipulating prices, and lending to his ruined rival Abdullah, who drowns himself. Having monopolised all pipkin-making, Mahmoud then persuades the King to buy him out for half a million dinars as a patriotic 'renunciation' and departs rich.

testi/belloc/atomized/belinda/part/part_.plot: At a grand ball Belinda dances the 'Martagnaise' and her hand briefly touches that of the dark, melancholy Horatio Maltravers, leaving both filled with a nameless dreaming rapture. Next day, drawn by chance to the stream dividing their families' lands, the two meet in the pinewood and each beholds the other transfigured, as by a god.

The wounded, self-exiled Horatio is taken to the château of the English-born widow, the Marquise de la Ferronnière, where his arm is dressed and he is cared for. When his condition worsens overnight the Marquise nurses him devotedly with a mother's affection, and through his slow convalescence enriches him with tales of the great years.

themes: the mystique of the great man
testi/belloc/atomized/mr_petre/chapter_0.plot: A market rush on 'Touaregs', sparked by Mr Petre's public buying, nets him a profit of over £73,000, which Terrard banks for him. The amnesiac Petre opens a bank account to awed deference, then hires the private detective Daniels to find out who 'John K. Petre' is — leaving Daniels convinced the great man was merely testing him.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: The fleeing Boutroux dismisses his horses, turns his postilion's clothes inside out and blacks his face with ash to pass as a charcoal-burner. Hungry and sackless, he tricks his way to a burners' clearing, steals a sack of charcoal from a sleeping giant, and carries it to the farm girl who had ordered it, hoping for payment.

themes: a soldier's bond with his horse
testi/belloc/atomized/the_girondin/chapt.plot: Boutroux's hussar regiment, acting as rearguard, trails for days through incessant rain and mud in the wake of Kellermann's army. His faithful old mount Pascal is failing; on the alarm of enemy scouts near Dommartin the regiment sounds Boot-and-Saddle and rides off northward again into the night and the returning rain.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_missing_master.plot: Sir Henry Bensington finds his accomplice Goatcher has vanished with the picture, and concludes the culprit must be the collector Delgairn, who wants it for secret possession. He sets his two agents, Appleton and Ranford, to infiltrate North Merton House and the village inn to trace the missing masterpiece.

testi/belloc/atomized/but_soft_we_are_ob.plot: The Home Secretary, Sir Henry Hardham, and his Official Secretary agree to send the discreet agent Palmer to meet the arriving envoy Richard Mallard. Palmer boards Mallard's train at Southampton under a fabricated pretext, befriends him, rifles his despatch case for an itinerary, and writes up a detailed report on the unsuspecting traveller.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_green_overcoat.plot: Freed of his bonds but locked in an attic, Professor Higginson twice fails to escape through the skylight — once building a collapsing tower of furniture, once losing his knotted sheets through the broken glass. Finding the doors unbolted at dawn, he flees carrying the green overcoat, then bribes a broken-nosed loafer to deliver it to 'Lauderdale' under a false name.

Mr Kirby assembles the parties and exposes that Higginson forged Brassington's cheque after borrowing his coat. Threatening ruin all round, Kirby persuades the fuming Brassington to drop his revenge by dangling a Baronetcy for a fictitious £10,000 gift to Higginson's research, and the green overcoat finally returns to its master.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_haunted_house/.plot: The Maples work a staged haunting on the credulous Lord Mere de Beaurivage to sell him the house for £50,000, with John feeding his fears while Isabeau plays up her frightened dog. As faint ghostly voices spread panic to the butler Corton, cook and maids, the old lord retires to bed — and a heavy crash and cry sound from his room upstairs.

testi/belloc/atomized/the_postmaster_gen.plot: Anxious after a fall in 'Billies', the Postmaster-General Wilfrid Halterton hunts down the financier McAuley by telephone, only to be told flatly that it was Halterton who gave McAuley a letter, not the reverse. The narrative then introduces the shrewd, genial Home Secretary Jack Williams of Streatham, a man marked for higher office.

During a billiards game at the club, Home Secretary Williams, all genial 'Well played!', slips his hand into McAuley's hung coat and lifts the two crumpled envelopes into his own pocket. Halterton arrives hoping to catch Williams alone but, unable to wait out the long game, leaves frustrated as the two players finish, thick as thieves.

Years earlier, the young Wilfrid Halterton, having caused the accident that crippled Levina's brother Jacob, calls on Aaron Levina to insist on doing everything he can and refuses talk of insurance money. Levina, moved by Halterton's tears and sustained solicitude through the convalescence, forms a deep, lasting gratitude toward the one Gentile he cares for.

Professor Jacob Lawson enthuses to his brother Arthur about long-range Television and Dow's Patent, the one intensifier that makes it possible and which the contractors Durrant's will now monopolise. Without connecting the patent to politics, Arthur resolves next day to visit his friend Halterton to congratulate him after his ordeal in the public glare.

testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: A short appendix returning to prehistoric man, cautioning again against building confident histories on fragmentary remains.
He argues the Christ of the Gospels is not the mild teacher of modern imagination but a startling, riddling figure whose words no invented sage would have dared to speak.

themes: the war of gods and demons
testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: The Punic Wars become a battle between the human paganism of Rome and the demonic child-sacrificing cult of Carthage, whose defeat Chesterton reads as the survival of humanity itself.

themes: the end of the old world
testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: With paganism grown weary and its imagination spent, the ancient world reaches a quiet dead end, and Chesterton depicts a civilisation waiting, without knowing it, for a birth.
He reads the myths as works of the human imagination -- a search for God through beauty and story -- neither true religion nor mere error, but poetry seeking something real.

themes: the recurring death and revival of the Faith
testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: Tracing five moments when the Faith seemed dead -- from Julian to the Renaissance -- he argues that Christianity's repeated, improbable revivals are its most distinctive historical mark.
He proposes that both Christianity and man himself can only be judged truly by stepping outside them, as a traveller sees a country the native cannot.

themes: the pattern of the whole book
testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: Chesterton draws the threads together, presenting the story of Christ and His Church as a drama that keeps ending and beginning again, still unconcluded.
At Bethlehem the two strands -- the God behind the gods and the man in the cave -- meet, as the divine enters history in a cave and quietly overturns the ancient world.
Chesterton states that the book treats Christ and Christianity historically rather than devotionally, arguing the amateur has a right to weigh the facts the specialists supply.
Chesterton argues that the oldest recorded civilisations are already mature and complex, so barbarism is a decline rather than the natural origin of humanity.
Comparing Christ with Socrates and Buddha, Chesterton contends the central story -- a man who was also God, who died and rose -- is unlike anything else told of the founders of religions.
Behind the crowd of pagan gods he finds a buried memory of one God, kept alive chiefly by Israel, whom the nations half-remembered and mostly forgot.
A closing appendix on authority and accuracy, defending the book's use of sources and its historical method.
Alongside the poets he sets the philosophers and the darker cults, contrasting the calm sages of Asia with the demon-worship whose cruelty culminates in Carthage.
He mocks the confident reconstructions of 'prehistoric man' from a few bones, arguing the professors invent a Missing Link and a savage past the evidence cannot support.

themes: cave art and the uniqueness of man
art as the mark of the soul
the gulf between man and beast
testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: Examining the painted caves, Chesterton argues the earliest man is revealed as an artist, and that this creative power sets a difference in kind, not degree, between man and the animals.
The early heresies, by their very one-sidedness, testify to the fullness the Church defended, keeping a difficult balance the Empire and the sects kept losing.

themes: escape from the cycle of paganism
testi/chesterton/atomized/everlasting_ma.plot: Where the older religions turned in endless cycles, Chesterton sees Christendom as an escape into something linear and new, distinct even from the later simplifications of Islam.
